title: Monetizing Artificial Intelligence
description:
In this course, learners will explore the essentials of monetizing AI and data, focusing on evolving basic features into comprehensive platforms and aligning them with business strategies. The course delves into creating ethical, cost-effective infrastructures and transforming data into valuable products and services.

It emphasizes building a unified vision for AI products, ensuring consistent monetization, and understanding the vital role of infrastructure in AI initiatives. Practical frameworks and strategies are provided to navigate the complexities of AI and data monetization effectively.

parts.title: Product-first monetization
parts.description: Explore a  product-first, customer-focused approach to data and AI is promoted, emphasizing their strategic role in creating diverse value streams and addressing market needs, with a shift away from a purely technological perspective.

parts.title: Data-driven opportunities
parts.description: Learn to identify valuable data-driven opportunities by focusing on accessible, ethical data-generating processes, aligning them with business strengths, and strategically planning for long-term AI and analytics success.

parts.title: Strategic AI Monetization
parts.description: Learn how to strategically monetize AI and data by transitioning from basic features to comprehensive platforms, aligning with business strategies, and considering ethical and cost-effective infrastructure development.

proficiency.DS: The course focuses on translating AI and data insights into actionable strategies that drive business growth, optimize processes, and create new value streams, which aligns with the advanced proficiency level for business acumen.
Learners are taught to develop and implement AI strategies, align AI initiatives with business goals, and monetize AI solutions, matching the lead proficiency level for AI techniques.

title: Intermediate Power Query in Excel
description: Building on your foundational Power Query in Excel knowledge, this intermediate course takes you to the next level of data transformation mastery. Discover advanced data integration techniques, including appending and merging datasets with various join types. Delve into M language syntax for creating custom conditional columns and harness advanced table transformations. Unlock the Power Query Advanced Editor, exploring M's built-in functions, mastering best practices like query grouping, and dynamically adjusting filter criteria with parameters. Elevate your skills by crafting custom M formula language functions, unleashing advanced query design capabilities that will empower you to extract deeper insights from your data.

parts.title: Combining Queries in Power Query
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll delve into Power Query's data integration capabilities. You'll master the art of appending queries to combine datasets seamlessly. You'll also learn to merge datasets together, harnessing various join types to render datasets in multiple ways.

parts.title: Custom columns
parts.description: It's all about customization in this chapter. You'll learn the fundamentals of M language syntax, and how it underpins every transformation step in query development. You'll leverage M to create custom conditional columns using logical operators to suit numerous scenarios. You'll also delve into M table transformation expressions to create custom grouped index columns, enhancing your proficiency in advanced query design.

parts.title: M Formula Language
parts.description: In this final chapter, you'll delve into the Power Query Advanced Editor, unraveling M-Language syntax for code modification and debugging. You'll explore M's built-in functions, and master best practices such as query grouping and dynamic filtering with parameters. Lastly, you'll elevate your skills by crafting custom M formula language functions, unlocking advanced query design capabilities

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced data integration, merging datasets, custom transformations, and automation in Power Query, aligning with intermediate proficiency in combining, cleaning, and transforming data from multiple sources using scripts and advanced techniques.

The course introduces M language syntax, custom functions, and advanced editor usage, which matches the intermediate level of designing and implementing functions, using libraries, and automating data tasks in a programming context.

title: Introduction to GCP
description: Introduction to GCP is an insightful course designed to familiarize learners with the Google Cloud Platform (GCP). It starts by introducing GCP's architecture and core services, including Storage, Database, and Compute. It also delves into GCP's data handling capabilities, covering Cloud Spanner, BigQuery, and the integration of AI and ML technologies. Finally, the course discusses the modernization of business using GCP, addressing legacy systems, cloud migration, and digital transformation. This course is ideal for those looking to understand the breadth and application of GCP's offerings.

parts.title: Cloud basics and beyond
parts.description: This chapter introduces Google Cloud Platform (GCP), highlighting its unique advantages and diverse servicesin storage, database, and compute. It explores GCP's architecture, core components, and service interconnectivity. The chapter also discusses cloud data storage, virtual machines, container orchestration, and serverless computing, emphasizing their applications in GCP.

parts.title: The GCP infrastructure
parts.description: The chapter focuses on GCP's handling of data, highlighting storage solutions like Cloud Spanner and BigQuery. It explores business benefits of GCP data storage, analytics services, and integration strategies. It details GCP compute services like Kubernetes Engine and the application of AI and ML, emphasizing Google Cloud's unique strengths and practical business uses.

parts.title: Modernizing businesses with GCP
parts.description: This chapter discusses how to modernize a business with Google Cloud Platform (GCP). It addresses legacy infrastructure challenges, benefits of GCP upgrade, and distinctions between cloud setups. It explores motivations for application modernization and cloud-native applications. The effect of migration to cloud is also discussed, including expenditure shifts, responsibilities in cloud models, and selecting appropriate cloud setups . It concludes with GCP's role in facilitating digital and business transformations.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces foundational concepts of cloud data storage, database services, and data handling using GCP, aligning with entry-level data management skills.
Covers basic understanding of cloud migration, modernization, and the impact on business processes, suitable for foundational project management in a data context.
Discusses business benefits, digital transformation, and modernization using GCP, helping learners recognize how cloud technologies support business goals at a foundational level.

title: Improving Your Data Visualizations in Python
description: Great data visualization is the cornerstone of impactful data science. Visualization helps you to both find insight in your data and share those insights with your audience. Everyone learns how to make a basic scatter plot or bar chart on their journey to becoming a data scientist, but the true potential of data visualization is realized when you take a step back and think about what, why, and how you are visualizing your data. In this course you will learn how to construct compelling and attractive visualizations that help you communicate the results of your analyses efficiently and effectively. We will cover comparing data, the ins and outs of color, showing uncertainty, and how to build the right visualization for your given audience through the investigation of a datasets on air pollution around the US and farmer's markets. We will finish the course by examining open-access farmers market data to build a polished and impactful visual report.

parts.title: Highlighting your data
parts.description: How do you show all of your data while making sure that viewers don't miss an important point or points? Here we discuss how to guide your viewer through the data with color-based highlights and text. We also introduce a dataset on common pollutant values across the United States.

parts.title: Using color in your visualizations
parts.description: Color is a powerful tool for encoded values in data visualization. However, with this power comes danger. In this chapter, we talk about how to choose an appropriate color palette for your visualization based upon the type of data it is showing.

parts.title: Showing uncertainty
parts.description: Uncertainty occurs everywhere in data science, but it's frequently left out of visualizations where it should be included. Here, we review what a confidence interval is and how to visualize them for both single estimates and continuous functions. Additionally, we discuss the bootstrap resampling technique for assessing uncertainty and how to visualize it properly.

parts.title: Visualization in the data science workflow
parts.description: Often visualization is taught in isolation, with best practices only discussed in a general way. In reality, you will need to bend the rules for different scenarios.  From messy exploratory visualizations to polishing the font sizes of your final product; in this chapter, we dive into how to optimize your visualizations at each step of a data science workflow.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: This course goes beyond basic chart creation, focusing on constructing compelling and audience-appropriate visualizations, using color effectively, showing uncertainty, and integrating visualization throughout the data science workflow-skills expected at the intermediate proficiency level.

The course emphasizes communicating analytical results efficiently and effectively to different audiences, including building polished visual reports and tailoring visualizations to stakeholder needs, which aligns with intermediate technical communication competencies.

title: Image Modeling with Keras
description: Image modeling often requires deep learning methods that use data to train neural network algorithms for various machine learning tasks. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are particularly powerful neural networks that you'll use to classify different types of objects for the analysis of images. This four-hour course will teach you how to construct, train, and evaluate CNNs using Keras.

parts.title: Image Processing With Neural Networks
parts.description: Convolutional neural networks use the data that is represented in images to learn. In this chapter, we will probe data in images, and we will learn how to use Keras to train a neural network to classify objects that appear in images.

parts.title: Using Convolutions
parts.description: Convolutions are the fundamental building blocks of convolutional neural networks. In this chapter, you will be introducted to convolutions and learn how they operate on image data. You will also see how you incorporate convolutions into Keras neural networks.

parts.title: Going Deeper
parts.description: Convolutional neural networks gain a lot of power when they are constructed with multiple layers (deep networks). In this chapter, you will learn how to stack multiple convolutional layers into a deep network. You will also learn how to keep track of the number of parameters, as the network grows, and how to control this number.

parts.title: Understanding and Improving Deep Convolutional Networks
parts.description: There are many ways to improve training by neural networks. In this chapter, we will focus on our ability to track how well a network is doing, and explore approaches towards improving convolutional neural networks.

proficiency.DS: This course covers the construction, training, and evaluation of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) using Keras, which aligns with advanced proficiency in applying complex AI methodologies such as CNNs to solve image modeling problems.

The course requires using Python and Keras to build and train neural networks, which fits the intermediate level of implementing functions and using libraries for data manipulation and model construction.

title: Fundamentals of Bayesian Data Analysis in R
description: Bayesian data analysis is an approach to statistical modeling and machine learning that is becoming more and more popular. It provides a uniform framework to build problem specific models that can be used for both statistical inference and for prediction. This course will introduce you to Bayesian data analysis: What it is, how it works, and why it is a useful tool to have in your data science toolbox.

parts.title: What is Bayesian Data Analysis?
parts.description: This chapter will introduce you to Bayesian data analysis and give you a feel for how it works.

parts.title: How does Bayesian inference work?
parts.description: In this chapter we will take a detailed look at the foundations of Bayesian inference.

parts.title: Why use Bayesian Data Analysis?
parts.description: This chapter will show you four reasons why Bayesian data analysis is a useful tool to have in your data science tool belt.

parts.title: Bayesian inference with Bayes' theorem
parts.description: Learn what Bayes theorem is all about and how to use it for statistical inference.

parts.title: More parameters, more data, and more Bayes
parts.description: Learn about using the Normal distribution to analyze continuous data and try out a tool for practical Bayesian analysis in R.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course covers Bayesian inference and modeling, including Bayes' theorem and practical application in R, which aligns with advanced proficiency requiring knowledge of advanced statistical techniques and the ability to apply them to complex problems.
The course introduces Bayesian modeling as a machine learning approach, matching the intermediate level's expectation to apply AI techniques to real-world problems and develop AI-powered solutions.

title: AI Security and Risk Management
description: Discover the essentials of safeguarding AI systems in this introductory course on AI security and risk management. Learn to align security efforts with business goals, mitigate risks, and tackle key security challenges. You will explore specific AI security issues, assess risks from multiple perspectives, and understand threats related to AI model development and usage. Designed for professionals seeking to protect their organizations, this course offers practical, actionable practices to become an AI security champion. By the end, you'll be equipped to stay ahead in the fast-evolving world of AI security.

parts.title: AI's Security Landscape
parts.description: The purpose of this chapter is to establish a strategic understanding of AI security, identify the unique security risks associated with AI, examine how AI can be a security change agent, and consider the need to treat all players equally.

parts.title: Risk Management Fundamentals
parts.description: This chapter focuses on the operational side of AI security and risk management, diving deeper into different types of risks, secure development practices, and risk assessment. We will first examine risks broken down by internal and external risk categories and then learn about practices aimed at mitigating them.

parts.title: Strategic Integration of AI Security
parts.description: Bringing AI security into alignment with organizations' strategic goals is the focus of this chapter. It covers the importance of connecting security efforts to tangible business value, ensuring security isn't an afterthought but a strategic asset. In addition, it talks about the importance of fostering a security-aware culture within an organization and the importance of keeping up to date with evolving risks and opportunities in the constantly changing world of AI.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces the basics of AI security risks and risk management, aligning with foundational proficiency by covering core concepts, risk identification, and practical mitigation strategies relevant for entry-level professionals.

The course emphasizes aligning AI security with business goals and strategic integration, which matches the intermediate level's focus on connecting technical solutions to business objectives and communicating their impact.

title: Introduction to dbt
description: This course introduces you to dbt (data build tool), a popular tool that has given rise to analytics engineering for the creation and maintenance of extract, transform, and load (ELT) pipelines. You'll learn to build data warehouses, perform data modeling and transformations, and design tests to perform data validation. You'll use SQL and shell commands to perform a variety of tasks with dbt, along with discovering how to generate documentation for your warehouse users!

parts.title: Welcome to dbt
parts.description: Learn about the reasons behind dbt's existence and how it's used to create data transformation projects.

parts.title: dbt models
parts.description: Get into the true substance of dbt by working with data models and creating SQL based models within dbt. Learn about basic SQL models, define dependencies, update, and troubleshoot various model issues.

parts.title: Testing & Documentation
parts.description: Learn to take advantage of data validation in dbt using tests. Apply default tests to various models and properties, then create custom tests to handle specialized logic validation. Learn to document various details of dbt models and generate lineage information automatically.

parts.title: Implementing dbt in production
parts.description: Utilize what you've learned about dbt with some added details to implement dbt in a production environment. We'll cover dbt seeds and snapshots, along with how to automate builds. Finally review what you've learned throughout the course and implement a dbt pipeline.

proficiency.DS: This course covers building ELT pipelines, data modeling, and automating data transformations using dbt, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on combining datasets, automating cleaning tasks, and maintaining structured metadata.
Learners use SQL and shell commands to build and automate data pipelines, matching the intermediate proficiency in designing and implementing functions, using libraries, and automating data tasks.

The course includes generating documentation and managing code for data models, which fits the intermediate level's emphasis on organizing repositories, documenting code, and ensuring reproducibility.

title: Reinforcement Learning with Gymnasium in Python
description: Embark on an exhilarating exploration of Reinforcement Learning (RL), a pivotal branch of machine learning. This interactive course takes you on a comprehensive journey through the core principles of RL where you'll master the art of training intelligent agents, teaching them to make strategic decisions and maximize rewards. Your agents will learn to navigate a whole host of different environments from OpenAI's gym toolkit, including navigating frozen lakes and mountains.

parts.title: Introduction to Reinforcement Learning
parts.description: Dive into the exciting world of Reinforcement Learning (RL) by exploring its foundational concepts, roles, and applications. Navigate through the RL framework, uncovering the agent-environment interaction. You'll also learn how to use the Gymnasium library to create environments, visualize states, and perform actions, thus gaining a practical foundation in RL concepts and applications.

parts.title: Model-Based Learning
parts.description: Delve deeper into the world of RL focusing on model-based learning. Unravel the complexities of Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), understanding their essential components. Enhance your skill set by learning about policies and value functions. Gain expertise in policy optimization with policy iteration and value Iteration techniques.

parts.title: Model-Free Learning
parts.description: Embark on a journey through the dynamic realm of Model-Free Learning in RL. Get introduced to to the foundational Monte Carlo methods, and apply first-visit and every-visit Monte Carlo prediction algorithms. Transition into the world of Temporal Difference Learning, exploring the SARSA algorithm. Finally, dive into the depths of Q-Learning, and analyze its convergence in challenging environments.

parts.title: Advanced Strategies in Model-Free RL
parts.description: Dive into advanced strategies in Model-Free RL, focusing on enhancing decision-making algorithms. Learn about Expected SARSA for more accurate policy updates and Double Q-learning to mitigate overestimation bias. Explore the Exploration-Exploitation Tradeoff, mastering epsilon-greedy and epsilon-decay strategies for optimal action selection. Tackle the Multi-Armed Bandit Problem, applying strategies to solve decision-making challenges under uncertainty.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced reinforcement learning concepts, including model-based and model-free methods, policy optimization, and advanced strategies like Double Q-learning and exploration-exploitation tradeoffs, aligning with the advanced proficiency level for AI techniques.
The course requires and develops practical Python programming skills for implementing RL algorithms and using libraries like Gymnasium, matching the intermediate proficiency level for programming.

title: Improving Query Performance in SQL Server
description: A mission critical assignment is depending on your SQL coding skills. You've been given some code to fix.  It is giving the results you need but it's running too slow, and it's poorly formatted making it hard to read.  The deadline is tomorrow.  You'll need to reformat the code and try different methods to improve performance.  The pressure is on!!!  In this course we'll be using SQL on real world datasets, from sports and geoscience, to look at good coding practices and different ways how we can can improve the performance of queries to achieve the same outcome.

parts.title: Introduction, Review and The Order of Things
parts.description: In this chapter, students will learn how SQL code formatting, commenting, and aliasing is used to make queries easy to read and understand.  Students will also be introduced to query processing order in the database versus the order of the SQL syntax in a query.

parts.title: Filtering and Data Interrogation
parts.description: This chapter introduces filtering with WHERE and HAVING and some best practices for how (and how not) to use these keywords. Next, it explains the methods used to interrogate data and the effects these may have on performance.  Finally, the chapter goes over the roles of DISTINCT() and UNION in removing duplicates and their potential effects on performance.

parts.title: Sub-queries and presence or absence
parts.description: This chapter is an introduction to sub-queries and their potential impacts on query performance.  It also examines the different methods used to determine if the data in one table is present, or absent, in a related table.

parts.title: Query performance tuning
parts.description: Students are introduced to how STATISTICS TIME, STATISTICS IO, indexes, and executions plans can be used in SQL Server to help analyze and tune query performance.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: The course covers code formatting, commenting, and best practices for writing readable and efficient SQL, as well as using sub-queries and performance tuning tools, which aligns with the intermediate level's focus on implementing functions, optimizing code, and quality assurance.

The course involves filtering, data interrogation, and combining datasets using SQL, which matches the intermediate level's requirements for automating data cleaning, handling structured data, and optimizing queries for performance.

title: Generative AI Concepts
description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping our world like never before. Generative AI is a type of AI that can create new content from text, images, and more. In this no-coding course, you'll learn about the exciting concepts in this emerging field and how to prepare for a future where AI becomes widely adopted. You'll start by comprehending how these models create content, where they fit into the machine learning landscape, and how they are developed. Given the power of generative AI, you will also consider how laws and ethics play with these models, learning how to avoid bias and use generative AI responsibly. Finally, you'll look at the future of generative AI and how we can leverage and collaborate effectively with these tools. After this course, you, too, will be able to unlock the creative capabilities of generative AI. Let's go!

parts.title: Introduction to Generative AI
parts.description: Familiarize yourself with the concept of generative AI and its ability to create content is introduced, along with its real-world applications and limitations. You'll delve into the differences between traditional machine learning models, generative AI, and artificial general intelligence (AGI), and explore the key factors driving the development of generative AI.

parts.title: Developing Generative AI Models
parts.description: In this chapter, we cover the essential steps in creating generative AI models: research and design, data collection, model training, and evaluation. We examine the significance of diverse datasets and advanced training techniques, as well as various evaluation methods, while discussing their strengths and limitations.

parts.title: Using AI Models and Generated Content Responsibly
parts.description: This chapter focuses on the responsible use of generative AI. We discuss the challenges and strategies to mitigate social bias, intellectual property and privacy issues, and ethical considerations to prevent misuse. We conclude by exploring the immense potential and risks of Artificial Generative Intelligence (AGI), along with the approaches to control its outcomes.

parts.title: Getting Ready for the Age of Generative AI
parts.description: Chapter 4 examines the potential, impact, and integration of generative AI into human workflows. It discusses key contributors to AI development, from universities to companies, and explores societal adaptations to AI. It delves into AI's implications for productivity, job dynamics, education, media, entertainment, scientific advancements, and ethical considerations.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces core generative AI concepts, differences from traditional ML, and basic model development steps, aligning with foundational proficiency in understanding and applying basic AI concepts and responsible use.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Responsible and Ethical AI Use
proficiency.DS: The course addresses responsible AI use, bias mitigation, legal and ethical considerations, and privacy, matching foundational requirements for understanding and applying responsible and ethical AI practices.
By exploring the future impact and societal integration of generative AI, the course supports foundational proficiency in monitoring trends and new tools in AI.

title: Databricks Concepts
description: This course guides you from start to finish on how the Databricks Lakehouse Platform provides a single, scalable, and performant platform for your data processes. As you work through a real-world dataset, you will learn how to accomplish a variety of tasks within the Databricks platform. Throughout this course, you will learn about and practice the different features of the Databricks Lakehouse platform and see how they can be applied to different data use cases.

parts.title: Welcome to Databricks
parts.description: Learn about the new lakehouse paradigm for your cloud data strategy and how the Databricks Lakehouse platform can modernize your data architecture. Understand the foundational components of the Databricks platform and how they all fit together.

parts.title: Data Engineering
parts.description: Learn how to process, transform, and clean your data using Databricks functionality. Practice using capabilities such as the Delta storage format, Delta Live Tables, and Workflows together to create an end-to-end data pipeline.

parts.title: Databricks SQL and Data Warehousing
parts.description: Use the Databricks Lakehouse platform as your data warehousing solution for your Business Intelligence (BI) use cases. Use the built-in SQL-optimized capabilities within Databricks to create queries and dashboards on your data.

parts.title: Databricks for Large-scale Applications and Machine Learning
parts.description: Use Databricks to manage your Machine Learning pipelines with managed MLFlow. Follow the model development lifecycle from end-to-end with the Feature Store, Model Registry, and Model Serving Endpoints to create a robust MLOps platform in the lakehouse.

proficiency.DS: The course covers processing, transforming, and cleaning data using Databricks, including building end-to-end data pipelines and automating data workflows, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in Data Processing.

Learners practice using Databricks features to create data pipelines, automate workflows, and utilize SQL and scripting, matching intermediate programming skills in data manipulation and workflow automation.
The course guides learners through managing data projects from ingestion to deployment, including maintaining pipelines and workflows, which fits intermediate project management in data science.
The course introduces managing ML pipelines, model development, and MLOps with Databricks, aligning with intermediate skills in applying ML techniques to real-world business problems.
Learners use Databricks for data warehousing, Delta storage, and managing data architecture, which matches intermediate data management proficiency.

title: Introduction to Python for Developers
description:
Are you eager to dive into the world of programming but don't know where to start? This course is for you, designed specifically for beginners with zero prior experience in programming. Python, is a versatile and powerful language, perfect for software development!

This course introduces you to key concepts, from creating code comments and performing calculations to discovering Python's built-in data types including floats, strings, integers, and boolean values! You'll learn how to store information in variables using a variety of data structures such as lists, dictionaries, sets, and tuples.

You'll progress into comparison operators, using them to develop a customized workflow to conditionally execute code depending on whether conditions are met. The course wraps up by introducing for and while loops, which are essential for iterating over data and executing tasks!

parts.title: Introduction to Python
parts.description: Discover the wonders of Python - why it is popular and how to use it. No prior knowledge required!

parts.title: Working with Data Types
parts.description: Learn how and when to use Python's built-in data structures, including lists, dictionaries, sets, and tuples!

parts.title: Control flow and loops
parts.description: Conditional statements and operators, for and while loops all combine to enable customized workflows for your needs!

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers fundamental programming concepts such as variables, data types, basic data structures (lists, dictionaries, sets, tuples), control flow, and loops in Python, which aligns directly with the foundational proficiency level for Programming.

title: Data Manipulation in Julia
description:
Julia is a new and exciting programming language designed for machine learning, scientific computing, and data mining. This course will provide you with the knowledge necessary for starting your own data manipulation journey in Julia.

We'll build on your knowledge of DataFrames from the Introduction to Julia and Intermediate Julia courses. By the end of the course, you'll be equipped with core skills for inspecting, transforming, grouping, visualizing DataFrames, and many more.

parts.title: Inspecting DataFrames
parts.description: Take your first steps toward complex data manipulation in Julia! Learn how to personalize your experience with the DataFrames package and how to create data visualizations using the Plots package.

parts.title: Working with columns
parts.description: Columns are the basic building blocks of DataFrames. Knowing how to handle columns is essential for your data manipulation journey. You'll learn how to reorder and drop columns, as well as how to apply functions to individual rows and whole columns.

parts.title: Aggregating DataFrames
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn how to group data and calculate grouped summary statistics, as well as how to create pivot tables. You'll also learn how to improve the readability of your code with the Chain.jl package.

parts.title: Improving  Your Workflow
parts.description: Learn how to load and join datasets, as well as how to handle missing values. Then it's time to fit everything together!

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: The course covers loading, joining, cleaning, aggregating, and transforming datasets using Julia DataFrames, which aligns with the intermediate level's focus on automating data cleaning, handling missing values, combining datasets, and performing complex data manipulations.

Learners use Julia and its packages to manipulate data structures, apply functions, and improve workflow, matching the intermediate proficiency in designing and implementing functions, using libraries for data manipulation, and automating tasks.
The course introduces creating data visualizations with Julia's Plots package, which fits the foundational level's requirement to present basic data analysis results using simple charts and graphs.

title: Introduction to Alteryx
description: Alteryx Designer is a leading platform for data analytics, offering an intuitive interface ideal for professionals of all levels. This course introduces you to Alteryx Designer Desktop's essentials, from navigating its interface to employing its drag-and-drop functionality for efficient data workflows. You'll learn data importing, cleansing, and joining, moving on to advanced predictive, statistical, and spatial analysis techniques. By the end of this course, you'll be adept at transforming raw data into actionable insights, enhancing your data processing and analytical skills. Embark on your Alteryx Designer journey to unlock powerful data analytics capabilities!

parts.title: Getting Started with Alteryx
parts.description: In this chapter, you will get your first taste of Alteryx Designer. You will be introduced to the benefits of using Alteryx Designer: increased efficiency through automated workflows and improved data quality, setting the stage for practical application and mastery of Alteryx Designer. You will learn how the tool simplifies data cleaning, transformation, and analysis, serving users of varying expertise across multiple industries. It highlights the ease of creating workflows akin to recipes with a drag-and-drop interface and emphasizes the tool palette's role in effective data manipulation.

parts.title: Preparing the data
parts.description: This chapter delves into data preparation in Alteryx Designer, highlighting its crucial role in data analysis. Starting with data cleaning, transforming, and organizing, we underscore the importance of selecting correct data types for accurate analysis and efficient data profiling. To refine datasets for insightful decision-making, you will explore Alteryx Designer's preparation toolset, including Select, Sort, and Sample tools.

parts.title: Summarizing the Data
parts.description: In the final chapter, you will cover essential Alteryx Designer tools for enhancing workflow efficiency as you finalize your workflow. You will learn about the Unique tool and how it helps eliminate duplicate entries, the Summarize tool for data aggregation, and the Comment tool for workflow documentation. These tools collectively streamline data tasks, making the analysis process more efficient and understandable.

proficiency.DS: The course covers basic data importing, cleaning, transformation, and joining using Alteryx Designer, aligning with foundational skills in preparing and manipulating data for analysis.

The course introduces workflow automation, data profiling, and the use of tools for data aggregation and documentation, which are relevant for intermediate proficiency in handling more complex data preparation and workflow tasks.

title: Experimental Design in Python
description: Discover how to design experiments and conduct statistical analyses to begin making precise conclusions! In this course, you'll learn how different experimental design setups, including randomized block designs and factorial designs, can be implemented to measure treatment effects. You'll deep-dive into performing statistical analyses on experimental data, including selecting the correct statistical tests for the situation, conducting post-hoc analysis, and measuring effect size and minimum sample size with Cohen's d and power analysis. Finally, you'll learn how to extract insights from complex experimental data and communicate your findings to different stakeholders, address complexities like interactions, heteroscedasticity, and confounding, and implement nonparametric methods when data doesn't meet the assumptions of parametric tests.

parts.title: Experimental Design Preliminaries
parts.description: Building knowledge in experimental design allows you to test hypotheses with best-practice analytical tools and quantify the risk of your work. You'll begin your journey by setting the foundations of what experimental design is and different experimental design setups such as blocking and stratification. You'll then learn and apply visual and analytical tests for normality in experimental data.

parts.title: Experimental Design Techniques
parts.description: You'll delve into sophisticated experimental design techniques, focusing on factorial designs, randomized block designs, and covariate adjustments. These methodologies are instrumental in enhancing the accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability of experimental results. Through a combination of theoretical insights and practical applications, you'll acquire the skills needed to design, implement, and analyze complex experiments in various fields of research.

parts.title: Analyzing Experimental Data: Statistical Tests and Power
parts.description: Master statistical tests like t-tests, ANOVA, and Chi-Square, and dive deep into post-hoc analyses and power analysis essentials. Learn to select the right test, interpret p-values and errors, and skillfully conduct power analysis to determine sample and effect sizes, all while leveraging Python's powerful libraries to bring your data insights to life.

parts.title: Advanced Insights from Experimental Complexity
parts.description: Hop into the complexities of experimental data analysis. Learn to synthesize insights using pandas, address data issues like heteroscedasticity with scipy.stats, and apply nonparametric tests like Mann-Whitney U. Learn additional techniques for transforming, visualizing, and interpreting complex data, enhancing your ability to conduct robust analyses in various experimental settings.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: The course covers advanced experimental design (factorial, block designs), complex statistical analyses (ANOVA, post-hoc, power analysis, nonparametric tests), and addresses experimental complexities, matching the advanced proficiency requirements for applying rigorous statistical techniques and interpreting complex data.

The course teaches designing and managing complex experiments, selecting appropriate methodologies, and ensuring robust, reproducible analyses, which aligns with advanced proficiency in developing and managing complex studies and ensuring methodological rigor.

The course includes communicating findings to different stakeholders and extracting actionable insights from complex data, which matches the intermediate level of organizing data insights and adapting communication for various audiences.

The course leverages Python and its libraries (pandas, scipy.stats) for data analysis and visualization, aligning with intermediate proficiency in using libraries for data manipulation and implementing analytical workflows.

title: Intermediate Docker
description:
This course builds upon the foundations of learning Docker and containerization found in the Introduction to Docker course. We extend the concepts and tools covered in that course, adding the ideas of container image management and optimization, networking, file system communication, multi-platform and multi-container applications. When completed, you'll be able to:

- Create multi-stage builds to optimize the size, security, and reusability of containerized applications.
- Use Docker networking tools and concepts to add inter-container communications and provide networking services to the local network and the outside world.
- Share files and data between containers and the host machine using Docker file system mounts and volumes.
- Create mutli-container application deployments using Docker Compose, drastically simplifying the setup of complex tools common in data science and engineering environments.

You'll gain the most from this course if you have worked with and built some simple containers, but are looking to add to your development, testing, and distribution toolbox. We look forward to helping guide you during your journey of learning Docker.

parts.title: Commands and filesystems
parts.description: This chapter covers new Docker commands and details on how to share data between host system and containerized applications. Learn when and how to use persistent volumes and access host filesystems.

parts.title: Networking
parts.description: Learn to expose networking services in Docker, create Docker networks, and use Dockerfiles to maintain network settings.

parts.title: Building advanced container images
parts.description: Learn to use Docker's advanced image management and build tools to create compact effective container images. Create multi-platform images capable of running on different processor architectures.

parts.title: Docker Compose
parts.description: Combine the the volume, networking, and container handling capabilities of Docker into multi-container applications using Docker Compose. Update and manage application deployments via the docker-compose.yml file.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers intermediate programming skills related to containerization, including multi-stage builds, networking, and multi-container orchestration, which align with the ability to design and implement modular, scalable solutions and automate development workflows.

The course introduces tools like Docker Compose for managing multi-container deployments, supporting the management of moderately complex project tasks and resource coordination in data science environments.
By teaching file system mounts, volumes, and data sharing between containers, the course supports skills in automating and managing data flows and infrastructure for data processing pipelines.

title: Practicing Machine Learning Interview Questions in Python
description:
Have you ever wondered how to properly prepare for a Machine Learning Interview? In this course, you will prepare answers for 15 common Machine Learning (ML) in Python interview questions for a data scientist role.

These questions will revolve around seven important topics: data preprocessing, data visualization, supervised learning, unsupervised learning, model ensembling, model selection, and model evaluation.

You'll start by working on data pre-processing and data visualization questions. After performing all the preprocessing steps, you'll create a predictive ML model to hone your practical skills.

Next, you'll cover some supervised learning techniques before moving on to unsupervised learning. Depending on the role, you'll likely cover both topics in your machine learning interview.

Finally, you'll finish by covering model selection and evaluation, looking at how to evaluate performance for model generalization, and look at various techniques as you build an ensemble model.

By the end of the course, you will possess both the required theoretical background and the ability to develop Python code to successfully answer these 15 questions.

The coding examples will be mainly based on the scikit-learn package, given its ease of use and ability to cover the most important machine learning techniques in the Python language.

The course does not teach machine learning fundamentals, as these are covered in the course's prerequisites.

parts.title: Data Pre-processing and Visualization
parts.description: In the first chapter of this course, you'll perform all the preprocessing steps required to create a predictive machine learning model, including what to do with missing values, outliers, and how to normalize your dataset.

parts.title: Supervised Learning
parts.description: In the second chapter of this course, you'll practice different several aspects of supervised machine learning techniques, such as selecting the optimal feature subset, regularization to avoid model overfitting, feature engineering, and ensemble models to address the so-called bias-variance trade-off.

parts.title: Unsupervised Learning
parts.description: In the third chapter of this course, you'll use unsupervised learning to apply feature extraction and visualization techniques for dimensionality reduction and clustering methods to select not only an appropriate clustering algorithm but optimal cluster number for a dataset.

parts.title: Model Selection and Evaluation
parts.description: In the fourth and final chapter of this course, you'll really step it up and apply bootstrapping and cross-validation to evaluate performance for model generalization, resampling techniques to imbalanced classes, detect and remove multicollinearity, and build an ensemble model.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course focuses on practical application of supervised and unsupervised learning, model selection, and evaluation, aligning with the intermediate level's emphasis on applying ML techniques to real-world problems, fine-tuning models, and evaluating performance using appropriate metrics.

Participants develop and implement Python code for ML tasks, including data preprocessing, model building, and evaluation, which matches the intermediate proficiency of designing and implementing functions and using libraries like scikit-learn for data manipulation and analysis.

The course covers data preprocessing steps such as handling missing values, outliers, and normalization, as well as feature engineering and selection, which are key intermediate data processing skills.

Model evaluation, cross-validation, regularization, and understanding bias-variance trade-off require application of inferential statistics and regression techniques, which are expected at the intermediate level.

The course includes data visualization and dimensionality reduction for feature extraction and analysis, which aligns with the intermediate level's need to create and interpret complex visualizations.

title: Understanding Data Visualization
description: Visualizing data using charts, graphs, and maps is one of the most impactful ways to communicate complex data. In this course, you'll learn how to choose the best visualization for your dataset, and how to interpret common plot types like histograms, scatter plots, line plots and bar plots. You'll also learn about best practices for using colors and shapes in your plots, and how to avoid common pitfalls. Through hands-on exercises, you'll visually explore over 20 datasets including global life expectancies, Los Angeles home prices, ESPN's 100 most famous athletes, and the greatest hip-hop songs of all time.

parts.title: Visualizing distributions
parts.description: In this chapter you'll learn the value of visualizations, using real-world data on British monarchs, Australian salaries, Panamanian animals, and US cigarette consumption, to graphically represent the spread of a variable using histograms and box plots.

parts.title: Visualizing two variables
parts.description: You'll learn how to interpret data plots and understand core data visualization concepts such as correlation, linear relationships, and log scales. Through interactive exercises, you'll also learn how to explore the relationship between two continuous variables using scatter plots and line plots. You'll explore data on life expectancies, technology adoption, COVID-19 coronavirus cases, and Swiss juvenile offenders. Next you'll be introduced to two other popular visualizations-bar plots and dot plots-often used to examine the relationship between categorical variables and continuous variables. Here, you'll explore famous athletes, health survey data, and the price of a Big Mac around the world.

parts.title: The color and the shape
parts.description: It's time to make your insights even more impactful. Discover how you can add color and shape to make your data visualizations clearer and easier to understand, especially when you find yourself working with more than two variables at the same time. You'll explore Los Angeles home prices, technology stock prices, math anxiety, the greatest hiphop songs, scotch whisky preferences, and fatty acids in olive oil.

parts.title: 99 problems but a plot ain't one of them
parts.description: In this final chapter, you'll learn how to identify and avoid the most common plot problems. For example, how can you avoid creating misleading or hard to interpret plots, and will your audience understand what it is you're trying to tell them? All will be revealed! You'll explore wind directions, asthma incidence, and seats in the German Federal Council.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces basic data visualization concepts such as selecting appropriate chart types, interpreting common plots (histograms, scatter plots, bar plots), and understanding best practices for visual clarity, which aligns with foundational proficiency in Data Visualization.
The course emphasizes communicating complex data through clear visualizations and interpreting results for diverse audiences, matching the foundational level of Technical Communication.

title: Introduction to Data Modeling in Snowflake
description:
Step right into the dynamic world of data modeling with Snowflake! You will master the core principles while applying the theory in hands-on experience, turning data jungles into insightful gardens.
You'll uncover the secrets of data normalization and explore techniques like entity-relationship, dimensional modeling, and data vault to craft efficient cloud data warehouses.
Snowflake's architecture reveals its massive parallel processing power and optimization capabilities as you progress. Transition from a learner to a strategic asset, ready to make data-driven decisions. Your data modeling adventure awaits!

parts.title: Fundamentals of Data Modeling
parts.description: Embark on a foundational exploration of data modeling with Snowflake and uncover the art of organizing data efficiently. Start with the basics of data modeling concepts, understand its significance in a data-driven world, and learn how to represent and store data effectively. By visualizing data organization on a vast scale, you'll grasp the importance of a well-structured data model in simplifying data querying and analysis.

parts.title: Data Relationships and Normalization
parts.description: Unlock the secrets of effective data organization and management, focusing on the critical roles of keys in data relationships and the fundamental principles of data normalization within Snowflake. Delve into the foundational aspects of relational data, emphasizing the importance of primary and foreign keys in structuring and linking data entities. Embark on a journey through the normalization process, starting with 1NF to eliminate duplicate data, advancing to 2NF to address partial dependencies, and culminating in 3NF to remove transitive dependencies.

parts.title: Data Modeling Techniques for Data Warehouse
parts.description: Venture deeper into data warehousing strategies with Snowflake, exploring three pivotal data modeling approaches: Entity-Relationship Model, Dimensional Modeling, and Data Vault. Begin by mapping complex relationships within a university system using the Entity-Relationship model, which is perfect for visualizing data interactions. Transition into Dimensional Modeling to simplify data analysis through fact and dimension tables, ideal for insightful reporting. Then, delve into Data Vault modeling for a robust framework that excels in historical data tracking and flexibility.

parts.title: Snowflake Components
parts.description: Unlock the potential of Snowflake's architecture to optimize query performance, enhancing the speed and efficiency of your data models. Explore the advantages of columnar storage, Massively Parallel Processing (MPP), and micro-partitions in Snowflake, contrasting them with traditional databases for a clear understanding of Snowflake's superior performance. Delve into Snowflake's data objects-virtual warehouses, tables, views, and more-to smartly organize your data. Master techniques such as query optimization, the use of subqueries, and Common Table Expressions (CTEs) to streamline data processing.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces fundamental data modeling concepts, normalization, and basic Snowflake architecture, aligning with foundational skills in organizing, storing, and preparing data for analysis.

By covering advanced normalization (up to 3NF), entity-relationship, dimensional, and data vault modeling, as well as Snowflake optimization techniques, the course matches intermediate proficiency in combining, transforming, and optimizing data structures for analysis.

title: Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming in Python
description:
Embark on a journey into the heart of Python programming with our comprehensive course offering a foundation in the principles and practices of object-oriented programming (OOP). Through a series of hands-on exercises and real-world examples, learners will gain proficiency in leveraging the power of Python's OOP paradigm to create efficient, modular, and reusable code.

Foundations of OOP
Delve into the fundamental concepts that form the foundation of object-oriented programming. You'll discover the core principles of classes and objects, learn how to define and instantiate objectives in Python and explore how to assign attributes during instantiation.

Inheritance
Expand your knowledge by mastering inheritance and creating subclasses that build on functionality defined in other classes. You'll distinguish between class-level and instance-level data, implement class methods, and customize the functionality of subclasses!

Equality, Exception Handling, and Best Practices
Explore the versatility of Python in handling object comparisons and discover techniques for effective string representation of objects, enabling human-readable outputs.
Learn how to fortify your code against unexpected errors and enhance its reliability through exception handling. Understand the importance of error detection and graceful error recovery, ensuring a smoother execution of your programs. Acquire best practices for writing clean, maintainable, and Pythonic code that adheres to OOP principles.

parts.title: OOP Fundamentals
parts.description: Learn what object-oriented programming (OOP) is, how it differs from procedural programming, and how it can be applied. You'll define your own custom classes containing methods, attributes, and constructors, and use them to create objects!

parts.title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
parts.description: Discover two of OOP's core concepts: inheritance and polymorphism. Learn how to implement them to minimize code re-use and extend functionality, along with reviewing the differences between class-level data and instance-level data.

parts.title: Integrating with Standard Python
parts.description: Learn how to compare objects, define and customize string representations of objects, and even how to apply inheritance to create and catch custom exceptions, enabling bespoke error-handling.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers object-oriented programming concepts such as classes, inheritance, exception handling, and best practices in Python, aligning with the intermediate proficiency level which expects the ability to design and implement functions and classes, apply OOP principles, and write maintainable code.

title: R For SAS Users
description: If you have experience with SAS and want to learn R, this is the course for you. R is FREE (cost) and OPEN (license) and is one of the fastest growing software languages for statistics and data science. This course is a gentle introduction to the R language with every chapter providing a detailed mapping of R functions to SAS procedures highlighting similarities and differences. You will orient yourself in the R environment and discover how to wrangle, visualize, and model data plus customize your output for final presentation. Throughout the course, you will follow a consistent workflow of data quality checking and cleaning, exploring relationships, modeling, and presenting results. You will leave this course with coded examples that provide a template to use immediately with a dataset of your own.

parts.title: Getting Started with R
parts.description: This first chapter will get you oriented into the R programming environment. You'll learn how to get help, load a dataset, and increase functionality by adding packages. You'll begin working with the abalone dataset (through the dplyr package workflow) to get descriptive statistics and create helpful visualizations (using the ggplot2 package).

parts.title: Data Wrangling
parts.description: Now that you are oriented in the R environment, this chapter will advance your understanding of R's versatility working with data objects. You'll learn how to create and modify variables in the abalone data set. Using your ggplot2 visualization skills, you will discover the data errors in the abalone data and then create a final cleaned data set ready for analysis and modeling.

parts.title: Data Exploration
parts.description: Once your data set has been cleaned, the next step is exploration. In chapter 3 you will learn how to compute descriptive statistics, explore associations (e.g., correlations) among the variables, and perform bi-variate statistical tests (e.g., t-tests and chi-square tests). You will also create graphical visualizations which illustrate the bi-variate associations and group comparison tests.

parts.title: Models and Presentation
parts.description: In this final chapter, you will learn how to work with one of the most versatile data object types in R called a list. These skills will enable you to save and manipulate your output from descriptive statistics, associations, and group comparison computations. You will also learn how to perform ANOVA (analysis of variance) and linear regression in R. All your skills are put to use in the final exercises to create the best models for predicting abalone ages from their sex, size, and weight measurements.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: The course introduces R programming basics, including environment setup, data loading, and use of packages, which aligns with foundational programming skills such as writing simple scripts and using basic data structures.
Chapters on data wrangling and cleaning map to foundational data processing skills like loading datasets, handling missing values, and preparing data for analysis.
The course covers descriptive statistics, basic probability, and introductory statistical tests (t-tests, chi-square), which are core foundational statistical skills.
Learners use ggplot2 to create basic visualizations (bar charts, scatter plots), matching the foundational level of presenting data insights with simple graphs.
The course emphasizes presenting results and customizing output, which supports foundational skills in summarizing and communicating analysis findings clearly.

title: Intermediate Deep Learning with PyTorch
description: Deep learning is a rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence (AI) that revolutionized the field of machine learning, enabling breakthroughs in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. In this course, you'll develop robust deep learning models with PyTorch for a range of applications, including image and sequence models. You'll become familiar with core network architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs).

parts.title: Training Robust Neural Networks
parts.description: Learn how to train neural networks in a robust way. In this chapter, you will use object-oriented programming to define PyTorch datasets and models and refresh your knowledge of training and evaluating neural networks. You will also get familiar with different optimizers and, finally, get to grips with various techniques that help mitigate the problems of unstable gradients so ubiquitous in neural nets training.

parts.title: Images & Convolutional Neural Networks
parts.description: Train neural networks to solve image classification tasks. In this chapter, you will learn how to handle image data in PyTorch and get to grips with convolutional neural networks (CNNs). You will practice training and evaluating an image classifier while learning about how to improve the model performance with data augmentation.

parts.title: Sequences & Recurrent Neural Networks
parts.description: Build and train recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for processing sequential data such as time series, text, or audio. You will learn about the two most popular recurrent architectures, Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) networks, as well as how to prepare sequential data for model training. You will practice your skills by training and evaluating a recurrent model for predicting electricity consumption.

parts.title: Multi-Input & Multi-Output Architectures
parts.description: Build multi-input and multi-output models, demonstrating how they can handle tasks requiring more than one input or generating multiple outputs. You will explore how to design and train these models using PyTorch and delve into the crucial topic of loss weighting in multi-output models. This involves understanding how to balance the importance of different tasks when training a model to perform multiple tasks simultaneously.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced deep learning topics such as CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, and multi-input/output architectures, aligning with the advanced proficiency level which expects the ability to apply complex AI methodologies and build production-ready AI solutions.
The course requires and develops object-oriented programming skills in Python (PyTorch), including defining datasets and models, which matches the intermediate proficiency level for programming.

title: Data Analysis in Google Sheets
description:
Learn how to clear and analyze data in Google Sheets, discover how to use built-in functions to sort and filter data, and use the VLOOKUP function to combine data from different tables.

These Google Sheets skills, functions, and time-saving shortcuts can be applied to any industry, whether you're looking to move to a career in data analysis, or looking to improve your skills in marketing, finance, HR, logistics, and more.

parts.title: Exploring Data
parts.description: Learn how data analyst skills in spreadsheets can help you draw clearer insights from data. In this chapter, you'll learn how built-in functions can streamline your spreadsheet workflows and improve the readability of your formulas. You'll learn data exploration techniques, such as calculating summary statistics and manipulations like sorting and filtering.

parts.title: Cleaning and Preparing Data
parts.description: It is often said that data professionals spend 80% of their time cleaning data and only 20% analyzing it. In this chapter, you'll learn useful functions for cleaning text and DateTime data, two of the trickiest data types to clean. You'll extract date and time components, calculate intervals, and perform a host of common text manipulations on a dataset of the highest-grossing films.

parts.title: Analyzing Data
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn to draw insights from your data. You'll perform complex calculations using conditional functions, logical expressions, and conditional aggregation functions. You'll also learn and apply the most important spreadsheet function: VLOOKUP!

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: The course covers loading, cleaning, sorting, filtering, and combining data using Google Sheets, aligning with foundational skills in data processing such as handling missing values, formatting, and basic data transformations.
Learners calculate summary statistics and perform basic data analysis in spreadsheets, matching the foundational level's focus on measures of central tendency and summarizing datasets.

The course teaches the use of built-in spreadsheet functions and logical expressions for data manipulation, consistent with foundational programming skills involving basic functions and data structures.

title: Data Preparation in Alteryx
description:
Discover how to prepare, clean, and analyze data in Alteryx Designer! Whether you are new to data analytics in general or an experienced analyst in other platforms, this course will guide you to new levels of understanding the essentials of solid data preparation. You'll learn why clean and prepared data is important for optimal analytics and how to recognize what aspects of your datasets need cleaning.

Using the Preparation Toolset, you'll explore removing null data, filtering on specific criteria, applying various formulas, analyzing duplicate data, and many more features that will advance you to perform more intermediate-level analysis in the versatile Alteryx Designer platform. Achieve deeper knowledge of Alteryx Designer best practices and take your knowledge to the next level with hands-on experience. Now is the time to get started on your Alteryx journey!

parts.title: Data Cleaning and Preparation
parts.description: Accelerate your Alteryx knowledge by exploring data preparation techniques! You'll learn why clean and prepared data is important for optimal analytics and how to utilize the main data types. You'll also discover how to recognize "dirty data" and techniques for cleansing data, such as managing missing values and removing unnecessary data.

parts.title: Filtering and Using Expressions
parts.description: Expand your data preparation skills in Alteryx by uncovering ways to filter data and write expressions to create subsets of data. Basic and chained filters will be explored, along with custom filters, to get right to the data you need. You'll learn best practices in writing expressions, including understanding the differences between AND and OR statements, along with helpful tips for correct syntax.

parts.title: Applying Formulas
parts.description: Go further into the layers of data preparation by diving deeper into various formulas and how they can be quickly applied in Alteryx. Discover the wealth of pre-structured formulas available and ready to use in the Formula tool, along with techniques for writing efficient expressions based on data types. You'll learn the difference between length and position-based formulas and methods to update and create new fields.

parts.title: Sampling and Summarizing
parts.description: Explore the processes of sampling and summarizing your data, which are essential aspects of data preparation. You'll learn many options for sampling data, such as finding the top 10 records or obtaining the first N percentage of data, and much more with the Sample tool. You'll then expand your knowledge of summarizing data using numerical methods like sum, average, and median, as well as string functions like grouping by specific fields hierarchically in the Summarize tool.

proficiency.DS: The course covers basic data cleaning, handling missing values, filtering, and summarizing data in Alteryx, which aligns with foundational skills in preparing and cleaning data for analysis.

It introduces intermediate-level techniques such as using formulas, chaining filters, and summarizing data, which are consistent with intermediate proficiency in automating and performing more complex data manipulations.

title: Practicing Statistics Interview Questions in Python
description: Are you looking to land that next job or hone your statistics interview skills to stay sharp? Get ready to master classic interview concepts ranging from conditional probabilities to A/B testing to the bias-variance tradeoff, and much more! You'll work with a diverse collection of datasets including web-based experiment results and Australian weather data. Following the course, you'll be able to confidently walk into your next interview and tackle any statistics questions with the help of Python!

parts.title: Probability and Sampling Distributions
parts.description: This chapter kicks the course off by reviewing conditional probabilities, Bayes' theorem, and central limit theorem. Along the way, you will learn how to handle questions that work with commonly referenced probability distributions.

parts.title: Exploratory Data Analysis
parts.description: In this chapter, you will prepare for statistical concepts related to exploratory data analysis. The topics include descriptive statistics, dealing with categorical variables, and relationships between variables.  The exercises will prepare you for an analytical assessment or stats-based coding question.

parts.title: Statistical Experiments and Significance Testing
parts.description: Prepare to dive deeper into crucial concepts regarding experiments and testing by reviewing confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, multiple tests, and the role that power and sample size play. We'll also discuss types of errors, and what they mean in practice.

parts.title: Regression and Classification
parts.description: Wrapping up, we'll address concepts related closely to regression and classification models. The chapter begins by reviewing fundamental machine learning algorithms and quickly ramps up to model evaluation, dealing with special cases, and the bias-variance tradeoff.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course covers inferential statistics, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, regression, and exploratory data analysis, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on applying and interpreting statistical techniques and drawing conclusions from sample data.

The course addresses advanced topics such as the bias-variance tradeoff, model evaluation, and multiple tests, which are relevant for advanced proficiency where complex statistical concepts and rigorous evaluation are expected.

The final chapter introduces fundamental machine learning algorithms and model evaluation, matching the foundational level's requirement to apply basic machine learning algorithms and understand core concepts.

title: Containerization and Virtualization Concepts
description: Heard of Docker, containers, Kubernetes, and VMs but not sure what they mean? This course provides foundational knowledge in containerization and virtualization to enhance your modern software development skills. You'll learn to distinguish between containers and virtual machines, understand Docker and Kubernetes, read Dockerfiles, and run your first containerized application. By the end, you'll have the essential knowledge to dive deeper into Docker and Kubernetes and make informed architectural decisions.

parts.title: Foundations of Containerization and Virtualization
parts.description: Explore the concept of virtualization, its benefits, and the emergence of containerization as a lightweight alternative. You will then delve into the key differences between containers and virtual machines, enabling you to determine the ideal solution for your needs.

parts.title: Applications of Containerization
parts.description: Dive into the practical applications of containers and their orchestration. Learn about the modern tech stack of Docker and Kubernetes, and get hands-on in the final lesson by learning how to read Dockerfiles and run your first containerized application!

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course introduces foundational concepts in containerization and virtualization, including Docker and Kubernetes, which are essential for understanding modern software development environments and basic program deployment.

title: Text Mining with Bag-of-Words in R
description: It is estimated that over 70% of potentially usable business information is unstructured, often in the form of text data. Text mining provides a collection of techniques that allows us to derive actionable insights from unstructured data. In this course, we explore the basics of text mining using the bag of words method. The first three chapters introduce a variety of essential topics for analyzing and visualizing text data. The final chapter allows you to apply everything you've learned in a real-world case study to extract insights from employee reviews of two major tech companies.

parts.title: Jumping into Text Mining with Bag-of-Words
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn the basics of using the bag-of-words method for analyzing text data.

parts.title: Word Clouds and More Interesting Visuals
parts.description: This chapter will teach you how to visualize text data in a way that's both informative and engaging.

parts.title: Adding to Your TM Skills
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn more basic text mining techniques based on the bag of words method.

parts.title: Battle of the Tech Giants for Talent
parts.description: This chapter ties everything together with a case study in text mining for HR analytics.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces basic text mining and bag-of-words methods, which are foundational machine learning techniques for unstructured data.
Learners perform basic cleaning, transformation, and visualization of unstructured text data, aligning with foundational data processing skills.
The course covers visualizing text data (e.g., word clouds), supporting foundational skills in presenting data insights clearly.

title: Introduction to Data Versioning with DVC
description: Delve into Data Version Control (DVC), a tool for managing and versioning ML data. Explore its role in the ML lifecycle, differentiate data versioning from code versioning, and examine DVC's features and use cases. Learn about DVC setup, including cache management and remotes, and discover its applications in CI/CD, experiment tracking, and pipelines. Automate ML pipelines, emphasizing code modularization, and practice executing them efficiently. Conclude with model evaluation, exploring metric tracking in DVC for informed decision-making.

parts.title: Introduction to DVC
