parts.description: This chapter provides a comprehensive introduction to Data Version Control (DVC), a tool essential for data versioning in machine learning. Learners will explore the motivation behind data versioning, understand its differences from code versioning, and experiment with a simple classification problem. They will review basic Git commands, learn about DVC, and practice setting up a repository. The chapter concludes with an overview of DVC's features and use cases, including versioning data and models, CI/CD for machine learning, experiment tracking, pipelines, and more.

parts.title: DVC Configuration and Data Management
parts.description: This chapter delves into the setup of DVC, encompassing aspects such as installation, initialization of the repository, and the utilization of the .dvcignore file. It further navigates through the exploration of DVC cache and staging files, imparting knowledge on how to add and remove files, manage caches, and comprehend the underlying mechanisms using the MD5 hash. The chapter also elucidates on DVC remotes, distinguishing them from Git remotes, and guides you on how to add, list, and modify them. Lastly, it teaches you how to interact with these remotes by pushing and pulling data, checking out specific versions, and fetching data to the cache.

parts.title: Pipelines in DVC
parts.description: This chapter focuses on automating ML pipelines using DVC. Learners create a configuration file containing settings and hyperparameters. They also learn about pipeline visualization using directed acyclic graphs and use commands to describe dependencies, commands, and outputs. Execution of DVC pipelines is covered, including local model training and how Git tracks DVC metadata. Additionally, learners explore metrics and plots tracking in DVC, including how to print metrics, create plot files, and compare metrics and plots across different pipeline stages.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course covers DVC setup, repository initialization, branching between data and code versioning, and collaborative workflows, aligning with intermediate proficiency in code management for reproducibility and documentation.
It addresses automation of ML pipelines, CI/CD integration, experiment tracking, and modular code organization, which are hallmarks of advanced code management practices in data science projects.
Automating and optimizing ML pipelines, managing data lineage, and integrating DVC into scalable workflows correspond to advanced data processing competencies.
The course's focus on CI/CD, experiment tracking, and pipeline automation demonstrates advanced project management skills in orchestrating complex, reproducible ML projects.

title: Pivot Tables in Google Sheets
description: Working with large quantities of data in Google Sheets can be difficult and time-consuming. Have you ever wished there was a quick and efficient way to organize and evaluate your data within seconds? Pivot Tables are your answer! In this course we will explore the world of Pivot Tables within Google Sheets, and learn how to quickly organize thousands of datapoints with just a few clicks of the mouse. We will analyze the Average rainfall across multiple US cities, the Top 10 of the Fortune Global 500, and a selection of Films released between 2010 and 2016. You will learn techniques such as sorting, subtotaling, and filtering your data using these real world examples. By the end of the course, you will be able to create your own custom pivot tables with datasets of any size!

parts.title: Introduction to Pivot Tables for Google Sheets
parts.description: This chapter will discuss what a pivot table is, how it works, and will lead you through the steps of creating and setting up your first pivot table.

parts.title: Behind the Scenes of the Pivot Table
parts.description: This chapter discuss how a pivot table works, and how it deals with the underlying data.

parts.title: Advanced Options
parts.description: This chapter will discuss more advanced options that will help you to get the most of your pivot tables.

parts.title: Editing Data and Troubleshooting
parts.description: This chapter will walk you through modifying data in a pivot table, and troubleshooting various issues you may encounter.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: This course teaches basic data organization, sorting, filtering, and summarization using pivot tables, aligning with foundational skills in data cleaning and preparation.
The course covers combining, aggregating, and manipulating large datasets with pivot tables, which matches intermediate proficiency in handling and transforming structured data.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) Concepts
description: This course will dive into the captivating world of Explainable AI (XAI), a discipline that seeks to bring clarity and understanding to the often mysterious realm of artificial intelligence. This conceptual course is crafted with the non-technical audience in mind, aiming to illuminate the importance and methods behind making AI decisions transparent. Participants will delve into the rationale for XAI, its role amidst the broader landscape of AI, and its significant societal implications. By the course end, learners across varied roles will appreciate how XAI bridges the gap between intricate algorithms and everyday decision-making.

parts.title: Introduction To Explainable AI
parts.description: We delve into Explainable AI (XAI), emphasizing its role in rendering AI systems transparent, interpretable, and trustworthy. We explore AI's capabilities in prediction and content generation, underscoring the necessity for clear decision-making processes. Additionally, we investigate methods to make complex AI models more comprehensible to a wide range of audiences.

parts.title: Techniques in Explainable AI
parts.description: We explore Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, categorizing them into model-specific, model-agnostic, local, and global explanations to clarify AI decision-making. We discuss regression and classification for model-specific insights and introduce SHAP and LIME to interpret black box models. Additionally, we address the complexity of Large Language Models (LLMs), emphasizing the need for transparency in their decision-making processes.

parts.title: Implementing and Applying XAI
parts.description: We explore the transformative impact of XAI in making artificial intelligence more accessible and user-friendly across various sectors. By integrating explainability from the outset, we ensure AI systems are transparent, fostering trust and facilitating a deeper collaboration between humans and machines. Through real-world case studies, we highlight how XAI demystifies complex AI decisions, empowering users with diverse technical backgrounds to leverage AI insights for more informed decision-making.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces core concepts and societal implications of Explainable AI (XAI), focusing on transparency and interpretability for non-technical audiences, aligning with foundational proficiency in understanding basic AI concepts and responsible use.

The course emphasizes making complex AI decisions understandable to a wide audience, supporting foundational skills in presenting technical concepts clearly and ensuring accessibility for non-technical stakeholders.

proficiency.SA: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
proficiency.DS: By focusing on transparency, trust, and societal implications of AI, the course aligns with foundational ethical competencies, such as discussing ethical concerns and adhering to responsible AI practices.

title: Understanding Microsoft Azure Management and Governance
description: This course is the third course in preparing you for the Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) exam. Through interactive exercises and videos, you will learn about managing and governing resources in Microsoft Azure, focusing on tools for resource management, cost control, and security. Key topics include Azure Resource Manager (ARM), role-based access control (RBAC), cost management, and monitoring.

parts.title: Azure Management and Governance Fundamentals
parts.description: Start your journey by learning what the concepts of management and governance mean in Azure and what kind of use cases and tasks are involved. You'll learn more about cost management, governance, resource management, and monitoring in Azure.

parts.title: Cost Management and Governance
parts.description: Cost management and governance will have no secrets for you anymore after this chapter. You'll learn how to plan and manage costs in Azure and work with Azure cost management tools. You'll also familiarize yourself with the implementation of governance and compliance, and the tools Azure provides to help you with that.

parts.title: Resource Management and Monitoring
parts.description: In the final chapter, we'll dive deeper into resource management and monitoring. You'll learn how to apply resource management and monitoring to your projects, using the tools Azure provides to assist you with this.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces basic concepts of resource management, cost control, and monitoring in Azure, aligning with foundational project management skills such as planning tasks, managing resources, and maintaining project documentation.

Learners gain an understanding of managing and governing resources, including cost and compliance, which matches foundational data management skills like handling data lifecycles and ensuring data quality.

title: Vector Databases for Embeddings with Pinecone
description: Discover how the Pinecone vector database is revolutionizing AI application development. Pinecone is a fully-managed, ultra-low query latency vector database solution that is cornering the market. In this course, you'll learn to ingest, manipulate, and query vectors from Pinecone indexes. You'll use these skills, along with other fundamental concepts such as Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to enable AI applications such as semantic search engines and context-aware chatbots. Finally, you'll learn to optimize your production databases by looking at techniques for tuning performance, optimizing storage, and improving query latency.

parts.title: Introduction to Pinecone
parts.description: Explore the mechanics behind Pinecone's vector database, from pods and indexes to comparing it with other databases. Learn to differentiate pod types, acquire API keys, and initialise Pinecone connection using python. Finally, you'll learn how to create Pinecone indexes, exploring different parameters such as dimensionality, distance metrics, pod types, and others.

parts.title: Pinecone Vector Manipulation in Python
parts.description: Get hands-on with Pinecone in Python, where we explore the practical side of using Pinecone for managing indexes, adding vectors with metadata, searching and retrieving vectors, and making updates or deletions. Gain a solid grasp of the key functions and ideas to smoothly handle data in the Pinecone vector database.

parts.title: Performance Tuning and AI Applications
parts.description: In this chapter, learners delve into optimizing Pinecone index performance, leveraging multi-tenant namespaces for cost reduction, building semantic search engines, and creating retrieval-augmented question answering systems using Pinecone with the OpenAI API. Through these lessons, learners gain practical skills in performance tuning, semantic search, and retrieval-augmented question answering, empowering them to apply Pinecone effectively in real-world AI applications.

proficiency.DS: The course covers ingestion, manipulation, and querying of vector data using Pinecone, aligning with intermediate-level skills in combining datasets, automating data cleaning, and processing structured/unstructured data for AI applications.
Learners use Python to interact with Pinecone, manage indexes, and manipulate vectors, matching intermediate proficiency in implementing functions, using libraries, and automating data tasks.

The course teaches Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), semantic search, and context-aware chatbots, which are intermediate AI skills involving applying AI techniques to real-world problems and integrating AI agents into pipelines.

Managing vector databases, optimizing storage, and performance tuning correspond to intermediate data management skills, including maintaining metadata, publishing data in machine-readable formats, and prioritizing high-value datasets.

title: Introduction to Kubernetes
description:
Kubernetes is a solution that orchestrates and maintains containerized applications effectively. Since its introduction in 2014 by Google, this open-source system has developed into the tool of choice for managing all kinds of distributed workloads. It is an essential part of today's DevOps world, helping to develop and deploy scalable applications and workflows of any kind.

In this interactive course, you'll become a Kubernetes champ with hands-on experience using Kubernetes on the command line. You will master kubectl, the Kubernetes command line tool, and use it to interact with real Kubernetes clusters. You will learn the fundamentals of Kubernetes and understand how to deploy and orchestrate containers using Manifests and kubectl instructions.

parts.title: Introduction to Kubernetes (K8s)
parts.description: We will explore the role of Kubernetes in modern software design, and learn about its architecture.

parts.title: Deploying Software on K8s
parts.description: We learn how to deploy software using Kuberentes, and will use "kubectl" extensively.

parts.title: Data Engineering and MLOps
parts.description: Building upon what we learned in the previous chapters, we will understand how Kubernetes can support data pipelines and MLOps.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers deploying and orchestrating containerized applications using Kubernetes and kubectl, which aligns with the intermediate proficiency level's focus on implementing functions, using libraries, and automating tasks in programming.

The course introduces orchestration and deployment of scalable applications and workflows, supporting the intermediate level's requirement to manage tasks, monitor progress, and adjust resources in data-driven projects.

By addressing how Kubernetes supports data pipelines and MLOps, the course matches the intermediate level's emphasis on automating and processing data workflows, including handling infrastructure requirements.

title: Image Processing in Python
description: Images are everywhere! We live in a time where images contain lots of information, which is sometimes difficult to obtain. This is why image pre-processing has become a highly valuable skill, applicable in many use cases. In this course, you will learn to process, transform, and manipulate images at your will, even when they come in thousands. You will also learn to restore damaged images, perform noise reduction, smart-resize images, count the number of dots on a dice, apply facial detection, and much more, using scikit-image. After completing this course, you will be able to apply your knowledge to different domains such as machine learning and artificial intelligence, machine and robotic vision, space and medical image analysis, retailing, and many more. Take the step and dive into the wonderful world that is computer vision!

parts.title: Introducing Image Processing and scikit-image
parts.description:
Jump into digital image structures and learn to process them! Extract data, transform and analyze images using NumPy and Scikit-image. 

With just a few lines of code, you will convert RGB images to grayscale,  get data from them, obtain histograms containing very useful information, and separate objects from the background!

parts.title: Filters, Contrast, Transformation and Morphology
parts.description: You will learn to detect object shapes using edge detection filters, improve medical images with contrast enhancement and even enlarge pictures to five times its original size! You will also apply morphology to make thresholding more accurate when segmenting images and go to the next level of processing images with Python.

parts.title: Image restoration, Noise, Segmentation and Contours
parts.description: So far, you have done some very cool things with your image processing skills! In this chapter, you will apply image restoration to remove objects, logos, text, or damaged areas in pictures! You will also learn how to apply noise, use segmentation to speed up processing, and find elements in images by their contours.

parts.title: Advanced Operations, Detecting Faces and Features
parts.description: After completing this chapter, you will have a deeper knowledge of image processing as you will be able to detect edges, corners, and even faces! You will learn how to detect not just front faces but also face profiles, cat, or dogs. You will apply your skills to more complex real-world applications. Learn to master several widely used image processing techniques with very few lines of code!

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course covers using Python and libraries like NumPy and scikit-image for data manipulation, image processing, and automation of tasks, which aligns with intermediate programming proficiency.

Learners apply machine learning and computer vision techniques such as facial detection, segmentation, and feature extraction, matching the intermediate level's focus on applying AI to real-world problems.
The course teaches cleaning, transforming, and manipulating image data, including restoration and noise reduction, which fits the intermediate data processing proficiency.

title: Developing AI Systems with the OpenAI API
description: Get your AI applications ready for production with this OpenAI API course. You'll discover best practices for developing applications on the OpenAI API, including moderation and validation, testing, and practices for improved safety. You'll also learn how to connect your application with external systems and APIs through function calling. This course builds on core OpenAI functionalities introduced in Working with the OpenAI API and prompt writing best practices from ChatGPT Prompt Engineering for Developers to help you elevate your projects from proof of concept to production-ready systems.

parts.title: Structuring End-to-End Applications
parts.description: Learn how to seamlessly incorporate the OpenAI API into more complex systems, mastering the art of manipulating the response format and adeptly handling errors. This chapter provides essential knowledge for those looking to build components of AI systems that are not just interactive but also robust and efficient.

parts.title: Function Calling
parts.description: Dive into the mechanics of function calling, where you'll master defining parameters to call specific functions, extracting structured data, and working with multiple functions. Learn to seamlessly integrate external APIs and manipulate responses to communicate with other systems, to develop enhanced AI system interactions.

parts.title: Best Practices for Production Applications
parts.description: Elevate your OpenAI API skills to follow the industry's best practices. Learn to moderate content with precision, validate model behavior for consistency, and implement safety measures for secure API usage. This final chapter is an essential part of building robust AI-powered applications.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced topics such as building production-ready AI systems, integrating external APIs, implementing safety and moderation, and optimizing for robustness and efficiency, aligning with advanced proficiency in AI techniques.

The course teaches integration of APIs, error handling, and building robust, scalable AI applications, which matches the advanced programming proficiency level focused on complex system workflows and best coding practices.

title: Deep Learning for Text with PyTorch
description: Embark on an exciting journey into deep learning for text with PyTorch. This course will equip you with the skills to tackle various text-related challenges. You'll dive into the principles of text processing with encoding and embedding. You'll apply various models, including CNNs, RNNs, GANs, and pre-trained models, using text data. Finally, you'll delve into advanced topics, including transfer learning techniques, attention mechanisms, and how to protect your models from adversarial attacks. By the end of this course, you'll have the skills to build powerful deep learning models for text.

parts.title: Introduction to Deep Learning for Text with PyTorch
parts.description: This chapter introduces you to deep learning for text and its applications. Learn how to use PyTorch for text processing and get hands-on experience with techniques such as tokenization, stemming, stopword removal, and more. Understand the importance of encoding text data and implement encoding techniques using PyTorch. Finally, consolidate your knowledge by building a text processing pipeline combining these techniques.

parts.title: Text Classification with PyTorch
parts.description: Explore text classification and its role in Natural Language Processing (NLP). Apply your skills to implement word embeddings and develop both Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for text classification using PyTorch, and understand how to evaluate your models using suitable metrics.

parts.title: Text Generation with PyTorch
parts.description: Venture into the exciting world of text generation and its applications in NLP. Understand how to leverage Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and pre-trained models for text generation tasks using PyTorch. Alongside, you'll learn to evaluate the performance of your models using relevant metrics.

parts.title: Advanced Topics in Deep Learning for Text with PyTorch
parts.description: Understand the concept of transfer learning and its application in text classification. Explore Transformers, their architecture, and how to use them for text classification and generation tasks. You will also delve into attention mechanisms and their role in text processing. Finally, understand the potential impacts of adversarial attacks on text classification models and learn how to protect your models.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced deep learning models for text, including CNNs, RNNs, GANs, transformers, transfer learning, and attention mechanisms, aligning with the advanced proficiency requirements for applying complex AI methodologies to challenging problems.
Learners implement and optimize deep learning models using PyTorch, requiring advanced programming skills to work with frameworks, optimize code, and build production-ready solutions.
The course teaches text preprocessing, encoding, and embedding, which are key intermediate-level data processing tasks for preparing unstructured text data for analysis.

title: Analyzing Business Data in SQL
description: Businesses track data on everything, from operations to marketing to HR. Leveraging this data enables businesses to better understand themselves and their customers, leading to higher profits and better performance. In this course, you'll learn about the key metrics that businesses use to measure performance. You'll write SQL queries to calculate these metrics and produce report-ready results. Throughout the course, you'll study data from a fictional food delivery startup, modeled on data from real companies.

parts.title: Revenue, Cost, and Profit
parts.description: Profit is one of the first things people use to assess a company's success. In this chapter, you'll learn how to calculate revenue and cost, and then combine the two calculations using Common Table Expressions to calculate profit.

parts.title: User-Centric KPIs
parts.description: Financial KPIs like profit are important, but they don't speak to user activity and engagement. In this chapter, you'll learn how to calculate the registrations and active users KPIs, and use window functions to calculate the user growth and retention rates.

parts.title: ARPU, Histograms, and Percentiles
parts.description: Since a KPI is a single number, it can't describe how data is distributed. In this chapter, you'll learn about unit economics, histograms, bucketing, and percentiles, which you can use to spot the variance in user behaviors.

parts.title: Generating an Executive Report
parts.description: Executives often use the KPIs you've calculated in the three previous chapters to guide business decisions. In this chapter, you'll package the KPIs you've created into a readable report you can present to managers and executives.

topic.name: Reporting
topic.description: Most analyses are useless until they are communicated effectively to the right audience. Knowing how to report your findings in an interesting and interpretable way empowers others with greater understanding and the ability to make important data-driven decisions.

proficiency.DS: The course teaches writing SQL queries, using window functions, and Common Table Expressions, which aligns with intermediate programming skills in data manipulation and report generation.
Learners calculate business metrics, use percentiles, and analyze distributions, matching the intermediate level's focus on applying statistical techniques to uncover patterns and interpret data.

The course covers key business metrics (revenue, profit, ARPU, user retention) and ties data analysis to business objectives, reflecting intermediate business acumen in aligning data insights with business performance.

The course emphasizes generating executive reports and presenting KPIs to managers, which fits the intermediate level's requirement to organize insights and adapt communication for business stakeholders.

title: Introduction to Python for Finance
description:
The financial industry uses Python extensively for quantitative analysis, ranging from understanding trading dynamics to risk management systems. This course will show you how to analyze your financial data by building your Python skills.

The first chapter explains how Python and finance go hand in hand. You will then learn Python basics such as printing output, performing calculations, understanding data types, and creating variables.

Next, you'll cover lists and arrays in Python, exploring how you can use them to work with data. You'll use the NumPy and Matplotlib packages to manipulate and visualize data.

Finally, you will finish the course by conducting a Python financial analysis on an S&P 100 dataset. Here, you will apply your Python skills to filter lists, summarize sector data, plot P/E ratios in histograms, visualize financial trends, and identify outliers.

By the end of the course, you will be confident in your basic Python skills and practical financial analysis skills. These skills are highly rewarded in the finance industry to solve quantitative finance problems. This course is part of our Finance Fundamentals in Python track which is perfect for those who wish to delve deeper into Python for finance.

parts.title: Welcome to Python
parts.description: This chapter is an introduction to basics in Python, including how to name variables and various data types in Python.

parts.title: Lists
parts.description: This chapter introduces lists in Python and how they can be used to work with data.

parts.title: Arrays in Python
parts.description: This chapter introduces packages in Python, specifically the NumPy package and how it can be efficiently used to manipulate arrays.

parts.title: Visualization in Python
parts.description: In this chapter, you will be introduced to the Matplotlib package for creating line plots, scatter plots, and histograms.

parts.title: S&P 100 Case Study
parts.description: In this chapter, you will get a chance to apply all the techniques you learned in the course on the S&P 100 data.

topic.name: Applied Finance
topic.description: The finance community has been one of the eager to embrace data science. From stock market predictions, to asset pricing and calculating the probability of loan defaults, the applications are nearly endless!

proficiency.DS: The course teaches Python basics, including variables, data types, lists, arrays, and use of libraries like NumPy and Matplotlib, aligning with foundational programming skills for data manipulation and analysis.
Learners summarize and describe financial data features using visualizations (histograms, plots) and basic statistics, matching foundational statistical competency.
The course introduces Matplotlib for creating line plots, scatter plots, and histograms, which fits foundational data visualization skills.

By applying Python to financial datasets and analyzing sector data, the course helps learners recognize business problems and present findings relevant to business stakeholders, which matches foundational business acumen.

title: Introduction to Optimization in Python
description: This course transforms beginners into skilled optimizers, teaching you to convert and solve real-world problems using mathematical modeling in Python with SciPy and PuLP. Starting with the basics of optimization and its applications, you'll employ SymPy for analytical solutions without manually calculating derivatives, and utilize SciPy for numerical answers. You'll progress to tackling linear programming, constrained convex optimization, and mixed integer optimization with SciPy and PuLP, focusing on practical issues like manufacturing, profit maximization, and resource allocation.

parts.title: Introduction to Optimization
parts.description: This chapter introduces optimization, its core components, and its wide applications across industries and domains. It presents a quick, exhaustive search method for solving an optimization problem. It provides a mathematical primer for the concepts required for this course.

parts.title: Unconstrained and Linear Constrained Optimization
parts.description: This chapter covers solving unconstrained and constrained optimization problems with differential calculus and SymPy, identifying potential pitfalls.  SciPy is also introduced to solve unconstrained optimization problems, in single and multiple dimensions, numerically, with a few lines of code.  The chapter goes on to solve linear programming in SciPy and PuLP.

parts.title: Non-linear Constrained Optimization
parts.description: This chapter introduces convex-constrained optimization problems with different constraints and looks at mixed integer linear programming problems, essentially linear programming problems where at least one variable is an integer.

parts.title: Robust Optimization Techniques
parts.description: This chapter covers finding the global optimum when multiple good solutions exist. We will conduct sensitivity analysis and learn linearization techniques that reduce non-linear problems to easily solvable ones with SciPy or PuLP.  In terms of applications, we will solve an HR allocation with training costs problem and capital budgeting with dependent projects.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: The course covers mathematical modeling, linear programming, and constrained optimization, aligning with intermediate proficiency in applying statistical and mathematical techniques to real-world problems.

Learners use Python libraries (SciPy, PuLP, SymPy) to implement optimization algorithms and solve practical problems, matching the intermediate level of designing and implementing functions and using libraries for data manipulation and analysis.

title: Introduction to Redshift
description: This course offers a foundational understanding of Amazon Redshift, a distributed columnar database within the AWS cloud. Explore its integration into the AWS ecosystem and its SQL constructs, including common table expressions and analytics queries. Learn to create tables, manage data distribution, handle raw data files, and extract information from JSON. Additionally, optimize queries, tune performance, and enhance data security. By the end of the course, you'll have a strong command of SQL on Redshift and the knowledge and skills needed to use Redshift effectively.

parts.title: Redshift, a data warehouse
parts.description: Meet Redshift, a robust columnar data warehouse. We'll explore how columnar and typical data warehouses differ, what makes Redshift unique, how it fits into the AWS and data warehouse ecosystems, and what data types it supports.

parts.title: SQL on Redshift
parts.description: Let's learn about some nuances with Redshift SQL syntax, a close cousin of PostgreSQL's syntax. We compare CTEs and subqueries before moving into mastering date and time, exploring window queries, and wrapping up learning how transactions affect some functions.

parts.title: Tables and working with semi-structured data
parts.description: We'll explore how to create tables, the impact DISTKEY and SORTKEYs have on performance, external schemas/tables with Spectrum and wrap up with handling semi-structured data like JSON with Redshift.

parts.title: Optimization and Security
parts.description: It is time to peak into the world of writing optimized queries and tools available to help optimize. Then, we turn our attention to Redshift security capabilities and how they can impact query output.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces foundational concepts of data warehousing, basic SQL, data types, and handling raw/semi-structured data, aligning with foundational data management skills.

Covers intermediate skills such as optimizing queries, understanding data distribution (DISTKEY/SORTKEY), managing external schemas, and enhancing data security, which are relevant for intermediate proficiency.

title: Power Pivot in Excel
description: In this comprehensive course, you will embark on a journey to harness the power of Power Pivot in Excel. Starting with the fundamentals, you will learn to set up Power Pivot, import data from various sources, and establish relationships in a data model. As the course progresses, you will delve into the world of DAX, mastering basic calculations and measures. You will then create visualizations and dynamic dashboards that tell compelling data stories to uncover actionable insights from your data. By the end of the course, you will have mastered Power Pivot and take your skills into the real world.

parts.title: Starting with Power Pivot
parts.description: You will take your first steps in setting up Power Pivot by enabling the add-in. Then, you will import data from various source types and practice preparing your data for analysis.

parts.title: Data Modeling in Power Pivot
parts.description: In this chapter, you will begin exploring data modeling concepts in Power Pivot, including creating relationships and hierarchies.

parts.title: DAX in Power Pivot
parts.description: In this chapter, you will explore DAX (Data Analysis Expressions) in Power Pivot. You will learn to write DAX formulas to create calculated columns and measures. You will also understand the importance of row and filter context when using DAX.

parts.title: Dashboards with Power Pivot
parts.description: In the final chapter, you will make your Excel reports interactive with Power Pivot by adding slicers and organizing your visuals in a way that tells a data story.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: The course covers importing data from various sources, preparing data for analysis, and creating relationships in a data model, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in data management.
The course introduces basic calculations and measures using DAX, supporting foundational understanding of summarizing and describing data features.
The course teaches creating dashboards and visualizations to tell data stories and uncover insights, matching intermediate proficiency in data visualization.
The course emphasizes telling compelling data stories and uncovering actionable insights, which aligns with foundational business acumen and storytelling.

title: Introduction to BigQuery
description: Embark on this course for practical insights into data analysis. Explore BigQuery's architecture, run analytical queries, and optimize workflows. Gain confidence in navigating datasets, query elements, and data manipulation. Unlock advanced techniques for efficient analysis and master the art of joining data. Upon completion, navigate BigQuery effectively, optimize queries, and analyze data swiftly.

parts.title: BigQuery Architecture and Structure
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn about the unique features of BigQuery, how it runs large analytical queries, and how it compares to other data warehouses and databases.

parts.title: Writing queries and data types
parts.description: This chapter will cover the fundamentals of how to write queries in BigQuery while also providing a review of SQL concepts. You will also learn how to ingest bulk data into BigQuery and the different data types within BigQuery.

parts.title: Querying data in BigQuery
parts.description: Learn how to query data using common table expressions, aggregations, and window functions.

parts.title: Data management and optimization
parts.description: Understand all join types in BigQuery, mange data with data manipulation, and optimize your queries.

proficiency.DS: This course covers data ingestion, manipulation, and optimization in BigQuery, aligning with intermediate proficiency where combining datasets, automating cleaning tasks, and optimizing workflows are required.

The course teaches writing and optimizing queries, using SQL concepts, and managing data programmatically, which matches intermediate programming skills involving data manipulation and workflow optimization.

title: Case Study: Analyzing Fitness Data in Alteryx
description: The fitness product industry is intensely competitive, and success depends on developing effective marketing strategies and products that align with customers' fitness routines and lifestyles. In this Alteryx case study, you will analyze real-world fitness tracker data to identify app usage patterns, assess customers'  fitness levels, and understand their schedules. As you analyze the data, you'll provide feedback to Bellabeat, a fitness product company, on potential product improvements and marketing strategies. You will use your Alteryx skills to prepare, transform, and blend data to derive actionable insights. By consolidating your findings into a single, comprehensive table, you'll effectively communicate insights to the Bellabeat team, demonstrating the practical application of your Alteryx skills. Whether you're a data enthusiast, aspiring analyst, or seasoned professional looking to enhance your Alteryx proficiency, this course provides the perfect opportunity to apply your skills to a real-world dataset.

parts.title: Journey Into Data
parts.description:
Understand what is a case study and what are the steps included in data analysis process  .
Learn how to perform basic data check by finding - unique Ids, duplicate rows and NULL values.
Practice how to create calculated fields .

parts.title: Diving Further Into Data
parts.description: This chapter covers date field conversion, dataset integration through joins, average calculations, and the determination of activity/sitting thresholds and BMI categories to enable comprehensive user analysis.

parts.title: Wrapping Up
parts.description: Explore date transformations, activity level comparisons, and inference-based recommendations using Alteryx tools like Union, Sort, Transpose, and Crosstab in fitness-tracking data analysis.

proficiency.DS: The course covers basic data checks (unique IDs, duplicates, NULLs), calculated fields, and simple data transformations, which align with foundational data processing skills such as loading, cleaning, and preparing data for analysis.

The course includes dataset integration through joins, complex calculations (averages, thresholds, BMI categories), and blending data, which matches intermediate proficiency in combining datasets, automating cleaning tasks, and performing more complex data manipulations.

The course requires consolidating findings into a comprehensive table and communicating insights, which aligns with foundational technical communication skills such as presenting basic analysis results in clear, simple terms.
Participants provide actionable feedback on product improvements and marketing strategies, demonstrating a basic understanding of how data analysis can contribute to business goals.

title: Financial Trading in R
description: This course will cover the basics on financial trading and will give you an overview of how to use quantstrat to build signal-based trading strategies in R. It will teach you how to set up a quantstrat strategy, apply transformations of market data called indicators, create signals based on the interactions of those indicators, and even simulate orders. Lastly, it will explain how to analyze your results both from statistical and visual perspectives.

parts.title: Trading basics
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn the definition of trading, the philosophies of trading, and the pitfalls that exist in trading. This chapter covers both momentum and oscillation trading, along with some phrases to identify these types of philosophies. You will learn about overfitting and how to avoid it, obtaining and plotting financial data, and using a well-known indicator in trading.

parts.title: A boilerplate for quantstrat strategies
parts.description: Before building a strategy, the quantstrat package requires you to initialize some settings. In this chapter you will learn how this is done. You will cover a series of functions that deal with initializing a time zone, currency, the instruments you'll be working with, along with quantstrat's various frameworks that will allow it to perform analytics. Once this is done, you will have the knowledge to set up a quantstrat initialization file, and know how to change it.

parts.title: Indicators
parts.description: Indicators are crucial for your trading strategy. They are transformations of market data that allow a clearer understanding of its overall behavior, usually in exchange for lagging the market behavior. Here, you will be working with both trend types of indicators as well as oscillation indicators. You will also learn how to use pre-programmed indicators available in other libraries as well as implement one of your own.

parts.title: Signals
parts.description: When constructing a quantstrat strategy, you want to see how the market interacts with indicators and how indicators interact with each other. In this chapter you'll learn how indicators can generate signals in quantstrat. Signals are interactions of market data with indicators, or indicators with other indicators. There are four types of signals in quantstrat: sigComparison, sigCrossover, sigThreshold, and sigFormula. By the end of this chapter, you'll know all about these signals, what they do, and how to use them.

parts.title: Rules
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn how to shape your trading transaction once you decide to execute on a signal. This chapter will cover a basic primer on rules, and how to enter and exit positions. You'll also learn how to send inputs to order-sizing functions. By the end of this chapter, you'll learn the gist of how rules function, and where you can continue learning about them.

parts.title: Analyzing results
parts.description: After a quantstrat strategy has been constructed, it's vital to know how to actually analyze the strategy's performance. This chapter details just that. You will learn how to read vital trade statistics, and view the performance of your trading strategy over time. You will also learn how to get a reward to risk ratio called the Sharpe ratio in two different ways. This is the last chapter.

topic.name: Applied Finance
topic.description: The finance community has been one of the eager to embrace data science. From stock market predictions, to asset pricing and calculating the probability of loan defaults, the applications are nearly endless!

proficiency.DS: The course requires implementing trading strategies in R using quantstrat, working with functions, libraries, and data manipulation, which aligns with intermediate programming proficiency.
The course covers statistical analysis of trading results, including concepts like overfitting and the Sharpe ratio, matching intermediate-level statistical application.
Learners obtain, clean, transform, and analyze financial data, as well as automate parts of the workflow, which fits intermediate data processing skills.
The course teaches how to visualize financial data and trading results, including plotting and interpreting performance metrics, suitable for intermediate proficiency.
By focusing on financial trading strategies and performance analysis, the course links data science to business objectives in finance, aligning with intermediate business acumen.

title: Streamlined Data Ingestion with pandas
description: Before you can analyze data, you first have to acquire it. This course teaches you how to build pipelines to import data kept in common storage formats. You'll use pandas, a major Python library for analytics, to get data from a variety of sources, from spreadsheets of survey responses, to a database of public service requests, to an API for a popular review site. Along the way, you'll learn how to fine-tune imports to get only what you need and to address issues like incorrect data types. Finally, you'll assemble a custom dataset from a mix of sources.

parts.title: Importing Data from Flat Files
parts.description: Practice using pandas to get just the data you want from flat files, learn how to wrangle data types and handle errors, and look into some U.S. tax data along the way.

parts.title: Importing Data From Excel Files
parts.description: Automate data imports from that staple of office life, Excel files. Import part or all of a workbook and ensure boolean and datetime data are properly loaded, all while learning about how other people are learning to code.

parts.title: Importing Data from Databases
parts.description: Combine pandas with the powers of SQL to find out just how many problems New Yorkers have with their housing. This chapter features introductory SQL topics like WHERE clauses, aggregate functions, and basic joins.

parts.title: Importing JSON Data and Working with APIs
parts.description: Learn how to work with JSON data and web APIs by exploring a public dataset and getting cafe recommendations from Yelp. End by learning some techniques to combine datasets once they have been loaded into data frames.

proficiency.DS: This course covers combining multiple datasets from various sources, automating data cleaning tasks, handling data types, and merging data, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in Data Management.
The course teaches using Python and pandas for basic data import and manipulation, matching foundational programming skills such as using libraries for data tasks.

title: Understanding Digital Transformation
description: Dive into the world of digital transformation with this comprehensive course. Learn the impact of digitalization on organizations and individuals, uncover various roles within digital transformation, and understand the crucial triad of data, people, and processes. Develop key skills in data and AI literacy, empowering decision-making and effective implementation of digital initiatives. Tackle common challenges and obstacles faced in this journey, and master the art of creating and executing a strategic plan for successful digital transformation. Equip yourself to be an agent of change in this rapidly evolving digital landscape.

parts.title: Transformation journey
parts.description: Discover the essence of digital transformation and its sweeping impact on technology, businesses, and personal experiences. Learn through real-world examples like the evolution of smartphones and personal computers, highlighting the transformative power of this phenomenon.

parts.title: Impacting digital transformation
parts.description: Uncover the various roles crucial to digital transformation and where you fit in this evolving landscape. Learn about the triad of digital transformation: data, people, and processes, and how they interact to drive change.

parts.title: Organizational digital transformation
parts.description: Explore how digital transformation revolutionizes organizations by integrating a holistic approach. Dive into the challenges and obstacles faced during this transformation, including cultural shifts, legacy systems, and skill gaps.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces the fundamentals of digital transformation, emphasizing the importance of data, people, and processes in business contexts. It builds basic data and AI literacy, helping learners recognize business problems and opportunities where digital initiatives can contribute to organizational goals.

Learners are introduced to the process of creating and executing strategic plans for digital transformation, which aligns with foundational project management skills such as planning tasks, understanding timelines, and identifying challenges in digital projects.

The course empowers learners to become agents of change by understanding digital transformation, tackling obstacles, and developing skills to implement digital initiatives, which matches the foundational level of promoting innovation and guiding change.

title: Data Transformation in Alteryx
description: Welcome to Data Transformation in Alteryx! Dive into mastering the Formula Tool, Logical Operators, Crosstab, and Transpose. Efficiently reshape and analyze data with several of Alteryx's most powerful tools.

parts.title: The Formula Tool
parts.description: Discover the power of string functions, mathematical functions, and conditional statements such as IF, ELSEIF, and IIF with the formula tool. Dig into more complex conditional logic with AND (&&), OR (||), and NOT (!) keywords and operators. Be ready for numerous formula tool use cases you might encounter in your datasets.

parts.title: The Transpose Tool
parts.description: The transpose tool gives you the power to alter the orientation of a data table, pivoting so horizontal data fields become vertical. Learn how to configure this tool, and when to use it. This allows for extracting data in non-standard formats. There's no limit on the number of rows or fields that can be transposed. You'll be making datasets longer and skinnier in no time!

parts.title: The Cross Tab Tool
parts.description: Explore the Cross Tab Tool in Alteryx, unpivoting columns into rows and aggregating data based on specified parameters. Gain insights into configuring this tool to seamlessly reshape your data, facilitating streamlined analysis and reporting. With the Cross Tab Tool, you'll unlock the potential to efficiently organize your data in the desired format, paving the way for reporting, visualization, and deeper exploration of your datasets.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced data transformation techniques such as pivoting, unpivoting, and applying complex conditional logic using Alteryx tools, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on automating data cleaning, combining datasets, and performing complex manipulations.

title: Case Study: Set Up a Book Recommendation App in Azure
description:
Ready to apply your knowledge of Azure Fundamentals?

In this case study, you'll act as an Azure consultant with your team for AppSculpt, a company that specializes in creating recommendation apps. They wish to move their book recommendation app to Azure, and you'll assist them in this process.

Through hands-on exercises, you'll estimate costs using the pricing calculator, set up and configure the right resources, and ensure that your Azure environment is properly secured and monitored.

parts.title: Getting to know the case study
parts.description: The company AppSculpt wishes to set up its book recommendation app ReadRadar in Azure and they've hired you as their Azure consultant. You'll kick off this project by learning how the ReadRadar book recommendation app works, and how it will work in Azure. You'll then prepare your Azure environment and calculate the budget needed to set up the necessary services and resources.

parts.title: Setting up the necessary resources
parts.description: It's time to set up the project's first resources! You'll upload a text file with book data to Azure using Blob Storage for further use by the recommendation model underpinning ReadRadar. For the data science team, you'll set up a data science virtual machine to help them develop and test the recommendation engine.

parts.title: Optimizing security and performance
parts.description: You've set up the necessary resources and configured them correctly. Now, you can focus on optimizing security and performance using the management and monitoring tools available in Azure.

proficiency.DS: The course involves managing the migration of an app to Azure, including planning, resource allocation, risk identification, and stakeholder communication, aligning with intermediate project management competencies.
Learners upload and manage book data in Azure Blob Storage, automate resource setup, and ensure data is accessible for the recommendation model, matching intermediate data management skills.
The course covers basic setup and configuration of cloud resources, requiring foundational programming and scripting skills for automation and resource management.

title: Support Vector Machines in R
description: This course will introduce a powerful classifier, the support vector machine (SVM) using an intuitive, visual approach. Support Vector Machines in R will help students develop an understanding of the SVM model as a classifier and gain practical experience using R's libsvm implementation from the e1071 package. Along the way, students will gain an intuitive understanding of important concepts, such as hard and soft margins, the kernel trick, different types of kernels, and how to tune SVM parameters. Get ready to classify data with this impressive model.

parts.title: Introduction
parts.description: This chapter introduces some key concepts of support vector machines through a simple 1-dimensional example. Students are also walked through the  creation of a linearly separable dataset that is used in the subsequent chapter.

parts.title: Support Vector Classifiers - Linear Kernels
parts.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of support vector machines by applying the svm algorithm to a dataset that is linearly separable. Key concepts are illustrated through ggplot visualisations that are built from the outputs of the algorithm and the role of the cost parameter is highlighted via a simple example.  The chapter closes with a section on how the algorithm deals with multiclass problems.

parts.title: Polynomial Kernels
parts.description: Provides an introduction to polynomial kernels via a dataset that is radially separable (i.e. has a circular decision boundary). After demonstrating the inadequacy of linear kernels for this dataset, students will see how a simple transformation renders the problem linearly separable thus motivating an intuitive discussion of the kernel trick. Students will then apply the polynomial kernel to the dataset and tune the resulting classifier.

parts.title: Radial Basis Function Kernels
parts.description: Builds on the previous three chapters by introducing the highly flexible Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel. Students will create a "complex" dataset that shows up the limitations of polynomial kernels. Then, following an intuitive motivation for the RBF kernel, students see how it addresses the shortcomings of the other kernels discussed in this course.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course covers practical application of support vector machines (SVMs), including kernel methods, parameter tuning, and multiclass classification, which aligns with the intermediate proficiency level's focus on applying machine learning techniques to real-world problems and evaluating model performance.

The course provides an intuitive understanding of SVMs, including concepts like margins and kernels, and involves interpreting model outputs and tuning, which matches the intermediate level's requirements for applying and interpreting statistical and machine learning models.

Students gain hands-on experience implementing SVMs in R using the e1071 package, working with code to manipulate data and tune models, which fits the intermediate level's expectation for designing and implementing functions and using libraries for data analysis.

title: Data Fluency
description:
Data is everywhere, and in today's data-driven world, being data-fluent is a necessity, not only for individuals but for organizations overall. Data fluency isn't just about understanding data; it's about the ability to work with and use data effectively to make data-driven decisions. This exciting conceptual course will equip you with unearth best practices and essential skills required for data fluency mastery!

You'll start by learning the meaning of data fluency and its difference with data literacy You'll also learn about the importance of data fluency in today's world. You will be introduced to a framework on how to achieve data fluency; at the individual but also organizational levels!

Next, you'll discover the behaviors of data-fluent individuals along with the skills they utilize from the first step of identifying business problems with data up to communicating insights effectively for decision-making.

You'll finish by deep-diving into the elements of a data-fluent organization. You'll discover the behaviors and habits of a data-fluent culture, and how to shape such culture. Lastly, you'll learn how a strong ecosystem covering infrastructure, tools, and processes can enable organizational data fluency!

parts.title: The Journey to Data Fluency
parts.description: Embarking on a journey to data fluency! To begin the course, you'll learn what data fluency is and how it differs from data literacy. You'll also discover the outcomes of data fluency and the required elements to achieve data fluency at individual and organizational levels.

parts.title: Data Fluent Individuals
parts.description: Individual data fluency encompasses the skills individuals need to have to effectively make data-driven decisions. In this chapter, you'll learn how data-fluent individuals identify business problems with data, translate those problems into analytical questions, as well as how they work with data effectively, and communicate their findings to take action.

parts.title: Data Fluent Organization
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll dive deeper into the various elements that shape organizational data fluency. You'll learn the behaviors present in a data-fluent culture as well as the power of a strong data ecosystem that supports data fluency including the data infrastructure, tools, and lastly, the processes and organizational structure.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces the basics of identifying business problems with data and understanding how data-driven decisions impact organizations, aligning with foundational business acumen requirements.
The course covers communicating insights effectively for decision-making, which matches the foundational level of technical communication competency.
By discussing organizational data fluency, infrastructure, and processes, the course supports foundational knowledge of project management in a data context.

title: Understanding Microsoft Azure Architecture and Services
description: Continue your journey towards the Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) certification with this introductory course on Microsoft Azure's architecture and services. Learn key components like virtual machines, databases, networking, and storage through interactive exercises. Gain hands-on experience designing scalable cloud infrastructure and managing resources using best practices.

parts.title: Azure Storage Services
parts.description: This chapter provides a brief overview of Azure architecture and services, with a subsequent focus on the storage services available in the Azure cloud.

parts.title: Compute and Networking Services
parts.description: This chapter provides an overview of compute services within Azure Cloud, exploring virtual machines, networking components, and app services in more detail.

parts.title: Identity, Access Control and Security
parts.description: This chapter explores Azure's identity and access control, covering the shift to cloud-based identity solutions, access control features, and key security concepts like RBAC and zero trust, with a focus on Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces basic concepts of cloud storage, compute, and networking, aligning with foundational data management skills such as loading, storing, and managing data using cloud infrastructure.

Learners gain exposure to managing cloud resources and understanding infrastructure components, supporting foundational project management skills like resource allocation and understanding project environments.

title: CI/CD for Machine Learning
description:
The course will empower you to streamline your machine learning development processes, enhancing efficiency, reliability, and reproducibility in your projects. Throughout the course, you'll develop a comprehensive understanding of CI/CD workflows and YAML syntax, utilizing GitHub Actions (GA) for automation, training models in a pipeline, versioning datasets with DVC, and performing hyperparameter tuning.

You'll be introduced to the fundamental concepts of CI/CD and YAML, and gain an understanding of the software development life cycle and key terms like build, test, and deploy. You'll define Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment while examining their distinctions. You'll also explore the utility of CI/CD in machine learning and experimentation.

You'll learn about GA, a powerful platform for implementing CI/CD workflows. You'll discover the various elements of GA, including events, actions, jobs, steps, runners, and context. You'll learn how to define workflows triggered by events such as push and pull requests and customize runner machines. You'll also gain practical experience by setting up basic CI pipelines and understanding the GA log.

You'll delve deep into Data Version Control (DVC) for versioning datasets, initializing DVC, and tracking datasets. Using DVC pipelines, you'll learn how to train classification models and generate metrics in a reproducible manner.

You'll then focus on model performance analysis and hyperparameter tuning and gain practical skills in comparing metrics and plots across branches to track changes in model performance. You'll learn how to perform hyperparameter tuning using scikit-learn's GridSearchCV. Additionally, you'll explore automating pull requests with the best model configuration.

parts.title: Introduction to Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery and YAML
parts.description: In this chapter, you will explore the essential principles of Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) and YAML. You'll grasp the software development life cycle and key terms like build, test, and deploy. Discover the differences between Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment. Moreover, you'll investigate the significance of CI/CD in machine learning and experimentation.

parts.title: GitHub Actions
parts.description: Get ready to explore GitHub Actions (GHA), an influential platform for executing CI/CD workflows. Uncover the diverse components of GHA, encompassing events, actions, jobs, steps, runners, and context. Gain insights into crafting workflows that activate upon events like push and pull requests, and tailor runner machines. Dive into hands-on learning as you establish fundamental CI pipelines and grasp the intricacies of the GHA log.

parts.title: Continuous Integration in Machine Learning
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll explore the integration of machine learning model training into a GitHub Action pipeline using Continuous Machine Learning GitHub Action. You'll generate a comprehensive markdown report including model metrics and plots. You will also delve into data versioning in Machine Learning by adopting Data Version Control (DVC) to track data changes. The chapter also covers setting DVC remotes and dataset transfers. Finally, you'll explore DVC pipelines, configuring a DVC YAML file to orchestrate reproducible model training.

parts.title: Comparing training runs and Hyperparameter (HP) tuning
parts.description:
In this chapter, you will direct your attention towards the analysis of model performance and the fine-tuning of hyperparameters. You will acquire practical expertise in comparing metrics and visualizations across different branches to assess changes in model performance. You will 
 conduct hyperparameter tuning using scikit-learn's GridSearchCV. Furthermore, you will delve into the automation of pull requests using the optimal model configuration.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced code management practices such as CI/CD workflows, version control with DVC, and automation using GitHub Actions, aligning with the advanced proficiency level's focus on optimizing workflows, enforcing standards, and ensuring reproducibility in collaborative projects.

The course teaches automation, workflow orchestration, and integration of advanced frameworks (e.g., GitHub Actions, DVC), which matches the advanced level's emphasis on optimizing code for performance, implementing best practices, and developing scalable solutions.

By introducing CI/CD for ML, resource management, and automation of model deployment, the course supports advanced project management skills such as planning complex projects, risk mitigation, and coordinating cross-functional teams.

title: Introduction to Financial Statements in Power BI
description:
Analyzing financial statements is an important part of understanding the firm's financial health. In this course, we will examine the financial statements of a fictitious automotive company, Larry's Automotive.

We will focus our analysis on the income statement and balance sheet. You will use data visualization to create custom dashboards for the firm's financial information, which will help you identify trends, KPIs, and errors.

In addition to calculating key performance measures, such as COGs and EBITDA, we will spend time determining key profitability ratios, like profit margin. These skills will put you on a good path to becoming a financial analyst.

parts.title: The Evolution of the Financial Statement
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn the components the balance sheet and income statement and see how they are derived from the accounting equation.  With this information, you will examine these financial statements using DAX and creating key measures.

parts.title: Budgetary Planning
parts.description: Budgetary and Forecast planning plays a key role in the financial well-being of a company. By calculating and visualizing the budget, forecast and variance, you will learn how to detect valuable business trends.

parts.title: Company Performance  and Financial Analysis
parts.description: Performance ratios are financial ratios and other information, that allows a company to determine how well they are doing. You will learn liquidity ratios and how they indicate a firms debt obligation and firm risk.

topic.name: Applied Finance
topic.description: The finance community has been one of the eager to embrace data science. From stock market predictions, to asset pricing and calculating the probability of loan defaults, the applications are nearly endless!

proficiency.DS: The course introduces basic data visualization techniques in Power BI, enabling learners to create dashboards and visualize financial data, which aligns with foundational skills in presenting data clearly.

Learners gain an understanding of financial statements, key business metrics, and profitability ratios, matching the foundational level of recognizing business problems and presenting data findings relevant to stakeholders.
The course covers calculation of key performance measures and ratios, which aligns with foundational proficiency in summarizing and describing data using basic statistics.

title: Working with Hugging Face
description: Hugging Face is a vital platform for machine learning and AI tasks due to its robust workflows and extensive model repository. In this course, you'll first explore the basics of Hugging Face, including its components, available models, and datasets. You'll then unlock the potential of state-of-the-art transformers and frameworks for ML and AI tasks, starting with NLP. You'll discover essential pipelines and expand into tasks involving images and audio. The journey concludes with a focus on fine-tuning models and using embeddings for downstream tasks like searching.

parts.title: Getting Started with Hugging Face
parts.description: Start your journey with the Hugging Face platform by understanding what Hugging Face is and common use cases. Then, you'll learn about the Hugging Face Hub including models and datasets available, how to search for them, navigate model, or dataset, cards, and download. Lastly, you'll learn about the high-level components of transformers and LLMs.

parts.title: Building Pipelines with Hugging Face
parts.description: It's time to dive into the Hugging Face ecosystem! You'll start by learning the basics of the pipeline module and Auto classes from the transformers library. Then, you'll learn at a high level what natural language processing and tokenization is. Finally, you'll start using the pipeline module for several text-based tasks, including text classification.

parts.title: Building Pipelines for Image and Audio
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll apply pipeline methodologies to new tasks using image and audio data. Specifically, you will learn ways to process these types of data in preparation for tasks such as classification, question and answering and automatic speech recognition.

parts.title: Fine-tuning and Embeddings
parts.description: Explore the different frameworks for fine-tuning, text generation, and embeddings. Start with the basics of fine-tuning a pre-trained model on a specific dataset and task to improve performance. Then, use Auto classes to generate the text from prompts and images. Finally, you will explore how to generate and use embeddings.

proficiency.DS: The course covers applying and fine-tuning state-of-the-art models, using pipelines for NLP, image, and audio tasks, and working with embeddings-matching the intermediate level's focus on applying deep learning, fine-tuning models, and integrating AI techniques into real-world tasks.
Learners use Python and Hugging Face libraries to build and automate pipelines for various data types, aligning with the intermediate level's emphasis on implementing libraries and automating tasks.
The course includes preparing and processing text, image, and audio data for ML tasks, which fits the intermediate level's requirements for handling and transforming diverse data types for analysis.

title: LLMOps Concepts
description:
Embark on a journey into Large Language Model Operations (LLMOps). This course, designed for enthusiasts and professionals alike, guides you through the basics, from ideation to operational deployment.

Delving into the LLM application lifecycle will reveal its pivotal role in organizations. You will gain insights into the challenges and considerations at each stage and how to refine development and ensure smooth deployment while embracing data governance and security. By the end of the course, you'll have a solid grasp of LLMOps concepts and know how to apply them to your applications.

parts.title: Introduction to LLMOps & Ideation Phase
parts.description: This chapter provides an introduction to LLMOps and the ideation phase of LLM application development. It explains the basics of LLMOps, highlights the lifecycle stages of LLMs, and covers key activities in the ideation phase, such as data sourcing and selecting between open-source and proprietary LLMs.

parts.title: Development Phase
parts.description: This chapter focuses on the development phase of LLM application creation. It covers prompt engineering, agents and chains, RAG versus fine-tuning techniques, and testing methods.

parts.title: Operational Phase
parts.description: This chapter focuses on the operational phase of LLM application deployment and management. We will cover deployment strategies like CI/CD, scaling techniques, monitoring practices, cost management strategies, and governance and security considerations. Mastering these concepts will help you efficiently manage LLM applications in operational environments.

proficiency.DS: The course covers the LLM application lifecycle, including development (prompt engineering, fine-tuning, agents), deployment, and monitoring, aligning with intermediate proficiency in applying AI techniques to real-world problems and integrating AI agents into pipelines.

The course addresses the end-to-end lifecycle of LLM applications, including planning, development, deployment, and operational management, which matches the intermediate level of managing project phases, monitoring progress, and addressing governance and security.

The course discusses data sourcing, data governance, and operational considerations for LLMs, fitting the intermediate level of combining datasets, automating cleaning, and ensuring data readiness for AI applications.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Responsible and Ethical AI Use
proficiency.DS: The course emphasizes governance and security in LLM deployment, aligning with the intermediate level of using tools like Algorithmic Impact Assessment and communicating risks of AI-generated content.

title: Data Manipulation in Alteryx
description: In today's data-driven landscape, efficient data manipulation is crucial, and Alteryx offers powerful tools to achieve just that. In this course, you'll explore unions, appends, joins, parsing, and performance optimization, empowering you to streamline your workflow and elevate your analytics game. We will delve into the core elements of Alteryx, mastering techniques to harmonize your data seamlessly and supercharge your analytical capabilities. Learn to transform data challenges into triumphs!

parts.title: Unions and appends
parts.description: In Chapter One, you will explore the realms of Unions and Appends, delving into the fundamentals of data manipulation using Alteryx. By the chapter's end, you will adeptly blend diverse data sources, merging datasets with precision, and mastering the art of unions and appends to gain a comprehensive understanding of your data.

parts.title: Joins
parts.description: In Chapter Two, you will delve into the world of Joins, uncovering the intricacies of combining data from multiple tables using Alteryx. By the end of the chapter, you will skillfully navigate various join types, merging data with precision, and mastering the art of inner, left, right, and full outer joins to achieve a deeper understanding of your data relationships.

parts.title: Parsing
parts.description: In Chapter Three, you will explore the realm of string and date/time parsing in Alteryx, unraveling the complexities of transforming text and temporal data. By the conclusion of the chapter, you will adeptly manipulate strings, extract valuable information, and convert date/time formats with finesse. Mastering these techniques will empower you to cleanse and prepare your data for more accurate analysis and insightful interpretations.

parts.title: Performance optimization
parts.description: In Chapter Four, you will delve into the critical aspect of performance optimization in Alteryx. This chapter is dedicated to identifying and addressing various bottlenecks that can impede workflow efficiency, such as data volume, tool-specific limitations, workflow design, and resource management. You will learn strategies to enhance performance by employing performance profiling, disabling unnecessary outputs, and caching workflows. By the end of this chapter, you will be equipped with the knowledge and skills to optimize your Alteryx workflows, ensuring they run smoothly and efficiently, even with large datasets and complex operations.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: This course covers combining datasets using unions, appends, and joins, as well as parsing and performance optimization in Alteryx. These skills align with the intermediate level, which requires handling multiple data sources, automating cleaning tasks, and performing complex data manipulations.
