title: Statistical Thinking in Python (Part 2)
description: After completing Statistical Thinking in Python (Part 1), you have the probabilistic mindset and foundational hacker stats skills to dive into data sets and extract useful information from them. In this course, you will do just that, expanding and honing your hacker stats toolbox to perform the two key tasks in statistical inference, parameter estimation and hypothesis testing. You will work with real data sets as you learn, culminating with analysis of measurements of the beaks of the Darwin's famous finches. You will emerge from this course with new knowledge and lots of practice under your belt, ready to attack your own inference problems out in the world.

parts.title: Parameter estimation by optimization
parts.description: When doing statistical inference, we speak the language of probability. A probability distribution that describes your data has parameters. So, a major goal of statistical inference is to estimate the values of these parameters, which allows us to concisely and unambiguously describe our data and draw conclusions from it. In this chapter, you will learn how to find the optimal parameters, those that best describe your data.

parts.title: Bootstrap confidence intervals
parts.description: To "pull yourself up by your bootstraps" is a classic idiom meaning that you achieve a difficult task by yourself with no help at all. In statistical inference, you want to know what would happen if you could repeat your data acquisition an infinite number of times. This task is impossible, but can we use only the data we actually have to get close to the same result as an infinitude of experiments? The answer is yes! The technique to do it is aptly called bootstrapping. This chapter will introduce you to this extraordinarily powerful tool.

parts.title: Introduction to hypothesis testing
parts.description: You now know how to define and estimate parameters given a model. But the question remains: how reasonable is it to observe your data if a model is true? This question is addressed by hypothesis tests. They are the icing on the inference cake. After completing this chapter, you will be able to carefully construct and test hypotheses using hacker statistics.

parts.title: Hypothesis test examples
parts.description: As you saw from the last chapter, hypothesis testing can be a bit tricky. You need to define the null hypothesis, figure out how to simulate it, and define clearly what it means to be "more extreme" in order to compute the p-value. Like any skill, practice makes perfect, and this chapter gives you some good practice with hypothesis tests.

parts.title: Putting it all together: a case study
parts.description: Every year for the past 40-plus years, Peter and Rosemary Grant have gone to the Galápagos island of Daphne Major and collected data on Darwin's finches. Using your skills in statistical inference, you will spend this chapter with their data, and witness first hand, through data, evolution in action. It's an exhilarating way to end the course!

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course covers parameter estimation, hypothesis testing, and bootstrap confidence intervals, which align with the intermediate proficiency level requiring application of inferential statistics, hypothesis testing, and interpretation of statistical results.
The course uses Python for statistical inference tasks, matching the intermediate level where learners implement data analysis using libraries and write scripts for statistical tasks.

title: Case Study: Analyzing Sales Data in Alteryx
description:
Are you ready to explore the power of Alteryx Designer with a focus on retail sales data? In this case study, you will analyze data from a fictional department store to tackle questions related to sales performance.
Using Alteryx Designer, you'll prepare, blend, and analyze data to help answer questions about sales trends and patterns. This hands-on course will guide you through creating workflows to analyze product performance, helping you identify key drivers of sales success.
By the end of this case study, you'll have the skills to leverage Alteryx Designer for comprehensive sales analysis, enabling informed business decisions and strategic planning. Dive into data and transform it into actionable insights with Alteryx Designer.

parts.title: Data Blending and Date Conversion
parts.description: You have gained many new Alteryx skills over the past several courses. After introducing the case study, this chapter will test your knowledge of combining data, working with dates, and cleaning up general data. You'll also get a surprise assignment added by your boss!

parts.title: Data Transformations
parts.description: Get ready to transform some data! This chapter will allow you to pivot, parse, clean, and calculate data. Once the data is ready, you'll join it to the data from the previous chapter in preparation for any upcoming analysis.

parts.title: Ready, Set, Analyze
parts.description: Your data is finally ready for analysis! After carefully prepping and combining your data, you'll use this chapter to transform, calculate, and summarize your way to the answers asked of you by the company bosses.

proficiency.DS: The course covers combining datasets, cleaning, transforming, and preparing data for analysis using Alteryx, which aligns with intermediate-level skills such as automating data cleaning tasks, processing structured data, and performing complex data manipulations.

The course applies data analysis to answer business questions about sales performance and strategic planning, matching the intermediate level's focus on aligning data projects with business objectives and communicating findings to influence decisions.

title: ETL and ELT in Python
description: Data pipelines are at the foundation of every strong data platform. Building these pipelines is an essential skill for data engineers, who provide incredible value to a business ready to step into a data-driven future. This introductory course will help you hone the skills to build effective, performant, and reliable data pipelines.

parts.title: Introduction to Data Pipelines
parts.description: Get ready to discover how data is collected, processed, and moved using data pipelines. You will explore the qualities of the best data pipelines, and prepare to design and build your own.

parts.title: Building ETL Pipelines
parts.description: Dive into leveraging pandas to extract, transform, and load data as you build your first data pipelines. Learn how to make your ETL logic reusable, and apply logging and exception handling to your pipelines.

parts.title: Advanced ETL Techniques
parts.description: Supercharge your workflow with advanced data pipelining techniques, such as working with non-tabular data and persisting DataFrames to SQL databases. Discover tooling to tackle advanced transformations with pandas, and uncover best-practices for working with complex data.

parts.title: Deploying and Maintaining a Data Pipeline
parts.description: In this final chapter, you'll create frameworks to validate and test data pipelines before shipping them into production. After you've tested your pipeline, you'll explore techniques to run your data pipeline end-to-end, all while allowing for visibility into pipeline performance.

proficiency.DS: The course covers building, automating, and maintaining ETL pipelines, handling structured and non-tabular data, and using Python tools like pandas-matching the intermediate level's focus on combining datasets, automating cleaning tasks, and processing data for analysis.

Learners design and implement reusable ETL functions, apply exception handling, and use libraries such as pandas, aligning with intermediate programming skills in Python for data manipulation and automation.

title: Case Study: Net Revenue Management in Google Sheets
description:
The world of Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) is a dynamic world that plays a significant role in our daily lives. Have you ever wondered how well-known brands like Coca-Cola, Nivea, and Lay's are being managed? This case study will help you get a better understanding of this industry.

You will start by analyzing a big dataset and by performing your own market analysis. You will go from calculating market share to creating clear visuals to reveal actionable insights. Next, you will use the principles of Net Revenue Management (NRM), which will help you to identify new growth opportunities for your company.

You will have to use a variety of Google Sheets tools and functions to calculate the true potential of these growth buckets. You will not only master everything which relates to PivotTables, VLOOKUP, and forecasting but also have a better understanding of what is happening behind the scenes of your favorite FMCG brands.

Are you ready to use your Google Sheets skills to build a complete business case?

parts.title: Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG)
parts.description: In the first chapter, you will be working as a category manager for Healthmax, a FMCG company active in the shampoo business. You will calculate Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) such as market share and value growth on various time dimensions such as year-to-date (YTD) and moving annual (MAT) total.

parts.title: Net Revenue Management (NRM)
parts.description:
In this chapter, you will learn about the concept of Net Revenue Management (NRM) and will focus on two of its pillars: Brand Portfolio Pricing and Mix Management.

You'll calculate important KPIs such as net sales contribution and gross margin. You'll also use brand Portfolio Pricing to identify the correct price for your consumers. Consecutively you'll use Mix Management techniques to help Healthmax launch a new product and expand into a new subcategory.

parts.title: Optimizing Net Revenue
parts.description:
In the last chapter, you will focus on the three remaining pillars of Net Revenue Management (NRM). Trade Terms Management will help you to decide in which customers and products you should be investing to grow your business.

You'll combine that information with Pack Price Architecture to develop a new pricing strategy for a small shampoo bottle and use a Promotion Management technique to identify the most successful promotion. Finally, you'll wrap it up by forecasting next year's growth by combining organic growth with the additional revenue of your NRM activities.

topic.name: Applied Finance
topic.description: The finance community has been one of the eager to embrace data science. From stock market predictions, to asset pricing and calculating the probability of loan defaults, the applications are nearly endless!

proficiency.DS: The course requires learners to conduct market analysis, calculate KPIs, and align data-driven insights with business objectives in the FMCG sector, matching the intermediate level's focus on applying data analysis to real-world business problems and collaborating with business teams.

Participants perform calculations such as market share, value growth, forecasting, and KPI analysis, which aligns with the intermediate proficiency in applying inferential statistics and regression to draw business-relevant conclusions.

The course involves analyzing large datasets, using Google Sheets functions like PivotTables and VLOOKUP, and automating calculations, reflecting intermediate skills in combining data sources, cleaning, and transforming data for analysis.

Learners are tasked with creating clear visuals to reveal actionable insights, which matches the intermediate level's requirement to create complex visualizations and communicate findings to stakeholders.

title: Introduction to Databricks
description: Welcome to the world of Databricks! In this course, you will be introduced to the Databricks Lakehouse platform and understand how it modernizes data architecture using the new Lakehouse paradigm. You'll explore the foundational components of Databricks, including the UI, platform architecture, and workspace administration. Interactive exercises will guide you through SQL queries, platform features, and external system connections for efficient data management and seamless integration. Additionally, you'll delve into the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, covering data management, compute capabilities, catalog management, and data ingestion. You'll also learn to use Databricks as a data warehousing solution for Business Intelligence (BI), leveraging SQL-optimized capabilities to create queries and analyze data.

parts.title: Introduction to Databricks
parts.description: Discover how the Databricks Lakehouse platform modernizes data architecture using the new Lakehouse paradigm. Explore the foundational components of Databricks and their integration. Engage with the Databricks UI, platform architecture, and workspace administration. At the same time, practical exercises guide you through SQL queries, platform features, and external system connections, introducing you to the efficient data management and seamless integration Databricks can offer.

parts.title: Data Intelligence Platform Fundamentals
parts.description: Learn the key components of the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform and how it can enhance your analytical processes. Explore Databricks fundamentals for data management and compute capabilities. You will also cover data catalog management and data ingestion. Get your hands dirty with interactive exercises that will guide you through integrating datasets, setting permissions, and configuring clusters.

parts.title: Introduction to SQL in Databricks
parts.description: Use the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform as your data warehousing solution for your Business Intelligence (BI) use cases. Use the built-in SQL-optimized capabilities within Databricks to create queries and dashboards on your data.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces foundational concepts of data management using Databricks, covering data ingestion, catalog management, and integration, which aligns with foundational proficiency in handling and preparing data for analysis.
Learners practice basic SQL queries and interact with Databricks' UI, matching foundational programming skills such as using built-in functions and performing simple data tasks.

The course demonstrates how Databricks supports business intelligence use cases and data-driven decision-making, which is relevant for foundational business acumen in understanding how data solutions support business functions.

title: Time Series Analysis in Power BI
description:
Analyze Time-Series Data With Power BI
You've taken datasets and analyzed them from every possible angle, but did you know that there is one dimension that every analysis shares in common? That's right; it's time! Have you ever thought about how your data varies over time as well?

Practice Common Analysis Techniques
In this Time Series Analysis in Power BI course, you will work with two different datasets and practice common techniques to analyze data over time. You will start by analyzing Superstoredata for Point of Sale (PoS) data across various locations and times, where you will calculate changes with different kinds of window, period-to-date, and period-over-period functions.

Use Built-In and DAX Algorithms
Then, you will dive into financial data from Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) and see how we can forecast data into the future, using both built-in and DAX algorithms to do so.

Following the course, you will have a well-rounded toolkit to tackle time series data and master the fourth dimension.

parts.title: Introduction to time series data
parts.description: An introduction to time series data. Learn to identify common patterns and formats of time data, and transform them to meet your needs.

parts.title: Working with window functions
parts.description: Learn about and create window functions within Power BI to analyze data over a set period of time.

parts.title: Looking ahead with forecasting
parts.description: Learn the basics of forecasting and how to predict values in the future using different methods in Power BI.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: The course covers time series analysis, including forecasting and period-over-period calculations, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in applying statistical techniques such as time series analysis and interpreting trends over time.

Learners use Power BI to visualize time series data, apply window functions, and create forecasts, matching the intermediate level's focus on creating complex visualizations and linking insights to business objectives.

title: Intermediate Python for Developers
description:
Are you ready to elevate your Python skills to the next level? This course will delve deeper into Python's rich ecosystem, focusing on essential aspects such as built-in functions, modules, and packages. You'll learn how to harness the power of Python's built-in functions effectively, enabling you to streamline your code.

The course will introduce you to the power of Python's modules, empowering you to develop quicker by reusing existing code rather than writing your own from scratch every time! You'll see how people have extended modules to create their own open-source software, known as packages, discovering how to download, import, and work with packages in your programs.

You'll progress to mastering the art of writing custom functions in Python. You'll learn best practices for defining functions, including comprehensive knowledge of how to write user-friendly docstrings to ensure clarity and maintainability. You'll dive into advanced concepts such as default arguments, enabling you to create versatile functions with predefined values. The course will equip you with the knowledge and skills to handle arbitrary positional and keyword arguments effectively, enhancing the flexibility and usability of your functions. By understanding how to work with these arguments, you'll be able to create more robust and adaptable solutions to various programming challenges.

Wrap up the course with debugging and error handling. You'll learn to interpret error messages, including tracebacks from incorrectly using functions from packages. You'll use keywords and techniques to adapt your custom functions, effectively handling errors and providing bespoke feedback messages to developers who misuse your code!

parts.title: The Python Ecosystem
parts.description: Discover Python's rich ecosystem of built-in functions and modules, plus how to download and work with packages.

parts.title: Working with functions
parts.description: Learn the fundamentals of functions, from Python's built-in functions to creating your own from scratch!

parts.title: Lambda functions and error-handling
parts.description: Build lambda functions on the fly, and discover how to error-proof your code!

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers intermediate programming concepts such as custom functions, modules, packages, and error handling in Python, aligning with the intermediate proficiency level which expects the ability to design and implement functions, use libraries for data manipulation, and write code with quality assurance practices.

The course introduces best practices for writing user-friendly docstrings and maintaining clarity in code, which matches the foundational level's emphasis on code documentation and understanding the purpose of version control and file structure.

title: Introduction to Importing Data in Python
description: As a data scientist, you will need to clean data, wrangle and munge it, visualize it, build predictive models, and interpret these models. Before you can do so, however, you will need to know how to get data into Python. In this course, you'll learn the many ways to import data into Python: from flat files such as .txt and .csv; from files native to other software such as Excel spreadsheets, Stata, SAS, and MATLAB files; and from relational databases such as SQLite and PostgreSQL.

parts.title: Introduction and flat files
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn how to import data into Python from all types of flat files, which are a simple and prevalent form of data storage. You've previously learned how to use NumPy and pandas-you will learn how to use these packages to import flat files and customize your imports.

parts.title: Importing data from other file types
parts.description: You've learned how to import flat files, but there are many other file types you will potentially have to work with as a data scientist. In this chapter, you'll learn how to import data into Python from a wide array of important file types. These include pickled files, Excel spreadsheets, SAS and Stata files, HDF5 files, a file type for storing large quantities of numerical data, and MATLAB files.

parts.title: Working with relational databases in Python
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn how to extract meaningful data from relational databases, an essential skill for any data scientist. You will learn about relational models, how to create SQL queries, how to filter and order your SQL records, and how to perform advanced queries by joining database tables.

proficiency.DS: This course teaches foundational skills in importing and handling data from various sources (flat files, Excel, databases) using Python, which aligns with entry-level requirements for loading and preparing data for analysis.
The course covers basic use of Python and its libraries (NumPy, pandas) for data import, matching the foundational proficiency in writing simple programs and manipulating data structures.

title: Python Toolbox
description: In this Python Toolbox course, you'll continue to build more advanced Python skills. First, you'll learn about iterators, objects you have already encountered in the context of for loops. You'll then learn about list comprehensions, which are extremely handy tools for all data professionals and developers working in Python. You'll end the course by working through a case study in which you'll apply all the techniques you learned in both parts of this course.

parts.title: Using iterators in PythonLand
parts.description: You'll learn all about iterators and iterables, which you have already worked with when writing for loops. You'll learn some handy functions that will allow you to effectively work with iterators. And you'll finish the chapter with a use case that is pertinent to the world of data science and dealing with large amounts of data-in this case, data from Twitter that you will load in chunks using iterators.

parts.title: List comprehensions and generators
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll build on your knowledge of iterators and be introduced to list comprehensions, which allow you to create complicated lists-and lists of lists-in one line of code! List comprehensions can dramatically simplify your code and make it more efficient, and will become a vital part of your Python toolbox. You'll then learn about generators, which are extremely helpful when working with large sequences of data that you may not want to store in memory, but instead generate on the fly.

parts.title: Bringing it all together!
parts.description: This chapter will allow you to apply your newly acquired skills toward wrangling and extracting meaningful information from a real-world dataset-the World Bank's World Development Indicators. You'll have the chance to write your own functions and list comprehensions as you work with iterators and generators to solidify your Python chops.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers iterators, list comprehensions, and generators, which align with intermediate proficiency in programming by teaching efficient data manipulation and more advanced Python constructs beyond the basics.
The course reinforces foundational programming skills by providing practical experience with iterators and list comprehensions, building on basic knowledge of loops and data structures.

title: Building Dashboards with Dash and Plotly
description: You don't need expensive vendor software to create insight-rich dashboards-you can do this using Plotly and Dash. Come on a journey and learn how to turn your Plotly visualizations into interactive dashboards using global e-commerce data. You'll learn the basics of web applications and discover how to structure and style your dashboards using HTML and CSS-building a portfolio of dashboards you can adapt to your data and projects. Are you ready to bring your plots to life?

parts.title: From Plotly to Dash
parts.description: Take Plotly to the next level with Dash.  After briefly revising Plotly, you'll dive straight into building your first Dash app. You'll then get your first taste of HTML and how Dash harnesses this vital web development language to structure larger Dash apps. Finally, you'll put all this together in your first multi-graph dashboard for a global e-commerce organization.

parts.title: Styling Dash Apps
parts.description: Take control of the elements in your Dash apps with HTML and CSS. Learn what each of these is and how they are at the core of modern web development, then incorporate their powerful abilities in your Dash apps to change the size, color, and placement of your objects.

parts.title: Interactivity with Callbacks and Components
parts.description: Turn your Dash apps into user-driven experiences by mastering interactive components. Learn how to include dropdowns, date pickers, and event free text fields to modify elements on your Dash apps and build truly self-service dashboards your users can explore.

parts.title: Advanced Dash Apps
parts.description: Unleash the full power of Dash app interactivity by triggering changes to one graph when a user clicks on or hovers over, another graph. Additionally, you'll learn the basics of Dash's Data Table module for creating tables that can be easily filtered, sorted, and paginated; as well as trigger changes in other graphs as well.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: This course teaches how to build interactive dashboards using Plotly and Dash, covering web app basics, HTML/CSS styling, and user-driven interactivity, which aligns with the intermediate level's focus on creating complex visualizations and adapting communication for different audiences.

Learners implement Python-based Dash apps, use libraries, and incorporate HTML/CSS, matching the intermediate proficiency of designing and implementing functions, using libraries for data manipulation, and enhancing applications with interactivity.

By building dashboards that communicate data insights interactively and visually, the course supports intermediate skills in organizing insights, adapting communication for stakeholders, and linking findings to business objectives.

title: Case Studies in Statistical Thinking
description:
Mastery requires practice. Having completed Statistical Thinking I and II, you developed your probabilistic mindset and the hacker stats skills to extract actionable insights from your data. Your foundation is in place, and now it is time practice your craft.

In this course, you will apply your statistical thinking skills, exploratory data analysis, parameter estimation, and hypothesis testing, to two new real-world data sets. First, you will explore data from the 2013 and 2015 FINA World Aquatics Championships, where you will quantify the relative speeds and variability among swimmers. You will then perform a statistical analysis to assess the "current controversy" of the 2013 Worlds in which swimmers claimed that a slight current in the pool was affecting result. Second, you will study the frequency and magnitudes of earthquakes around the world. Finally, you will analyze the changes in seismicity in the US state of Oklahoma after the practice of high pressure waste water injection at oil extraction sites became commonplace in the last decade. As you work with these data sets, you will take vital steps toward mastery as you cement your existing knowledge and broaden your abilities to use statistics and Python to make sense of your data.

parts.title: Fish sleep and bacteria growth: A review of Statistical Thinking I and II
parts.description: To begin, you'll use two data sets from Caltech researchers to rehash the key points of Statistical Thinking I and II to prepare you for the following case studies!

parts.title: Analysis of results of the 2015 FINA World Swimming Championships
parts.description: In this chapter, you will practice your EDA, parameter estimation, and hypothesis testing skills on the results of the 2015 FINA World Swimming Championships.

parts.title: The "Current Controversy" of the 2013 World Championships
parts.description: Some swimmers said that they felt it was easier to swim in one direction versus another in the 2013 World Championships. Some analysts have posited that there was a swirling current in the pool. In this chapter, you'll investigate this claim! References - Quartz Media, Washington Post, SwimSwam (and also here), and Cornett, et al.

parts.title: Statistical seismology and the Parkfield region
parts.description: Herein, you'll use your statistical thinking skills to study the frequency and magnitudes of earthquakes. Along the way, you'll learn some basic statistical seismology, including the Gutenberg-Richter law. This exercise exposes two key ideas about data science: 1) As a data scientist, you wander into all sorts of domain specific analyses, which is very exciting. You constantly get to learn. 2) You are sometimes faced with limited data, which is also the case for many of these earthquake studies. You can still make good progress!

parts.title: Earthquakes and oil mining in Oklahoma
parts.description: Of course, earthquakes have a big impact on society, and recently are connected to human activity. In this final chapter, you'll investigate the effect that increased injection of saline wastewater due to oil mining in Oklahoma has had on the seismicity of the region.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course applies inferential statistics, hypothesis testing, parameter estimation, and exploratory data analysis to real-world datasets, matching the intermediate proficiency level's focus on applying and interpreting statistical techniques such as hypothesis testing, regression, and multivariate analysis.

Learners analyze complex, domain-specific problems (e.g., statistical seismology, sports analytics), interpret findings, and broaden their statistical toolkit, aligning with advanced proficiency's emphasis on applying rigorous statistical techniques to solve complex problems and providing expert consultation.

title: Case Study: Analyzing Job Market Data in Power BI
description: In this Power BI case study, you'll explore a real-world job posting dataset to uncover insights for a fictional recruitment company called DataSearch. Using what you've learned from previous courses, you'll use Power Query to investigate and clean the data to find out what skills are most in-demand for data scientists, data analysts, and data engineers. You'll then use DAX to build insightful visualizations of your findings. Finally, you'll bring it all together using everything Power BI has to offer to create a business dashboard so that you can answer questions for the DataSearch team.

parts.title: Exploratory Analysis
parts.description: You'll start this Power BI case study by importing and cleaning the job posting dataset using Power Query. Once you've done this, it's time to roll up your sleeves and do some initial data exploration.

parts.title: Analyzing Market Trends
parts.description: The DataSearch team still needs answers. Luckily, they have you on their team! In this chapter, you'll continue to apply your Power BI skills to extract data insights with tools like DAX and begin to build unique data visualizations.

parts.title: Dashboard Build
parts.description: It's almost time to hand over the final deliverable. In this final chapter, you'll combine all of the job listing insights you've discovered into an interactive Power BI dashboard for the DataSearch team.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: This course requires learners to clean, manipulate, and merge real-world job posting data using Power Query, aligning with intermediate-level skills in handling and preparing data for analysis.

Learners build insightful visualizations and interactive dashboards in Power BI, demonstrating the ability to create complex visuals and communicate findings to stakeholders, which matches intermediate proficiency.

The course focuses on extracting business insights from job market data and presenting them to a fictional recruitment company, reflecting the intermediate level of aligning data analysis with business objectives.

Learners synthesize and present findings in a dashboard format for a business audience, requiring clear organization and adaptation of communication for stakeholders, which fits the intermediate level.

title: Manipulating Time Series Data in Python
description: In this course you'll learn the basics of manipulating time series data. Time series data are data that are indexed by a sequence of dates or times. You'll learn how to use methods built into Pandas to work with this index. You'll also learn how resample time series to change the frequency. This course will also show you how to calculate rolling and cumulative values for times series. Finally, you'll use all your new skills to build a value-weighted stock index from actual stock data.

parts.title: Working with Time Series in Pandas
parts.description: This chapter lays the foundations to leverage the powerful time series functionality made available by how Pandas represents dates, in particular by the DateTimeIndex. You will learn how to create and manipulate date information and time series, and how to do calculations with time-aware DataFrames to shift your data in time or create period-specific returns.

parts.title: Basic Time Series Metrics & Resampling
parts.description: This chapter dives deeper into the essential time series functionality made available through the pandas DataTimeIndex. It introduces resampling and how to compare different time series by normalizing their start points.

parts.title: Window Functions: Rolling & Expanding Metrics
parts.description: This chapter will show you how to use window function to calculate time series metrics for both rolling and expanding windows.

parts.title: Putting it all together: Building a value-weighted index
parts.description: This chapter combines the previous concepts by teaching you how to create a value-weighted index. This index uses market-cap data contained in the stock exchange listings to calculate weights and 2016 stock price information. Index performance is then compared against benchmarks to evaluate the performance of the index you created.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: The course covers combining, resampling, and transforming time series data using Pandas, which aligns with intermediate-level skills such as automating data cleaning tasks, processing structured data, and performing complex data manipulations.

The course teaches calculation of rolling, expanding, and cumulative metrics, and building a value-weighted index, which matches intermediate proficiency in applying statistical techniques like time series analysis and interpreting relationships between variables.

Learners use Python and Pandas to implement time series manipulations and calculations, which fits the intermediate level of designing and implementing functions and using libraries for data manipulation.

title: Intermediate Data Modeling in Power BI
description:
In this course, you'll extend your knowledge about facts, dimensions, and their relationships. You learn about the cardinality of relationships and how you can use bi-directional cross-filtering in your model.
You'll also explore the use of quick measures and hierarchies and write DAX to fully customize your data model. Finally, you'll get introduced to Power BI reporting best practices to improve the performance of your reports.

parts.title: Date Dimensions and Relationships
parts.description: In the first chapter, you'll extend your data modeling skills by adding more tables and relationships.

parts.title: Granularity, Measures, and Hierarchies
parts.description: You'll learn how to use hierarchies and explore several granularity levels of your data.

parts.title: Advanced Data Modeling
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll look at some advanced data modeling techniques. You'll learn how and when to use bi-directional cross filters and role-playing dimensions.

parts.title: Identifying Performance Problems
parts.description: In this final chapter, you'll study performance optimization tips and tricks in Power BI.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: The course covers intermediate data modeling concepts such as relationships, cardinality, hierarchies, and performance optimization in Power BI, aligning with the ability to combine datasets, automate cleaning tasks, and process structured data as expected at the intermediate level.

The course introduces Power BI reporting best practices and performance improvements, which matches the intermediate level's focus on creating complex visualizations and optimizing reports for specific audiences.

title: Introduction to Network Analysis in Python
description: From online social networks such as Facebook and Twitter to transportation networks such as bike sharing systems, networks are everywhere-and knowing how to analyze them will open up a new world of possibilities for you as a data scientist. This course will equip you with the skills to analyze, visualize, and make sense of networks. You'll apply the concepts you learn to real-world network data using the powerful NetworkX library. With the knowledge gained in this course, you'll develop your network thinking skills and be able to look at your data with a fresh perspective.

parts.title: Introduction to networks
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll be introduced to fundamental concepts in network analytics while exploring a real-world Twitter network dataset. You'll also learn about NetworkX, a library that allows you to manipulate, analyze, and model graph data. You'll learn about the different types of graphs and how to rationally visualize them.

parts.title: Important nodes
parts.description: You'll learn about ways to identify nodes that are important in a network. In doing so, you'll be introduced to more advanced concepts in network analysis as well as the basics of path-finding algorithms. The chapter concludes with a deep dive into the Twitter network dataset which will reinforce the concepts you've learned, such as degree centrality and betweenness centrality.

parts.title: Structures
parts.description: This chapter is all about finding interesting structures within network data. You'll learn about essential concepts such as cliques, communities, and subgraphs, which will leverage all of the skills you acquired in Chapter 2. By the end of this chapter, you'll be ready to apply the concepts you've learned to a real-world case study.

parts.title: Bringing it all together
parts.description: In this final chapter of the course, you'll consolidate everything you've learned through an in-depth case study of GitHub collaborator network data. This is a great example of real-world social network data, and your newly acquired skills will be fully tested. By the end of this chapter, you'll have developed your very own recommendation system to connect GitHub users who should collaborate together.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: The course covers network analysis concepts such as centrality, cliques, and communities, and applies them to real-world datasets, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on uncovering patterns in data, applying multivariate techniques, and interpreting relationships between variables.

Learners use Python and the NetworkX library to manipulate, analyze, and visualize network data, which matches the intermediate proficiency in designing and implementing functions and using libraries for data manipulation.

The course emphasizes visualizing different types of graphs and network structures, supporting the intermediate level's requirement to create complex visualizations and demonstrate trends and relationships in data.

title: Introduction to APIs in Python
description: Dive into the exciting world of APIs as we introduce you to the basics of consuming and working with Web APIs using Python. This course is designed to demystify the concepts and practical applications of APIs. It offers you a hands-on introduction where you'll learn how to interact with a REST API and integrate it into your applications or workflows. By the end of this course, you'll have a comprehensive understanding of APIs and the confidence to apply your knowledge in real-world scenarios.

parts.title: Making API Requests with Python
parts.description: This chapter introduces Web APIs, showing you how to make your first API requests with the requests Python package. You'll learn about the key components of an API request, HTTP verbs, and how to build URLs and send & receive data. We'll also cover headers and status codes, using a music catalog API for practical examples. By the end of this chapter you'll be able to confidently integrate a simple REST API with Python.

parts.title: More API request concepts
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn how to authenticate with APIs, covering different methods like Basic and API key authentication using the requests package. We'll then dive into working with structured data, focusing on requesting and handling JSON data. Finally, you'll master error handling, including how to manage errors with requests, understand error types, and respect API rate limits.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course introduces the basics of making API requests, handling authentication, and working with JSON data in Python, aligning with foundational programming skills such as using libraries, handling data, and correcting common errors.
Learners gain hands-on experience in retrieving and handling structured data (JSON) from APIs, which matches foundational data processing tasks like loading and preparing data for analysis.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning in Python
description:
Embark on a journey to empower machines through Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). This course offers hands-on experience with powerful algorithms using PyTorch and Gymnasium.
Start with DRL foundations and traditional Reinforcement Learning, then implement Deep Q-Networks (DQN) with advanced refinements like Prioritized Experience Replay.
Advance your skills with policy-based methods and explore industry-standard algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) before optimizing your models using Optuna.

parts.title: Introduction to Deep Reinforcement Learning
parts.description: Discover how deep reinforcement learning improves upon traditional Reinforcement Learning while studying and implementing your first Deep Q Learning algorithm.

parts.title: Deep Q-learning
parts.description: Dive into Deep Q-learning by implementing the original DQN algorithm, featuring Experience Replay, epsilon-greediness and fixed Q-targets. Beyond DQN, you will then explore two fascinating extensions that improve the performance and stability of Deep Q-learning:  Double DQN and Prioritized Experience Replay.

parts.title: Introduction to Policy Gradient Methods
parts.description: Learn about the foundational concepts of policy gradient methods found in DRL. You will begin with the policy gradient theorem, which forms the basis for these methods. Then, you will implement the REINFORCE algorithm, a powerful approach to learning policies. The chapter will then guide you through Actor-Critic methods, focusing on the Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) algorithm, which combines the strengths of both policy gradient and value-based methods to enhance learning efficiency and stability.

parts.title: Proximal Policy Optimization and DRL Tips
parts.description: Explore Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for robust DRL performance. Next, you will examine using an entropy bonus in PPO, which encourages exploration by preventing premature convergence to deterministic policies. You'll also learn about batch updates in policy gradient methods. Finally, you will learn about hyperparameter optimization with Optuna, a powerful tool for optimizing performance in your DRL models.

proficiency.DS: The course covers advanced deep reinforcement learning algorithms (DQN, Double DQN, Prioritized Experience Replay, PPO, Actor-Critic) and their implementation in PyTorch, aligning with the advanced proficiency level's focus on complex AI methodologies, production-ready solutions, and optimization techniques.

Hands-on implementation of sophisticated DRL algorithms in PyTorch requires advanced programming skills, including optimizing code and using advanced frameworks, matching the advanced proficiency level.

title: Extreme Gradient Boosting with XGBoost
description: Do you know the basics of supervised learning and want to use state-of-the-art models on real-world datasets? Gradient boosting is currently one of the most popular techniques for efficient modeling of tabular datasets of all sizes. XGboost is a very fast, scalable implementation of gradient boosting, with models using XGBoost regularly winning online data science competitions and being used at scale across different industries. In this course, you'll learn how to use this powerful library alongside pandas and scikit-learn to build and tune supervised learning models. You'll work with real-world datasets to solve classification and regression problems.

parts.title: Classification with XGBoost
parts.description: This chapter will introduce you to the fundamental idea behind XGBoost-boosted learners. Once you understand how XGBoost works, you'll apply it to solve a common classification problem found in industry: predicting whether a customer will stop being a customer at some point in the future.

parts.title: Regression with XGBoost
parts.description: After a brief review of supervised regression, you'll apply XGBoost to the regression task of predicting house prices in Ames, Iowa. You'll learn about the two kinds of base learners that XGboost can use as its weak learners, and review how to evaluate the quality of your regression models.

parts.title: Fine-tuning your XGBoost model
parts.description: This chapter will teach you how to make your XGBoost models as performant as possible. You'll learn about the variety of parameters that can be adjusted to alter the behavior of XGBoost and how to tune them efficiently so that you can supercharge the performance of your models.

parts.title: Using XGBoost in pipelines
parts.description: Take your XGBoost skills to the next level by incorporating your models into two end-to-end machine learning pipelines. You'll learn how to tune the most important XGBoost hyperparameters efficiently within a pipeline, and get an introduction to some more advanced preprocessing techniques.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced machine learning techniques, focusing on XGBoost-a state-of-the-art gradient boosting algorithm. It teaches model tuning, integration into pipelines, and solving real-world classification and regression problems, aligning with the advanced proficiency level's emphasis on applying complex methodologies and building production-ready solutions.

Learners use Python and libraries like pandas and scikit-learn to build, tune, and integrate XGBoost models into pipelines, demonstrating advanced programming skills such as optimizing code, using advanced frameworks, and implementing best practices in machine learning workflows.

The course requires understanding and applying advanced statistical concepts for model evaluation and tuning, such as performance metrics and regression analysis, which matches the advanced level's focus on rigorous statistical techniques and interpreting complex model outputs.

title: Sampling in R
description: Sampling is a cornerstone of inference statistics and hypothesis testing. It's tremendously important in survey analysis and experimental design. This course explains when and why sampling is important, teaches you how to perform common types of sampling, from simple random sampling to more complex methods like stratified and cluster sampling. Later, the course covers estimating population statistics, and quantifying uncertainty in your estimates by generating sampling distributions and bootstrap distributions. Throughout the course, you'll explore real-world datasets on coffee ratings, Spotify songs, and employee attrition.

parts.title: Introduction to Sampling
parts.description: Learn what sampling is and why it is useful, understand the problems caused by convenience sampling, and learn about the differences between true randomness and pseudo-randomness.

parts.title: Sampling Methods
parts.description: Learn how to and when to perform the four methods of random sampling: simple, systematic, stratified, and cluster.

parts.title: Sampling Distributions
parts.description: Learn how to quantify the accuracy of sample statistics using relative errors, and measure variation in your estimates by generating sampling distributions.

parts.title: Bootstrap Distributions
parts.description: Learn how to use resampling to perform bootstrapping, used to estimate variation in an unknown population. Understand the difference between sampling distributions and bootstrap distributions.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: Covers fundamental statistical concepts such as sampling, randomness, and basic estimation, which align with foundational proficiency in understanding and applying core statistical methods.

Teaches application of various sampling methods, estimation of population statistics, and quantifying uncertainty, which matches intermediate proficiency in applying inferential statistics and understanding when to use different statistical techniques.

title: HR Analytics: Exploring Employee Data in R
description: HR analytics, people analytics, workforce analytics -- whatever you call it, businesses are increasingly counting on their human resources departments to answer questions, provide insights, and make recommendations using data about their employees. In this course, you'll learn how to manipulate, visualize, and perform statistical tests on HR data through a series of HR analytics case studies.

parts.title: Identifying the best recruiting source
parts.description: In this chapter, you will get an introduction to how data science is used in a human resources context. Then you will dive into a case study where you'll analyze and visualize recruiting data to determine which source of new candidates ultimately produces the best new hires. The dataset you'll use in this and the other chapters in this course is synthetic, to maintain the privacy of actual employees.

parts.title: What is driving low employee engagement?
parts.description: Gallup defines engaged employees as those who are involved in, enthusiastic about and committed to their work and workplace.  There is disagreement about the strength of the connection between employee engagement and business outcomes, but the idea is that employees that are more engaged will be more productive and stay with the organization longer. In this chapter, you'll  look into potential reasons that one department's engagement scores are lower than the rest.

parts.title: Are new hires getting paid too much?
parts.description: When employers make a new hire, they must determine what the new employee will be paid. If the employer is not careful, the new hires can come in with a higher salary than the employees that currently work at the same job, which can cause  employee turnover and dissatisfaction. In this chapter, you will check whether new hires are really getting paid more than current employees, and how to double-check your initial observations.

parts.title: Are performance ratings being given consistently?
parts.description: Performance management helps an organization keep track of which employees are providing extra value, or below-average value, and compensating them accordingly. Whether performance is a rating or the result of a questionnaire, whether employees are rated each year or more often than that, the process is somewhat subjective. An organization should check that ratings are being given with regard to performance, and not individual managers' preferences, or even biases (conscious or subconscious).

parts.title: Improving employee safety with data
parts.description: In many industries, workplace safety is a critical consideration. Maintaining a safe workplace provides employees with confidence and reduces costs for workers' compensation and legal liabilities. In this chapter, you'll look for  explanations for an increase in workplace accidents.

proficiency.DS: The course teaches data manipulation and cleaning in R through HR case studies, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on automating and processing structured data for analysis.
Learners perform statistical tests and interpret results in HR contexts, matching the intermediate proficiency of applying inferential statistics and regression to real-world data.

The course emphasizes visualizing HR data to uncover trends and support business decisions, fitting the intermediate level's requirement for creating complex visualizations and linking insights to business objectives.
Case studies focus on HR business questions (recruitment, engagement, compensation), requiring learners to align data analysis with business objectives and communicate findings to stakeholders.

title: ChIP-seq with Bioconductor in R
description: ChIP-seq analysis is an important branch of bioinformatics. It provides a window into the machinery that makes the cells in our bodies tick. Whether it is a brain cell helping you to read this web page or an immune cell patrolling your body for microorganisms that would make you sick, they all carry the same genome. What differentiates them are the genes that are active at any given time. Which genes these are is determined by a complex system of proteins that can activate and deactivate genes. When this regulatory machinery gets out of control, it can lead to cancer and other debilitating diseases. ChIP-seq analysis allows us to understand the function of regulatory proteins, how they can contribute to disease and can provide insights into how we may be able to intervene to prevent cells from spinning out of control. In this course, you will explore a real dataset while learning how to process and analyze ChIP-seq data in R.

parts.title: Introduction to ChIP-seq
parts.description: Introduction to ChIP-seq experiments. Why are they interesting? What sort of phenomena can be studied with ChIP-seq and what can we learn from these experiments.

parts.title: Back to Basics - Preparing ChIP-seq data
parts.description: Now the ChIP-seq analysis begins in earnest. This chapter introduces Bioconductor tools to import and clean the data.

parts.title: Comparing ChIP-seq samples
parts.description: This chapter introduces techniques to identify and visualise differences between ChIP-seq samples.

parts.title: From Peaks to Genes to Function
parts.description: Being able to identify differential binding between groups of samples is great, but what does it mean?  This chapter discusses strategies to interpret differential binding results to go from peak calls to biologically meaningful insights.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: The course covers importing, cleaning, and processing ChIP-seq data using Bioconductor in R, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on automating data cleaning and handling structured biological datasets.

Learners analyze and interpret differences between ChIP-seq samples, applying statistical techniques to uncover patterns and draw biological conclusions, which matches the intermediate proficiency in applying inferential statistics and interpreting multivariate data.

The course requires using R and Bioconductor libraries for data manipulation and analysis, consistent with intermediate-level programming skills such as implementing functions and using specialized libraries for data science tasks.

The course includes visualizing differences between ChIP-seq samples, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in creating complex visualizations to demonstrate trends and correlations in biological data.

title: Conquering Data Bias
description:
Learn to capture the full potential of your data by identifying and mitigating data bias, which is crucial for precise analysis and robust model development.

Begin by exploring various forms of data bias and their impact on decision-making. Delve into data collection to uncover hidden biases within sampling methods, historical data, and measurement tools. Then, switch to data analysis and model development, learning how cognitive, reporting and algorithmic biases can distort interpretations. The course provides you with the knowledge and tools to detect and mitigate these biases, ensuring transparent and fair analysis practices.

By the end, you'll be a data bias expert, ready to conquer bias and uncover true insights within your datasets.

parts.title: Understanding data bias
parts.description: Discover the essence of data bias! Explore its impact on decision-making, unraveling its various forms from collection to analysis. Dive into cognitive and systemic biases, equipping yourself to navigate the complex landscape of bias in data.

parts.title: Bias in data collection
parts.description: Delve into the complexities of bias in data collection! From selection and historical bias to measurement bias, uncover the nuances shaping data interpretation. Discover strategies to identify and mitigate biases, ensuring the integrity of your datasets.

parts.title: Bias in data analysis
parts.description: Navigate the intricate world of bias in data analysis. Understand how cognitive biases like confirmation and anchoring affect result interpretation, and learn about the pervasive issue of reporting bias. Delve into the realm of algorithmic bias, exploring how it can seep into models and impact outcomes. Finally, master techniques to detect and mitigate bias, ensuring transparency and fairness in your data analysis practices.

proficiency.DS: This course addresses the identification and mitigation of various data biases during collection and analysis, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on evaluating data for bias, ensuring fairness, and applying best practices to mitigate discrimination in AI.
The course covers algorithmic bias and its impact on model outcomes, matching the intermediate proficiency's emphasis on recognizing ethical implications, bias reduction, and trust in AI design.

proficiency.SA: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
proficiency.DS: By teaching how to detect and mitigate bias for transparent and fair analysis, the course supports the intermediate level's requirements to evaluate data and models for bias, ensure fairness, and use best practices to mitigate discrimination.

title: Responsible AI Data Management
description: Handling data responsibly is critical, particularly in Artificial Intelligence (AI). This conceptual course will teach you the fundamentals of responsible data practices, including data acquisition, key regulations, and data validation and bias mitigation strategies. You can apply these skills to use critical thinking on any data project, ensuring you have a successful, responsible, and compliant project from start to finish.

parts.title: Introduction to Responsible AI Data Management
parts.description: Learn about the fundamental theory behind responsible data management in AI. You'll review key dimensions such as security, transparency, fairness, and more before conceptualizing the metrics and challenges associated with these dimensions and understanding how to balance responsible AI with other business and technical requirements.

parts.title: Regulation Compliance and Licensing
parts.description: Data regulation is essential to the legality of any AI project. Learn about key regulations, third-party licenses, and compliance strategies for informed consent and data-sharing agreements (with legal counsel). Finally, you'll learn about developing robust data governance strategies and management plans to ensure your project remains compliant throughout its lifecycle.

parts.title: Data Acquisition
parts.description: Navigate through the responsible selection and integration of data sources by understanding the importance of data origin, nature, and temporality, emphasizing legal compliance, diversity, and fairness. By exploring types of bias and their origins, you'll look at data fairness and representation to create a comprehensive dataset for modeling.

parts.title: Data Validation and Bias Mitigation Strategies
parts.description: Understand data audits, data validation, and bias mitigation. Data pre-processing and catching bias in modeling do not sound like fun, but let's streamline them with common approaches and trusted techniques!

proficiency.DS: The course covers responsible data acquisition, validation, and governance, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on combining datasets, automating cleaning, and ensuring compliance with regulations and ethical standards.

Emphasizes bias mitigation, fairness, and responsible data practices in AI, which matches the intermediate proficiency's requirements for recognizing ethical implications, applying fairness, and using validation techniques in AI projects.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Legal, Policy and Ethical Frameworks
proficiency.DS: Addresses regulation compliance, licensing, and data governance, directly supporting the intermediate level's need to comply with data sovereignty and consult government policy documents.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Responsible and Ethical AI Use
proficiency.DS: Focuses on responsible AI, bias mitigation, and compliance, which aligns with the intermediate level's emphasis on communicating risks and using tools like the Algorithmic Impact Assessment.

title: Introduction to Financial Concepts in Python
description: Understanding the basic principles of finance is essential for making important financial decisions ranging from taking out a student loan to constructing an investment portfolio. Combining basic financial knowledge with Python will allow you to construct some very powerful tools. You'll come out of this course understanding the time value of money, how to compare potential projects and how to make rational, data-driven financial decisions.

parts.title: The Time Value of Money
parts.description: Learn about fundamental financial concepts like the time value of money, growth and rate of return, discount factors, depreciation, and inflation.

parts.title: Making Data-Driven Financial Decisions
parts.description: In this chapter, you will act as the CEO of a company, making important data-driven financial decisions about projects and financing using measures such as IRR and NPV.

parts.title: Simulating a Mortgage Loan
parts.description: You just got married, and you're looking for a new home in Hoboken, New Jersey. You will build a mortgage payment simulator to estimate your mortgage payments and analyze different possible economic scenarios.

parts.title: Budgeting Application
parts.description: You just got a new job as a data scientist in San Francisco, and you're looking for an apartment. In this chapter, you'll be building your own budgeting application to plan out your financial future.

topic.name: Applied Finance
topic.description: The finance community has been one of the eager to embrace data science. From stock market predictions, to asset pricing and calculating the probability of loan defaults, the applications are nearly endless!

proficiency.DS: This course introduces fundamental financial concepts and demonstrates their application to real-world decisions using Python, aligning with foundational business acumen requirements such as understanding key financial metrics and making data-driven decisions relevant to business stakeholders.
Learners use Python to build simple financial tools and simulators, matching the foundational programming level where basic data manipulation and scripting are applied to practical problems.

title: Defensive R Programming
description: Writing R scripts is easy. Writing good R code is hard. In this course, we'll discuss defensive programming - a set of standard techniques that will help reduce bugs and aid working in teams. We examine techniques for avoiding common errors and also how to handle the inevitable error that arises in our code. The course will conclude looking at when to make the transition from script to project to package.

parts.title: Avoiding Conflict
parts.description: In this first chapter, you'll learn what defensive programming is,  and how to use existing packages for increased efficiency. You will then learn to manage the packages loaded in your environment and the potential conflicts that may arise.

parts.title: Early warning systems
parts.description: Programming is simpler when you get feedback on your code execution. In R, we use messages, warnings and errors to signal to keep the user informed. This chapter will discuss when and where you should use these communication tools.

parts.title: Preparing your defenses
parts.description: We can avoid making mistakes using a consistent programming approach. In this chapter, we will introduce you to R best practices.

parts.title: Creating a Battle Plan
parts.description: Creating a script is nice, but working on a project with several scripts and assets requires structure. This final chapter will teach you good organization practices, so you can go from script to package with an optimal workflow.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: The course covers defensive programming, error handling, best practices, and transitioning from scripts to packages in R, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on designing functions, implementing quality assurance, and managing code for collaborative work.

The course addresses organizing code, managing packages, and structuring projects, which matches the intermediate level's emphasis on repository organization, documentation, and collaborative coding practices.

title: Intermediate Object-Oriented Programming in Python
description:
Ready to unlock the power of object-oriented programming? You're in the right place! In this course, you'll build on the foundations of object-oriented programming to develop and hone the skills you need to write robust, production-ready code with Python.

Apply the basic principles of inheritance to create classes that inherit functionality from more than a single parent. Unlock a new array of capabilities with method overloading to create your own implementations of built-in operators, enabling your classes to be used in new and exciting ways.

Take your skills to the next-level with type hinting, and watch as your code becomes easier to read, write, and troubleshoot. Customize the way an attribute is set, accessed, and deleted using descriptors and other Python-native techniques. Learn to build your own custom iterators to navigate a collection or generate a stream of data.

Discover the power of abstract base classes, and how they can be used to create "blueprints" for similar classes. Practice building formal and informal interfaces to create and implement contracts between classes. Finally, wrap up the course by architecting and building classes using the factory method design pattern.

parts.title: Overloading and Multiple Inheritance
parts.description: Recall the fundamentals of object-oriented programming, and unlock the functionality of Python operators using overloading. Design and build classes that implement multiple and multilevel inheritance.

parts.title: Custom Class Features and Type Hints
parts.description: Level-up your Python skills with type hinting. Practice creating magic methods to handle attempts to access an attribute outside an object's namespace, or customize how an attribute is set. Build descriptors to control the way an attribute is stored, retrieved or deleted, and create your own custom iterators to traverse a collection of objects or a data stream.

parts.title: Object-oriented design patterns
parts.description: Learn to build "blueprints" for Python classes using abstract base classes. Explore how interfaces create contracts to be fulfilled by other classes. Leverage interfaces and build classes using the  factory method design pattern.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers intermediate object-oriented programming concepts in Python, including inheritance, method overloading, type hinting, descriptors, custom iterators, and design patterns. These skills align with the intermediate proficiency level, which expects the ability to design and implement functions and classes, apply object-oriented principles, and use advanced features of Python for robust code development.

The course introduces advanced programming constructs such as multiple inheritance, abstract base classes, design patterns (factory method), and custom iterators, which are relevant for the advanced proficiency level. This level requires implementing advanced data structures, optimizing code, and applying software engineering best practices.

title: Case Study: Inventory Analysis in Tableau
description:
You'll analyze a dataset from a fictitious company named Acropolis Retail Inc. Many retailers want to investigate possible improvements in inventory management and purchases, but they need some help. Here is where you come to the rescue. But as you will see, in a real-world case, not everything is perfect.

You will start by cleaning and exploring the data to verify everything makes sense. Next, you'll create calculated fields and ensure there is the appropriate level of detail for analyzing the clean information to obtain focused insights. Finally, you'll finish by creating attractive, informative visualizations and dashboards.

By the time you're finished, you'll be more confident performing an inventory analysis using Tableau.

parts.title: Exploratory Analysis
parts.description: In this first chapter, you will prepare and explore your new dataset in Tableau to set things up for your inventory analysis. Of course, as with a real-world dataset, things might not be perfect, so you should keep your eyes open to check your data is in order and that all required variables for analysis are readily available.

parts.title: Inventory Analysis
parts.description: Here, you will continue developing more interesting metrics and methods for inventory analysis in Tableau, such as inventory turnover and ABC analysis, to help you investigate which items are best for Acropolis Retail Inc.

parts.title: Reporting Inventory Analytics
parts.description: In the final chapter, it's time to start creating dashboards to share information with suitable applications on management practices, such as assisting in purchase decisions to improve stock management efficiently.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: The course involves cleaning and exploring real-world data, handling imperfect datasets, and preparing data for analysis, which aligns with intermediate-level data processing skills.
The course covers creating calculated fields, informative visualizations, and dashboards in Tableau, matching the intermediate proficiency in data visualization.
The course includes reporting analytics and sharing dashboards to inform management decisions, which fits intermediate technical communication by organizing insights for stakeholders.
The focus on inventory analysis and supporting purchase decisions demonstrates the application of data insights to business operations, aligning with intermediate business acumen.

title: Feature Engineering for Machine Learning in Python
description: Every day you read about the amazing breakthroughs in how the newest applications of machine learning are changing the world. Often this reporting glosses over the fact that a huge amount of data munging and feature engineering must be done before any of these fancy models can be used. In this course, you will learn how to do just that. You will work with Stack Overflow Developers survey, and historic US presidential inauguration addresses, to understand how best to preprocess and engineer features from categorical, continuous, and unstructured data. This course will give you hands-on experience on how to prepare any data for your own machine learning models.

parts.title: Creating Features
parts.description: In this chapter, you will explore what feature engineering is and how to get started with applying it to real-world data. You will load, explore and visualize a survey response dataset, and in doing so you will learn about its underlying data types and why they have an influence on how you should engineer your features. Using the pandas package you will create new features from both categorical and continuous columns.

parts.title: Dealing with Messy Data
parts.description: This chapter introduces you to the reality of messy and incomplete data. You will learn how to find where your data has missing values and explore multiple approaches on how to deal with them. You will also use string manipulation techniques to deal with unwanted characters in your dataset.

parts.title: Conforming to Statistical Assumptions
parts.description: In this chapter, you will focus on analyzing the underlying distribution of your data and whether it will impact your machine learning pipeline. You will learn how to deal with skewed data and situations where outliers may be negatively impacting your analysis.

parts.title: Dealing with Text Data
parts.description: Finally, in this chapter, you will work with unstructured text data, understanding ways in which you can engineer columnar features out of a text corpus. You will compare how different approaches may impact how much context is being extracted from a text, and how to balance the need for context, without too many features being created.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course covers combining, cleaning, transforming, and engineering features from various data types (categorical, continuous, unstructured), which aligns with intermediate-level data processing tasks such as automating cleaning, handling missing data, and preparing data for analysis.

Learners analyze data distributions, address skewness and outliers, and conform to statistical assumptions, which matches the intermediate proficiency in applying statistical analysis and understanding when to use specific techniques.
