The course uses Python and pandas for data manipulation, feature creation, and string processing, aligning with intermediate programming skills in implementing data transformations and using libraries for data tasks.
The course prepares data for machine learning models and introduces basic feature engineering, which is foundational for applying machine learning algorithms.

title: Case Study: Exploratory Data Analysis in R
description: Once you've started learning tools for data manipulation and visualization like dplyr and ggplot2, this course gives you a chance to use them in action on a real dataset. You'll explore the historical voting of the United Nations General Assembly, including analyzing differences in voting between countries, across time, and among international issues. In the process you'll gain more practice with the dplyr and ggplot2 packages, learn about the broom package for tidying model output, and experience the kind of start-to-finish exploratory analysis common in data science.

parts.title: Data cleaning and summarizing with dplyr
parts.description: The best way to learn data wrangling skills is to apply them to a specific case study. Here you'll learn how to clean and filter the United Nations voting dataset using the dplyr package, and how to summarize it into smaller, interpretable units.

parts.title: Data visualization with ggplot2
parts.description: Once you've cleaned and summarized data, you'll want to visualize them to understand trends and extract insights. Here you'll use the ggplot2 package to explore trends in United Nations voting within each country over time.

parts.title: Tidy modeling with broom
parts.description: While visualization helps you understand one country at a time, statistical modeling lets you quantify trends across many countries and interpret them together. Here you'll learn to use the tidyr, purrr, and broom packages to fit linear models to each country, and understand and compare their outputs.

parts.title: Joining and tidying
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn to combine multiple related datasets, such as incorporating information about each resolution's topic into your vote analysis. You'll also learn how to turn untidy data into tidy data, and see how tidy data can guide your exploration of topics and countries over time.

proficiency.DS: The course covers data cleaning, filtering, summarizing, and joining datasets using dplyr, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in handling and preparing data from multiple sources for analysis.

Learners practice using R and its libraries (dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr, purrr, broom) for data manipulation, visualization, and modeling, matching the intermediate level of implementing functions and using libraries for data tasks.
The course emphasizes using ggplot2 for creating visualizations to explore trends and insights, which fits the intermediate level of creating complex visualizations and interpreting trends.
The course introduces fitting and interpreting linear models across groups, matching the intermediate level of applying and interpreting regression and basic multivariate techniques.

title: Hierarchical and Recursive Queries in SQL Server
description: Do you want to query complex data structures in an iterative way? Do you have access to hierarchical data structures that need to be queried? This course will teach you the tools required to solve these questions. You will learn how to write recursive queries and query hierarchical data structures. To do this, you will use Common Table Expressions (CTE) and the recursion principle on a wide variety of datasets. You will, for example, dig into a flight plan dataset and learn how to find the best and cheapest connection between two airports. After completing this course, you will understand the principle of recursion, and be able to identify and create hierarchical data models.

parts.title: Recursion and Common Table Expression (CTE)
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn about recursion and why it is beneficial to apply this technique.  You will also refresh your knowledge about Common Expression Tables (CTE).

parts.title: Hierarchical and Recursive Queries
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn about recursive CTEs,  how to query hierarchical datasets,  and finally, how to apply recursive CTEs on hierarchical data.

parts.title: Creating Data Models on Your Own
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn how to create and modify database tables. You will learn about relational and hierarchical data models, how they differ, and when each model should be used.

parts.title: Hierarchical Queries of Real-World Examples
parts.description: In this chapter, you will practice your learnings about hierarchical and recursive querying on real-world problems, such as finding possible flight routes, assembling a car, and modeling a power grid.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: The course covers recursive queries, Common Table Expressions (CTEs), and hierarchical data models, which align with intermediate-level programming skills such as implementing advanced data manipulation and understanding complex data structures.

Learners practice querying and modeling hierarchical datasets, automating data extraction and transformation, and working with complex data structures, which matches intermediate data processing competencies.

title: Working with Llama 3
description: Open-source LLMs like Llama can be hosted locally on consumer-grade hardware, enhancing data privacy and reducing costs. Explore the techniques to enable this in this Llama course. Use the model locally, fine-tune it for domain-specific problems with Hugging Face libraries, and integrate it with LangChain to build AI-powered application. Finally, run the model more efficiently using compression techniques. This course is designed for learners with some experience in Hugging Face's transformers library and familiarity with LLM concepts such as fine-tuning and prompting.

parts.title: Understanding LLMs and Llama
parts.description: The field of large language models has exploded, and Llama is a standout. With Llama 3, possibilities have soared. Explore how it was built, learn to use it with llama-cpp-python, and understand how to craft precise prompts to control the model's behavior.

parts.title: Using Llama Locally
parts.description: Language models are often useful as agents, and in this Chapter, you'll explore how you can leverage llama-cpp-python's capabilities for local text generation and creating agents with personalities. You'll also learn about decoding parameters' impact on output quality. Finally, you'll build specialized inference classes for diverse text generation tasks.

parts.title: Finetuning Llama for Customer Service using Hugging Face & Bitext Dataset
parts.description: Language models are powerful, and you can unlock their full potential with the right techniques. Learn how fine-tuning can significantly improve the performance of smaller models for specific tasks. Dive into fine-tuning smaller Llama models to enhance their task-specific capabilities. Next, discover parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques such as LoRA, and explore quantization to load and use even larger models.

parts.title: Creating a Customer Service Chatbot with Llama and LangChain
parts.description: LLMs work best when they solve a real-world problem, such as creating a customer service chatbot using Llama and LangChain. Explore how to customize LangChain, integrate fine-tuned models, and craft templates for a real-world use case, utilizing RAG to enhance your chatbot's intelligence and accuracy. This chapter equips you with the technical skills to develop responsive and specialized chatbots.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced AI skills such as local deployment of LLMs, fine-tuning with Hugging Face, parameter-efficient tuning (LoRA), quantization, and integration with LangChain for real-world applications, aligning with advanced proficiency in AI techniques.

Learners implement and optimize code for deploying and fine-tuning LLMs, use advanced frameworks (Hugging Face, LangChain), and apply efficiency techniques like quantization and compression, matching advanced programming competency.

title: Natural Language Processing with spaCy
description: Learn spaCy, the fast-growing industry-standard NLP library, for tasks like tokenization, parsing, and named entity recognition. Master core operations, use classes like Doc and Token, and train models. Extract terms with pattern matching, create custom pipeline components, and handle real-world examples for your NLP projects.

parts.title: Introduction to NLP and spaCy
parts.description: This chapter will introduce you to NLP, some of its use cases such as named-entity recognition and AI-powered chatbots. You'll learn how to use the powerful spaCy library to perform various natural language processing tasks such as tokenization, sentence segmentation, POS tagging, and named entity recognition.

parts.title: spaCy Linguistic Annotations and Word Vectors
parts.description: Learn about linguistic features, word vectors, semantic similarity, analogies, and word vector operations. In this chapter you'll discover how to use spaCy to extract word vectors, categorize texts that are relevant to a given topic and find semantically similar terms to given words from a corpus or from a spaCy model vocabulary.

parts.title: Data Analysis with spaCy
parts.description: Get familiar with spaCy pipeline components, how to add a pipeline component, and analyze the NLP pipeline. You will also learn about multiple approaches for rule-based information extraction using EntityRuler, Matcher, and PhraseMatcher classes in spaCy and RegEx Python package.

parts.title: Customizing spaCy Models
parts.description: Explore multiple real-world use cases where spaCy models may fail and learn how to train them further to improve model performance. You'll be introduced to spaCy training steps and understand how to train an existing spaCy model or from scratch, and evaluate the model at the inference time.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course covers practical NLP tasks such as named entity recognition, tokenization, and model fine-tuning using spaCy, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on applying AI techniques to real-world problems, developing AI-powered solutions, and evaluating model performance.

Learners use Python and spaCy libraries to manipulate data, implement NLP pipelines, and customize models, matching the intermediate proficiency in designing and implementing functions, using libraries for data manipulation, and automating tasks.

The course teaches extracting, transforming, and analyzing text data, including rule-based information extraction and pipeline customization, which fits the intermediate level's requirements for processing structured and unstructured data and automating data cleaning.

title: Data-Driven Decision Making in SQL
description: In this course, you will learn how to use SQL to support decision making. It is based on a case study about an online movie rental company with a database about customer information, movie ratings, background information on actors and more. You will learn to apply SQL queries to study for example customer preferences, customer engagement, and sales development. This course also covers SQL extensions for online analytical processing (OLAP), which makes it easier to obtain key insights from multidimensional aggregated data.

parts.title: Introduction to business intelligence for a online movie rental database
parts.description: The first chapter is an introduction to the use case of an online movie rental company, called MovieNow and focuses on using simple SQL queries to extract and aggregated data from its database.

parts.title: Decision Making with simple SQL queries
parts.description: More complex queries with GROUP BY, LEFT JOIN and sub-queries are used to gain insight into customer preferences.

parts.title: Data Driven Decision Making with advanced SQL queries
parts.description: The concept of nested queries and correlated nested queries is introduced and the functions EXISTS and UNION  are used to categorize customers, movies, actors, and more.

parts.title: Data Driven Decision Making with OLAP SQL queries
parts.description: The OLAP extensions in SQL are introduced and applied to aggregated data on multiple levels.  These extensions are the CUBE, ROLLUP and GROUPING SETS operators.

proficiency.DS: The course covers SQL queries including GROUP BY, JOINs, sub-queries, and OLAP extensions, which align with the intermediate level's focus on data manipulation, automation, and use of advanced SQL features.
Learners automate data extraction, aggregation, and transformation using SQL, including combining datasets and handling complex queries, matching the intermediate proficiency in data processing.

The course applies SQL analysis to real business scenarios (customer preferences, sales), supporting data-driven business decisions, which fits the intermediate level's focus on aligning data projects with business objectives.

title: Introduction to Data Security
description: In today's data-driven world, the severity of data breaches and cyber threats is escalating. The explosion of generative AI has raised the stakes even higher. This course provides a comprehensive understanding of data security fundamentals. We'll also delve into the importance of cultivating a data security mindset, a crucial factor for success. Doing so will empower you to safeguard sensitive information and protect your organization's digital assets.

parts.title: The Power of Data Security
parts.description: The goal of this chapter is to set the groundwork for an understanding of what data security is. It gives a high-level overview of what it encompasses, emphasizes the importance of being compliant with relevant regulations, and outlines real-life consequences of data breaches.

parts.title: Data Fortress 101: A Beginner's Guide
parts.description: In this chapter, we start by covering a core concept of data security: understanding what sensitive data is. We then move through the various data security measures that create the elements of a comprehensive data security ecosystem.

parts.title: Data Security: Organization-wide Fortification
parts.description: This chapter aims to round out your understanding of data security by helping you know how to manage data security in real life.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces fundamental concepts of data security, compliance, and the importance of protecting sensitive information, aligning with foundational proficiency in understanding and applying basic data management and security measures.

proficiency.SA: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
proficiency.DS: The course emphasizes compliance with regulations and ethical handling of sensitive data, matching the foundational level's focus on adhering to legal, privacy, and ethical frameworks.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Legal, Policy and Ethical Frameworks
proficiency.DS: By highlighting compliance with regulations and the consequences of data breaches, the course fits the foundational level's requirement to consult and comply with relevant legal and policy standards.

title: Writing Functions and Stored Procedures in SQL Server
description: Take your SQL Server programming to the next level. First, we demystify how to manipulate datetime data by performing temporal exploratory data analysis with the Washington DC BikeShare transactional dataset. Then, you'll master how to create, update, and execute user-defined functions and stored procedures. You will learn the proper context for each modular programming tool and best practices. In the final chapter, you will apply all of your new skills to solve a real-world business case identifying the New York City yellow taxi utilization for each borough, and which pickup locations should be scheduled for each driver shift.

parts.title: Temporal EDA, Variables & Date Manipulation
parts.description: Learn how to do effective exploratory data analysis on temporal data, create scalar and table variables to store data, and learn how to execute date manipulation. This chapter will also cover the following SQL functions: DATEDIFF( ), DATENAME( ), DATEPART( ), CAST( ), CONVERT( ), GETDATE( ), and DATEADD( ).

parts.title: User Defined Functions
parts.description: This chapter will explain how to create, update, and execute user-defined functions (UDFs). You will learn about the various types of UDFs: scalar, inline, and multi-statement table-valued. You'll also learn best practices.

parts.title: Stored Procedures
parts.description: Learn how to create, update, and execute stored procedures. Investigate the differences between stored procedures and user defined functions, including appropriate scenarios for each.

parts.title: NYC Taxi Ride Case Study
parts.description: Apply your new skills in temporal EDA, user-defined functions, and stored procedures to solve a business case problem. Analyze the New York City taxi ride dataset to identify average fare per distance, ride count, and total ride time for each borough on each day of the week. And which pickup locations within the borough should be scheduled for each driver shift?

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: The course covers creating, updating, and executing user-defined functions and stored procedures, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in programming by applying modular programming principles and best practices in SQL.

The course involves temporal exploratory data analysis, date manipulation, and solving real-world business cases using SQL, matching the intermediate level of combining datasets, automating cleaning tasks, and performing complex data manipulations.

The final case study applies technical SQL skills to solve a real-world business problem (NYC taxi utilization), demonstrating the ability to align data analysis with business objectives at the intermediate level.

title: Marketing Analytics for Business
description: In this no-code course, you'll learn about the role of a Marketing Analyst and how they leverage data to better understand their customers and help companies grow. Through hands-on exercises, you'll learn how to answer the big questions like "did my campaign increase sales six months after launch?" You'll also work with real-world data to perform essential marketing analysis, including building customer segments, market response models, calculating customer lifetime value (LTV), and much more.

parts.title: Marketing Levers and Questions
parts.description: What does a marketing analyst do? Why is this role in high demand? In this chapter, you'll learn about roles and business questions that a marketing analyst encounters. From revenue impact to campaign insights-you'll find that marketers will never run out of problems to analyze.

parts.title: Marketing Data Challenges
parts.description: Marketing analytics is not for the faint of heart! Between numerous data sources and ever-increasing privacy legislation, marketing analysts must consider multiple factors in reporting. Add in measuring the indirect impact of marketing, and you'll see why marketing analysts get extremely comfortable with imperfect data.

parts.title: Marketing Campaign Analysis
parts.description: Now that you know more about the marketing analytics landscape, let's talk about how you can use it to assess campaign performance. To do this, you'll dive into text and sentiment analysis, audience segmentation, and predictive analytics. Marketers and executives rely on analytics to send the right message to the right people at the right time.

parts.title: Marketing ROI
parts.description: The big question every marketer asks is "did my marketing efforts make any money?" To answer that question you'll have to consider: seasonal patterns, business model, campaign goals, and ROI. Most importantly, you'll be responsible for setting and measuring KPIs to evaluate marketing effectiveness.

proficiency.DS: The course teaches how to align marketing analytics with business objectives, assess the impact of campaigns, and communicate findings to stakeholders, which matches the intermediate proficiency level for business acumen.

Learners perform marketing analysis such as customer segmentation, market response modeling, and calculating LTV, which involves applying inferential statistics and regression techniques, aligning with the intermediate level.

The course emphasizes communicating marketing insights and campaign effectiveness to business stakeholders, matching the intermediate level's focus on adapting communication for different audiences and linking findings to business objectives.

title: Understanding Machine Learning
description:
What's behind the machine learning hype? In this non-technical course, you'll learn everything you've been too afraid to ask about machine learning. There's no coding required. Hands-on exercises will help you get past the jargon and learn how this exciting technology powers everything from self-driving cars to your personal Amazon shopping suggestions.

How does machine learning work, when can you use it, and what is the difference between AI and machine learning? They're all covered. Gain skills in this hugely in-demand and influential field, and discover why machine learning is for everyone!

parts.title: What is Machine Learning?
parts.description: In this chapter,  we'll define machine learning and its relation to data science and artificial intelligence.  Then, we'll unpack important machine learning jargon and end with the machine learning workflow for building models.

parts.title: Machine Learning Models
parts.description: Now that you know the basics of machine learning, let's dive a little bit deeper. At the end of this chapter, you will know the different types of machine learning, as well as how to evaluate and improve your models.

parts.title: Deep Learning
parts.description: In this chapter, we'll unpack deep learning beginning with neural networks. Next, we'll take a closer look at two common use-cases for deep learning: computer vision and natural language processing. We'll wrap up the course discussing the limits and dangers of machine learning.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces the basics of machine learning, including key concepts, types of models, and the difference between AI and machine learning, all without requiring coding. It is well-suited for foundational proficiency as it focuses on understanding core ideas, terminology, and practical applications.

title: Intermediate ChatGPT
description: Elevate your ChatGPT expertise with 'Intermediate ChatGPT.' Designed for learners with a basic familiarity with ChatGPT and AI, this course simplifies complex concepts into understandable insights. It's perfect for those looking to deepen their knowledge without the technical minutiae. From exploring the architecture behind GPT models to mastering advanced prompt crafting and beyond, this course bridges the gap between introductory skills and advanced application, empowering you to unlock the full potential of ChatGPT for creative exploration.

parts.title: Understanding GPT Model Architecture
parts.description: Explore the fundamentals of ChatGPT's architecture, focusing on transformers, tokenization, and self-attention mechanisms. Learners will understand the evolution from GPT-1 to GPT-4, covering core components and training methods like pre-training, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), highlighting the advancements that revolutionized Natural Language Processing (NLP).

parts.title: Advanced prompt crafting
parts.description: Elevate your prompt crafting skills, focusing on advanced techniques for precision and creativity. Learners will practice negotiation scenarios using XML tags for clarity, enhancing their negotiation skills for seeking a raise. They will also explore methods for generating startup ideas with few-shot prompting and thinking tags. By the end, learners will craft high-quality, effective prompts for diverse applications.

parts.title: Advanced Functions of ChatGPT
parts.description: Explore the advanced functions of ChatGPT, starting with custom instructions to personalize interactions. Learners will explore the enhanced flexibility of building and deploying Custom GPTs for tailored solutions across various use cases. Finally, the chapter examines the future trajectory of ChatGPT, including potential advancements and ethical considerations in AI development as we progress towards artificial general intelligence (AGI).

proficiency.DS: This course covers intermediate-level AI concepts such as GPT model architecture, advanced prompt engineering, and fine-tuning, aligning with the proficiency level that expects learners to apply deep learning approaches, fine-tune models, and recognize ethical implications in AI.

The course emphasizes translating complex AI concepts into understandable insights and crafting effective prompts, which matches the intermediate level's focus on organizing insights, adapting communication for different audiences, and linking findings to business objectives.

title: Large Language Models (LLMs) Concepts
description: In this course, you'll journey through the world of Large Language Models (LLMs) and discover how they are reshaping the AI landscape. You'll see how they revolutionize businesses and everyday life with real-world examples and learn about their building block. As you progress, you'll gain insights into the training methodologies too. Finally, you'll tackle the critical ethical and environmental considerations for LLMs and see what the future of LLMs could look like. By the end of this course, you'll have a comprehensive understanding of LLMs, their capabilities, applications, and challenges.

parts.title: Introduction to Large Language Models (LLM)
parts.description: The AI landscape is evolving rapidly, and Large Language Models (LLMs) are at the forefront of this evolution. This chapter examines how LLMs are advancing the development of human-like artificial intelligence and transforming industries through their numerous applications. You will explore the challenges and complexity associated with language modeling.

parts.title: Building Blocks of LLMs
parts.description: This chapter emphasizes the novelty of LLMs and their emergent capabilities while outlining various NLP techniques for data preparation. You will learn the challenges of training LLMs and how fine-tuning can effectively address them. You will also understand how N-shot learning techniques enable efficient adaptation of pre-trained models when faced with limited labeled data.

parts.title: Training Methodology and Techniques
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn about the fundamental building blocks of training an LLM, such as pre-training techniques. You'll also gain an intuitive understanding of complex concepts like transformer architecture, including the attention mechanism. The chapter discusses an advanced fine-tuning technique and summarizes the training process to complete an LLM.

parts.title: Concerns and Considerations
parts.description: In this chapter, we delve into the key considerations when training LLMs, such as large data availability, data quality, accurate labeling, and the implications of biased data. You will also examine various LLM risks like data privacy, ethical concerns, and environmental impact. Lastly, the chapter concludes by discussing emerging research areas and the evolving landscape of LLMs.

proficiency.DS: The course covers LLM fundamentals, training methodologies, fine-tuning, and real-world applications, aligning with intermediate proficiency which expects understanding of deep learning, model fine-tuning, and ethical implications.

The course addresses advanced topics such as transformer architectures, attention mechanisms, advanced fine-tuning, and ethical/environmental risks, matching the advanced proficiency level's focus on complex AI methodologies and responsible deployment.

proficiency.SA: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
proficiency.DS: The course discusses ethical and privacy concerns, bias, and responsible AI use, which aligns with the intermediate level's emphasis on evaluating data/models for bias and ensuring fairness in AI outcomes.

proficiency.SA: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
proficiency.DS: By covering privacy, ethical risks, and environmental impact of LLMs, the course fits the advanced level's requirement to evaluate and advise on ethical, legal, and social implications of AI models.

title: Creating Dashboards in Tableau
description:
Dashboards are a must-have tool in today's data-driven world. By combining curated data visualizations, dashboards allow users to interpret and ask their own questions of data. By reducing the time to insight and empowering business analysts, dashboards can have a big impact on business performance.

Tableau's dashboarding abilities are powerful and easy to use. In this course, you'll learn to apply dashboard-composition best practices, add interactive or explanatory elements, and use dashboard actions to make your dashboard interactive. Additionally, you'll learn to modify an existing dashboard layout for mobile devices to share as an image or a PDF. Finally, you'll learn how to share your data story through Tableau's story functionality.

parts.title: Getting Started With Dashboards
parts.description: Learn the best practices to creating your own Tableau dashboard. You'll iteratively improve the dashboard with the use of dashboard objects like containers and dashboard actions, which add interactivity.

parts.title: Sharing Data Insights
parts.description: Get to know more about Tableau's story functionality and learn to share your data insights. You'll also learn to prepare dashboards for mobile layouts and share them in different file formats, like PDFs and images.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: This course covers dashboard composition best practices, interactivity, and sharing insights, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on creating complex visualizations and adapting communication for different audiences.

The course teaches how to share data stories and insights using Tableau's story functionality, matching the intermediate proficiency in organizing insights into clear narratives and adapting communication for stakeholders.

By focusing on dashboards that empower business analysts and impact business performance, the course supports foundational understanding of presenting data findings in simple, relevant terms for business stakeholders.

title: Foundations of Git
description:
This course introduces the concept of version control and highlights its benefits for software and data projects. You'll learn about Git, the popular software for implementing version control in projects, and use it to create repositories and track files.

Discover how Git stores data through blobs, trees, and commits. Use this information to compare the state of your project at different points in time, understanding what changes have been made, by who, and when. Learn valuable tips and tricks to customize your view of a repository's history and how to undo changes to revert files!

parts.title: Introduction to Git
parts.description: Learn the benefits and fundamentals of Git for version control in software and data projects.

parts.title: Version history
parts.description: Learn how to compare files at different points in time, and restore files to their previous state.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers the basics of version control with Git, including creating repositories, tracking files, viewing history, and reverting changes, which aligns with foundational proficiency in code management for data science projects.

title: Introduction to Functions in Python
description: It's time to push forward and develop your Python chops even further. Python has tons of fantastic functions and a module ecosystem. However, as a data professional or developer, you'll constantly need to write your own functions to solve problems that are dictated by your data. You will learn the art of function writing in this first course. You'll come out of this course being able to write your very own custom functions, complete with multiple parameters and multiple return values, along with default arguments and variable-length arguments. You'll gain insight into scoping in Python, be able to write lambda functions and handle errors in your function writing practice. You'll wrap up each chapter by using your new skills to write functions that analyze Twitter data.

parts.title: Writing your own functions
parts.description: You'll learn how to write simple functions, as well as functions that accept multiple arguments and return multiple values. You'll also have the opportunity to apply these new skills to questions commonly encountered by data professionals and developers.

parts.title: Default arguments, variable-length arguments and scope
parts.description: You'll learn to write functions with default arguments so that the user doesn't always need to specify them, and variable-length arguments so they can pass an arbitrary number of arguments on to your functions. You'll also learn about the essential concept of scope.

parts.title: Lambda functions and error-handling
parts.description: Learn about lambda functions, which allow you to write functions quickly and on the fly. You'll also practice handling errors in your functions, which is an essential skill. Then, apply your new skills to answer data science questions.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers writing custom functions, handling multiple parameters and return values, default and variable-length arguments, scoping, lambda functions, and error handling in Python-skills aligned with the intermediate proficiency level, which expects the ability to design and implement functions, apply object-oriented principles, and use libraries for data manipulation.

title: Advanced Deep Learning with Keras
description: This course shows you how to solve a variety of problems using the versatile Keras functional API. You will start with simple, multi-layer dense networks (also known as multi-layer perceptrons), and continue on to more complicated architectures. The course will cover how to build models with multiple inputs and a single output, as well as how to share weights between layers in a model. We will also cover advanced topics such as category embeddings and multiple-output networks. If you've ever wanted to train a network that does both classification and regression, then this course is for you!

parts.title: The Keras Functional API
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll become familiar with the basics of the Keras functional API.  You'll build a simple functional network using functional building blocks, fit it to data, and make predictions.

parts.title: Two Input Networks Using Categorical Embeddings, Shared Layers, and Merge Layers
parts.description: In this chapter, you will build two-input networks that use categorical embeddings to represent high-cardinality data, shared layers to specify re-usable building blocks, and merge layers to join multiple inputs to a single output. By the end of this chapter, you will have the foundational building blocks for designing neural networks with complex data flows.

parts.title: Multiple Inputs: 3 Inputs (and Beyond!)
parts.description: In this chapter, you will extend your 2-input model to 3 inputs, and learn how to use Keras' summary and plot functions to understand the parameters and topology of your neural networks. By the end of the chapter, you will understand how to extend a 2-input model to 3 inputs and beyond.

parts.title: Multiple Outputs
parts.description: In this chapter, you will build neural networks with multiple outputs, which can be used to solve regression problems with multiple targets.  You will also build a model that solves a regression problem and a classification problem simultaneously.

proficiency.DS: The course covers advanced deep learning architectures, including multi-input and multi-output networks, category embeddings, and simultaneous classification and regression tasks, aligning with advanced proficiency in designing and building production-ready AI solutions using complex methodologies.

Learners use the Keras functional API in Python to build and optimize complex neural network architectures, which matches the advanced level's focus on implementing advanced frameworks and optimizing code for performance.

title: Responsible AI Practices
description: Dive into Responsible AI with this course designed to help you implement ethical AI in your organization. You'll explore Responsible AI principles, their evolution, and practical applications through real-world case studies and interactive content. Learn to navigate risks like bias, privacy, and security, and understand global AI regulations. Gain strategies for fostering an ethical AI environment with tools for risk management and governance models. By the end, you'll be equipped to lead AI initiatives responsibly, making informed, ethical decisions. Ideal for both AI professionals and newcomers. Enrol now and shape the future responsibly.

parts.title: The foundations of Responsible AI
parts.description: Explore the defining moments and key principles of Responsible AI, from its historical roots to present applications. Discover how these principles differ and relate to AI Ethics through engaging case studies and real-life scenarios.

parts.title: Navigating AI risks and rules
parts.description: Unpack the complexities of AI risks and learn to evaluate their impact on society. Dive into global AI frameworks and regulations to avoid common pitfalls and ensure your AI strategies are robust and ethical.

parts.title: Building and safeguarding a RAI future
parts.description: Learn strategies for developing AI responsibly with a focus on inclusive teams and governance models. Apply practical tools and participatory design techniques to your AI projects to ensure they are ethical, effective, and aligned with global standards.

proficiency.DS: The course covers evaluating and mitigating ethical risks, understanding privacy and bias, and applying responsible AI frameworks, aligning with intermediate proficiency in ethical and legal standards for AI.
It addresses designing governance models, leading responsible AI initiatives, and mentoring others in ethical AI deployment, matching advanced proficiency in ethical leadership and guidance.

The course teaches practical application of responsible AI principles, risk management, and compliance with regulations, fitting the intermediate level focus on ethical implications and responsible use of AI.

It prepares learners to lead responsible AI initiatives, develop governance models, and ensure ethical deployment, which aligns with advanced proficiency in AI strategy and responsible implementation.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Responsible and Ethical AI Use
proficiency.DS: The course introduces responsible AI principles, compliance, and ethical frameworks, suitable for foundational understanding of responsible and ethical AI use.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Responsible and Ethical AI Use
proficiency.DS: It covers communicating risks, using assessment tools, and applying responsible AI practices, which are key at the intermediate proficiency level.

title: Understanding the EU AI Act
description: Act on Artificial Intelligence! This course explores the new EU AI Act. Learn risk-based approaches, provider/deployer obligations, and AI use cases. Understand AI risk categories and compliance, with examples in biometric AI, education, and general-purpose models. Gain essential knowledge to navigate and integrate AI safely and effectively in business.

parts.title: Introduction to the EU AI Act
parts.description: Explore the fundamentals of the EU AI Act, one of the most impactful digital regulations to date. This chapter unpacks the Act's purpose, scope, and risk-based framework, explaining its application across industries and its importance in ensuring safer AI technologies, enhancing trust, and driving societal and economic benefits.

parts.title: EU AI Act Obligations
parts.description: Delve into the distinction between AI systems and AI models under the EU AI Act. You will explore the obligations of general-purpose AI models, including documentation and transparency requirements. Understand the concept of systemic risk for powerful models and the additional responsibilities these entail, ensuring that AI deployment in Europe remains safe and human-centric.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Legal, Policy and Ethical Frameworks
proficiency.DS: The course covers compliance, obligations, and risk-based approaches under the EU AI Act, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on applying and understanding legal and ethical standards in AI.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Responsible and Ethical AI Use
proficiency.DS: By addressing risk categories, transparency, and safe deployment of AI, this course fits the intermediate proficiency in responsible and ethical AI use, emphasizing risk communication and compliance.
The course introduces core AI concepts, risk categories, and compliance frameworks, providing foundational knowledge for understanding AI regulation and its safe integration in business.

It teaches how to navigate and integrate AI safely and effectively in business, matching the intermediate level's emphasis on aligning AI solutions with business objectives and regulatory requirements.

title: Time Series Analysis in PostgreSQL
description: This course teaches you how to leverage PostgreSQL to handle date and time data. You'll learn about functions and calls to help you parse through and manipulate this data, make calculations, and use window functions. You'll apply these techniques to real-world data to analyze temperatures, look at train schedules, and review how the popularity of news articles can change over time.

parts.title: Introduction to Date and Time Data in PostgreSQL
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll be introduced to date and time data types. You'll learn how to convert text and numeric data to date and time format-and how to convert the other way around too!

parts.title: Working with Time Series
parts.description: It's time to get granular. In this chapter, you'll learn how to set the granularity of your time series reports. You'll then get to grips with adding, subtracting, and aggregating as you discover how to analyze time series data.

parts.title: Using Window Functions to Analyze Time Series Data
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll work with window functions. You'll begin learning about partitions and partitioning and how they work with window functions. You'll be able to find the top items when ranking your data.

parts.title: Calculating Running Totals and Moving Averages
parts.description: In the final chapter, you'll level up your skills by calculating the running total, running average, and even moving average to enhance your time series analysis.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: The course covers combining, aggregating, and transforming time series data in PostgreSQL, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in handling and automating complex data manipulations and transformations.
The course teaches calculation of running totals and moving averages, which are key statistical techniques for analyzing time series data at the intermediate level.

title: Generative AI for Business
description:
Firstly, you'll learn about generative AI and how it differs from traditional AI. You will dive deeper into the generative AI ecosystem and its key players: universities, governments, companies, and open-source communities. You'll discover the impact of the cloud and discuss various model breakthroughs. This will give you a better understanding of how we got to this huge technological breakthrough.

Consecutively, you'll learn how to use Generative AI to enhance workflows. You'll investigate how to use it through augmentation, co-creation, and replacement techniques. You'll discover generative AI's value to daily operations and strategic decisions. Finally, you'll dive into responsible AI and how to prepare and lead in a future with Generative AI through strategic alignment, change management and continuous improvement.

parts.title: Introduction to Generative AI
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn all about what generative AI is, and how it differs from traditional AI. You dive deeper into the generative AI ecosystem, its evolution, and how we got to this huge technological breakthrough.

parts.title: Generative AI Solutions
parts.description: In this chapter you'll learn how to use Generative AI to enhance workflows. You'll investigate how to use it through augmentation, co-creation and replacement techniques. Consecutively, you'll dive into responsible AI and how to prepare and lead in a future with Generative AI.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces generative AI concepts, differences from traditional AI, and foundational understanding of the generative AI ecosystem, aligning with foundational proficiency.

The course covers practical applications of generative AI in workflows, augmentation, co-creation, and responsible AI, matching intermediate-level skills in applying AI to real-world business problems and ethical considerations.

The course explores the value of generative AI in daily operations and strategic decisions, aligning with the intermediate level of assessing business impact and aligning AI solutions with business objectives.
The course addresses change management and strategic alignment for generative AI adoption, which fits the intermediate level of managing projects and adapting to new technologies.

title: Practicing Coding Interview Questions in Python
description: Coding interviews can be challenging. You might be asked questions to test your knowledge of a programming language. On the other side, you can be given a task to solve in order to check how you think. And when you are interviewed for a data scientist position, it's likely you can be asked on the corresponding tools available for the language. In either of the cases, to get a cool position as a data scientist, you need to do a little work to perform the best. That's why it's very important to practice in order to prove your expertise! This course serves as a guide for those who just start their path to become a professional data scientist and as a refresher for those who seek for other opportunities. We'll go through fundamental as well as advanced topics that aim to prepare you for a coding interview in Python. Since it is not a normal step-by-step course, some exercises can be quite complex. But who said that interviews are easy to pass, right?

parts.title: Python Data Structures and String Manipulation
parts.description: In this chapter, we'll refresh our knowledge of the main data structures used in Python.  We'll cover how to deal with lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries.  We'll also consider strings and how to write regular expressions to retrieve specific character sequences from a given text.

parts.title: Iterable objects and representatives
parts.description: This chapter focuses on iterable objects. We'll refresh the definition of iterable objects and explain, how to identify one.  Next, we'll cover list comprehensions, which is a very special feature of Python programming language to define lists.  Then, we'll recall how to combine several iterable objects into one. Finally, we'll cover how to create custom iterable objects using generators.

parts.title: Functions and lambda expressions
parts.description: This chapter will focus on the functional aspects of Python. We'll start by defining functions with a variable amount of positional as well as keyword arguments.  Next, we'll cover lambda functions and in which cases they can be helpful. Especially, we'll see how to use them with such functions as map(), filter(), and reduce(). Finally, we'll recall what is recursion and how to correctly implement one.

parts.title: Python for scientific computing
parts.description: This chapter will cover topics on scientific computing in Python. We'll start by explaining the difference between NumPy arrays and lists. We'll define why the former ones suit better for complex calculations. Next, we'll cover some useful techniques to manipulate with pandas DataFrames. Finally, we'll do some data visualization using scatterplots, histograms, and boxplots.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: The course covers basic Python data structures, string manipulation, functions, and lambda expressions, aligning with foundational programming skills such as using variables, loops, conditionals, and built-in data structures.

The inclusion of list comprehensions, generators, and functional programming concepts like map, filter, and reduce, as well as data manipulation with pandas and NumPy, matches intermediate proficiency in designing and implementing functions and using libraries for data manipulation.

The course presents complex exercises and advanced topics such as custom iterable objects, recursion, and scientific computing with NumPy and pandas, which are relevant for advanced proficiency involving optimization and advanced data structures.
The course introduces basic data visualization techniques using scatterplots, histograms, and boxplots, which aligns with foundational skills in presenting data using basic charts and graphs.

title: Understanding Prompt Engineering
description: Embark on an immersive journey to master ChatGPT, the groundbreaking conversational language model, and revolutionize your business and creative processes. This comprehensive course covers the essentials of prompt engineering, teaching you to construct clear, specific, and open-ended prompts, and advances into sophisticated techniques like zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot learning. Furthermore, you'll develop skills to evaluate ChatGPT's responses, ensuring accuracy and relevance critically. This all-encompassing course is your gateway to unlocking the full potential of ChatGPT, enhancing your workflow, and staying ahead in the world of generative AI.

parts.title: Prompting unveiled
parts.description: Embark on an introductory journey with prompt engineering, unraveling the essence of prompts and glimpsing future techniques, all while crafting real-world applications.

parts.title: Prompting Strategies and Techniques
parts.description: Explore the art of prompt engineering with ChatGPT. Dive into prompt structure essentials, understand output control techniques, and hone your ability to evaluate model responses. From crafting efficient prompts to using spacing and punctuation for clarity, master the nuances of effective language model interactions.

parts.title: Advanced Prompt Engineering
parts.description: Explore advanced techniques to enhance your interactions with ChatGPT, like zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot learning, and navigate around model limitations such as biases and hallucinations. Learn to chaining prompts and engineer advanced prompts.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces core concepts of prompt engineering, including constructing clear and specific prompts and evaluating model responses, which aligns with foundational proficiency in applying basic machine learning algorithms and performing effective prompt engineering.

By covering advanced prompt engineering strategies such as zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot learning, as well as techniques to evaluate and improve model outputs, the course matches intermediate proficiency in applying deep learning approaches, fine-tuning models, and using complex prompting and quality assurance techniques.

title: Visualization Best Practices in R
description: This course will help you take your data visualization skills beyond the basics and hone them into a powerful member of your data science toolkit. Over the lessons we will use two interesting open datasets to cover different types of data (proportions, point-data, single distributions, and multiple distributions) and discuss the pros and cons of the most common visualizations. In addition, we will cover some less common alternatives visualizations for the data types and how to tweak default ggplot settings to most efficiently and effectively get your message across.

parts.title: Proportions of a whole
parts.description: In this chapter, we focus on visualizing proportions of a whole; we see that pie charts really aren't so bad, along with discussing the waffle chart and stacked bars for comparing multiple proportions.

parts.title: Point data
parts.description: We shift our focus now to single-observation or point data and go over when bar charts are appropriate and when they are not, what to use when they are not, and general perception-based enhancements for your charts.

parts.title: Single distributions
parts.description: We now move on to visualizing distributional data, we expose the fragility of histograms, discuss when it is better to shift to a kernel density plots, and how to make both plots work best for your data.

parts.title: Comparing distributions
parts.description: Finishing off we take a look at comparing multiple distributions to each other. We see why the traditional box plots are very dangerous and how to easily improve them, along with investigating when you should use more advanced alternatives like the beeswarm plot and violin plots.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: This course covers a range of visualization types, discusses pros and cons, and teaches how to adapt visualizations for different data types and audiences, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on creating complex visualizations and tailoring communication for stakeholders.

The course emphasizes effective communication of data insights through visual means, including how to get your message across efficiently, which matches the intermediate proficiency in organizing insights and adapting communication for different audiences.

title: Case Study: Analyzing Customer Churn in Excel
description:
Are you ready to apply your Excel skills to a fictitious dataset? For subscription-based businesses, reducing customer churn is a top priority. In this Excel case study, you'll investigate a dataset from an example telecom company Databel and analyze their churn rates.

Analyzing churn doesn't just mean knowing the churn rate: it's also about figuring out why customers are churning at the rate they are and how to reduce churn. You'll answer these questions by creating calculated columns and fields, building PivotTables, and creating an eye-catching dashboard.

parts.title: Exploratory analysis
parts.description: In this first chapter, you'll start by exploring your new dataset in Excel and gain an initial understanding of why customers are churning.

parts.title: Investigating churn patterns
parts.description: You'll continue leveraging the Excel knowledge you gained from the prerequisite courses to investigate further why customers are leaving Databel.

parts.title: Creating a cohesive story
parts.description: In the last chapter, you'll create a dashboard-style sheet and arrange your visuals to present your results to stakeholders in a cohesive story.

topic.name: Reporting
topic.description: Most analyses are useless until they are communicated effectively to the right audience. Knowing how to report your findings in an interesting and interpretable way empowers others with greater understanding and the ability to make important data-driven decisions.

proficiency.DS: The course teaches basic dashboard creation and visual representation of churn data in Excel, aligning with foundational skills in presenting analysis results using simple charts and graphs.
Participants explore and investigate churn patterns, demonstrating the ability to systematically analyze problems and identify relevant issues, which matches foundational analytical thinking.
The course emphasizes arranging visuals and presenting findings to stakeholders in a cohesive story, which fits the foundational level of summarizing and communicating simple analysis results.
Learners connect churn analysis to business priorities, such as reducing customer loss, reflecting foundational understanding of how data analysis contributes to business goals.

title: Understanding Artificial Intelligence
description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is without any doubt the most breakthrough and omnipresent discipline in today's economy, media, industry, and society at large. This non-technical course will expose you to the basic elements of the rapidly evolving field of AI. Through plenty of hands-on activities and without any coding required, we will uncover together those jargon terms everyone keeps talking about, such as machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI, natural language processing, generative models, and more. We'll also explore a variety of AI applications in everyday life and the AI techniques behind the scenes, how can organizations become AI-driven, and what are the key lessons learned, challenges, and societal implications of AI's unstoppable progress.

parts.title: What is Artificial Intelligence (AI)?
parts.description: Get started with your journey into AI! Artificial Intelligence has rapidly shifted from a purely scientific subject to an umbrella field whose applications and uses are countless as of today, be it in business, industry, or simply as part of our daily lives. You will learn what is AI, what types of problems can be solved using AI, and what are its current limitations. You will also gain a broad understanding of the subareas within AI and its related disciplines.

parts.title: Tasks AI can solve
parts.description: What are the core functions of AI systems and the possibilities each of its areas has to offer? Where does the data that fuels AI systems come from, and how do techniques like machine learning make use of data to solve a variety of problems? This chapter answers these questions and more, unveiling how different forms of AI can acquire data, learn from the data, and interact with its surroundings- be it the physical or digital environment.

parts.title: Harnessing AI in Organizations
parts.description: Get ready to plunge into the exciting world of AI in business and enterprise! This chapter uncovers the fundamental concepts, guidelines, and best practices to build or become an AI-driven organization. Whether it is for equipping your products, services, and projects with a touch of intelligence, or revolutionizing operational processes within your organization, by the end of this chapter, you will understand the essential elements to embrace this technology: from culture to data and infrastructure, to building teams of talented AI professionals. You'll also learn about challenges that may appear along the way and examples of success stories from big companies that learned to make AI a central aspect of their brand.

parts.title: The human side of AI
parts.description: As our thrilling AI journey comes to an end, we delve into the profound connection between AI and its impact on humanity and society. We will explore subjects like AI democratization and responsible AI, encompassing ethics, interpretability, fairness, and safety - all crucial aspects for cultivating AI systems that positively influence our lives. Lastly, we cast our gaze towards the horizon, outlining the exciting prospects and challenges AI presents in shaping a sustainable future.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces basic AI concepts, terminology, and applications without requiring coding, aligning with foundational proficiency which expects understanding of core AI concepts, machine learning, deep learning, and societal implications.

The course covers how organizations can become AI-driven and explores business applications of AI, matching the foundational level's focus on recognizing business opportunities and understanding the relevance of AI to business functions.

proficiency.SA: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
proficiency.DS: By addressing responsible AI, ethics, fairness, and societal impact, the course supports foundational proficiency in understanding ethical considerations and the importance of transparency and fairness in AI.

title: End-to-End Machine Learning
description: Dive into the world of machine learning and discover how to design, train, and deploy end-to-end models with this comprehensive course. Through engaging, real-world examples and hands-on exercises, you'll learn to tackle complex data problems and build powerful ML models. By the end of this course, you'll be equipped with the skills needed to create, monitor, and maintain high-performing models that deliver actionable insights.

parts.title: Design and Exploration
parts.description: In this initial chapter,you will engage in the foundational stages of any machine learning project: designing an end-to-end machine learning use case, exploratory data analysis, and data preparation. By the end of the chapter, you will have a solid understanding of the early stages of a machine learning project, from conceptualizing a use case to preparing the data for further processing and model training.

parts.title: Model Training and Evaluation
parts.description: This chapter will delve deep into the essential processes of model training and evaluation. It comprises four comprehensive lessons, focusing on various aspects of feature engineering, model training, logging experiments, and model evaluation.

parts.title: Model Deployment
parts.description: This chapter delves into the essential elements of model deployment, a crucial phase in the machine learning lifecycle. Starting with testing, the chapter then progresses to architectural components, with a focus on feature stores and model registries. Subsequently, we will dive into the realm of packaging and containerization. The chapter concludes with an overview of Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD).

parts.title: Model Monitoring
parts.description: In the final chapter, you will navigate the intricacies of model monitoring, a critical phase in the machine learning lifecycle.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: This course covers the full machine learning lifecycle, including design, training, deployment, and monitoring of models, aligning with advanced proficiency which requires building production-ready AI solutions, deploying pipelines, and maintaining models post-deployment.

The course addresses advanced programming skills such as implementing CI/CD, packaging, and containerization, which are key for developing and deploying scalable, maintainable machine learning applications.
The course includes data preparation and exploratory data analysis, matching the intermediate level where learners automate data cleaning and transformation for model readiness.

Learners manage the end-to-end ML project lifecycle, including planning, deployment, and monitoring, which fits the advanced level of leading complex data science projects and coordinating cross-functional teams.

title: Foundations of Inference in Python
description:
What happens after you compute your averages and make your graphs? How do you go from descriptive statistics to confident decision-making? How can you apply hypothesis tests to solve real-world problems? In this four-hour course on inference foundations in Python, you'll get hands-on experience making sound conclusions based on data. You'll learn all about sampling and discover how improper sampling can throw statistical inference off course.

You'll start by working with hypothesis tests for normality and correlation, as well as both parametric and non-parametric tests. You'll run these tests using SciPy, and interpret their output for decision-making.

Next, you'll measure the strength of an outcome using effect size and statistical power, all while avoiding spurious correlations by applying corrections.

Finally, you'll use simulation, randomization, and meta-analysis to work with a broad range of data, including re-analyzing results from other researchers.

Following the course, you will be able to successfully take big data and use it to make principled decisions that leaders can rely on. You'll go beyond graphs and summary statistics to produce reliable, repeatable, and explainable results.

parts.title: Inferential Statistics and Sampling
parts.description: In this chapter, we'll explore the relationship between samples and statistically justifiable conclusions. Choosing a sample is the basis of making sound statistical decisions, and we'll explore how the choice of a sample affects the outcome of your inference.

parts.title: Hypothesis Testing Toolkit
parts.description: Learn all about applying normality tests, correlation tests, and parametric and non-parametric tests for sound inference. Hypothesis tests are tools, and choosing the right tool for the job is critical for statistical decision-making. While you may be familiar with some of these tests in introductory courses, you'll go deeper to enhance your inferential toolkit in this chapter.

parts.title: Effect Size
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll measure and interpret effect size in various situations, encounter the multiple comparisons problem, and explore the power of a test in depth. While p-values tell you if a significant effect is present, they don't tell you how strong that effect is. Effect size measures how strong an effect a treatment has. Master the factors underpinning effect size in this chapter.

parts.title: Simulation, Randomization, and Meta-Analysis
parts.description: You'll expand your inferential statistics toolkit further with a look at bootstrapping, permutation tests, and methods of combining evidence from p-values. Bootstrapping will provide you with a first look at statistical simulation. In the lesson meta-analysis, you'll learn all about combining results from multiple studies. You'll end with a look at permutation tests, a powerful and flexible non-parametric statistical tool.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course covers hypothesis testing, inferential statistics, effect size, statistical power, and simulation-all core intermediate-level skills for data science analysts. It goes beyond basic descriptive statistics to include practical application of statistical tests and interpretation of results for decision-making.

The course introduces advanced topics such as meta-analysis, bootstrapping, permutation tests, and corrections for multiple comparisons, which are relevant for advanced proficiency. It emphasizes producing reliable, repeatable, and explainable results, and interpreting complex statistical output.

title: Feature Engineering for NLP in Python
description: In this course, you will learn techniques that will allow you to extract useful information from text and process them into a format suitable for applying ML models. More specifically, you will learn about POS tagging, named entity recognition, readability scores, the n-gram and tf-idf models, and how to implement them using scikit-learn and spaCy. You will also learn to compute how similar two documents are to each other.  In the process, you will predict the sentiment of movie reviews and build movie and Ted Talk recommenders. Following the course, you will be able to engineer critical features out of any text and solve some of the most challenging problems in data science!

parts.title: Basic features and readability scores
parts.description: Learn to compute basic features such as number of words, number of characters, average word length and number of special characters (such as Twitter hashtags and mentions).  You will also learn to compute readability scores and determine the amount of education required to comprehend a piece of text.

parts.title: Text preprocessing, POS tagging and NER
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn about tokenization and lemmatization. You will then learn how to perform text cleaning, part-of-speech tagging, and named entity recognition using the spaCy library. Upon mastering these concepts, you will proceed to make the Gettysburg address machine-friendly, analyze noun usage in fake news, and identify people mentioned in a TechCrunch article.

parts.title: N-Gram models
parts.description: Learn about n-gram modeling and use it to perform sentiment analysis on movie reviews.

parts.title: TF-IDF and similarity scores
parts.description: Learn how to compute tf-idf weights and the cosine similarity score between two vectors. You will use these concepts to build a movie and a TED Talk recommender. Finally, you will also learn about word embeddings and using word vector representations, you will compute similarities between various Pink Floyd songs.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course covers practical NLP feature engineering techniques such as POS tagging, NER, n-grams, tf-idf, and document similarity, which align with the intermediate proficiency level's focus on applying AI techniques to real-world problems, using open-source libraries, and developing AI-powered solutions.

Learners implement NLP feature engineering using Python libraries like scikit-learn and spaCy, matching the intermediate level's requirement to use libraries for data manipulation and apply programming concepts to solve data problems.
The course teaches text preprocessing, cleaning, and transformation, which are key intermediate data processing skills, including handling unstructured data and automating data cleaning tasks.

title: Introduction to Data Engineering
description: Have you heard people talk about data engineers and wonder what it is they do? Do you know what data engineers do but you're not sure how to become one yourself? This course is the perfect introduction. It touches upon all things you need to know to streamline your data processing. This introductory course will give you enough context to start exploring the world of data engineering. It's perfect for people who work at a company with several data sources and don't have a clear idea of how to use all those data sources in a scalable way. Be the first one to introduce these techniques to your company and become the company star employee.

parts.title: Introduction to Data Engineering
parts.description: In this first chapter, you will be exposed to the world of data engineering! Explore the differences between a data engineer and a data scientist, get an overview of the various tools data engineers use and expand your understanding of how cloud technology plays a role in data engineering.

parts.title: Data engineering toolbox
parts.description: Now that you know the primary differences between a data engineer and a data scientist, get ready to explore the data engineer's toolbox! Learn in detail about different types of databases data engineers use, how parallel computing is a cornerstone of the data engineer's toolkit, and how to schedule data processing jobs using scheduling frameworks.

parts.title: Extract, Transform and Load (ETL)
parts.description: Having been exposed to the toolbox of data engineers, it's now time to jump into the bread and butter of a data engineer's workflow! With ETL, you will learn how to extract raw data from various sources, transform this raw data into actionable insights, and load it into relevant databases ready for consumption!

parts.title: Case Study: DataCamp
parts.description: Cap off all that you've learned in the previous three chapters by completing a real-world data engineering use case from DataCamp! You will perform and schedule an ETL process that transforms raw course rating data, into actionable course recommendations for DataCamp students!

proficiency.DS: This course introduces the basics of data engineering, including ETL processes, handling multiple data sources, and scheduling data jobs, which aligns with foundational skills in data processing such as loading, cleaning, and transforming data.

The course covers the use of Python and introduces tools and frameworks used by data engineers, matching the foundational level of programming competency where learners use open-source languages for basic data manipulation.

title: Data Visualization in Google Sheets
description: A picture can tell a thousand words - but only if you use the right picture! This course teaches you the fundamentals of data visualization with Google Sheets. You'll learn how to create common chart types like bar charts, histograms, and scatter charts, as well as more advanced types, such as sparkline and candlestick charts. You will look at how to prepare your data and use Data Validation and VLookup formulas to target specific data to chart. You'll learn how to use Conditional Formatting to apply a format to a cell or a range of cells based on certain criteria, and finally, how to create a dashboard showing plots and data together. Along the way, you'll use data from the Olympics, sharks attacks, and Marine Technology from the ASX.

parts.title: Business Intelligence and Using Dashboards
parts.description: Learn about business intelligence and dashboards for analyzing information in todays data-driven world.  Create a basic dashboard and master setting up your data to get the most out of it.

parts.title: Efficient Column Charts
parts.description: Create and format a column chart to showcase data and learn a few smart tricks along the way.  Look at using named ranges to refer to cells in your worksheet, making them user-friendly and easy to work with.

parts.title: Dashboard Controls
parts.description: A dashboard is like a control panel.  Look at ways to allow a user to use this control panel to get different results from your dashboard.

parts.title: Other Charts for Your Dashboard
parts.description: A picture paints a thousand words.  Look at what types of charts to use in what situation to showcase your data.

parts.title: Conditional Formatting
parts.description: Learn how to use rules based on criteria you set to format certain cells on your dashboard. See the formatting change as the values in the cells change.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: This course covers the fundamentals of creating and interpreting basic charts (bar, histogram, scatter) and introduces dashboard concepts, aligning with foundational skills in presenting data clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

The course includes more advanced chart types (sparkline, candlestick), dashboard controls, and conditional formatting, which match intermediate proficiency in creating complex visualizations and organizing insights for different stakeholders.
By teaching how to summarize and present findings using charts and dashboards, the course supports foundational skills in communicating data analysis results in clear, simple terms.
The introduction to business intelligence and dashboards helps learners recognize how data visualization supports business decision-making, matching foundational business acumen requirements.

title: Decoding Decision Modeling
description: Did you know that an average adult makes anywhere from 20,000 to 35,000 decisions each day? Enhance your decision-making skills with this foundational course on Decision Models and discover its importance in navigating uncertainties and risks. Learn to construct and analyze Decision Models using tools like decision trees, influence diagrams, and sensitivity analysis. Gain practical skills in integrating data analytics to optimize outcomes and make strategic decisions aligned with organizational goals. Perfect for anyone looking to elevate decision-making abilities in a data-driven world.
