parts.description: Having explored your data, it's now time to preprocess it and get it ready for machine learning. Learn the why, what, and how of preprocessing, including feature selection and feature engineering.

parts.title: Churn Prediction
parts.description: With your data preprocessed and ready for machine learning, it's time to predict churn! Learn how to build supervised learning machine models in Python using scikit-learn.

parts.title: Model Tuning
parts.description: Learn how to improve the performance of your models using hyperparameter tuning and gain a better understanding of the drivers of customer churn that you can take back to the business.

proficiency.DS: The course teaches use of Python libraries like pandas and scikit-learn for data analysis and machine learning, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on implementing functions, using libraries for data manipulation, and applying programming to real-world tasks.

Covers data exploration, preprocessing, feature selection, and engineering, which matches the intermediate level's requirements for automating data cleaning, combining datasets, and preparing data for analysis.

The course involves using summary statistics, visualizations, and supervised learning models, fitting the intermediate level's focus on applying inferential statistics, regression, and interpreting statistical outputs.

Focuses on building and tuning supervised machine learning models for churn prediction, which matches the intermediate level's expectation of applying AI techniques to real-world problems and evaluating model performance.
Emphasizes communicating actionable insights to stakeholders, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on structuring data insights and adapting communication for business audiences.

Applies data science to a business problem (customer churn), requiring understanding of business objectives and communicating findings relevant to business decisions, which fits the intermediate level.

title: User-Oriented Design in Power BI
description: In this course, you learn how to design with users in mind. You'll get introduced to some best practices in data visualization and optimize your visualizations to be more accessible to visually impaired individuals. This course also teaches you when to use paginated reports, a prerequisite for the official PL-300 exam!

parts.title: Design with Users in Mind
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn how a design is made using focal points to guide users naturally between visuals. You'll also explore some of the accessibility options for reports that Power BI offers.

parts.title: Readying for Production and Paginated Reports
parts.description: Let's get ready for production! In this chapter, you'll explore some best practices to ready your report, and you'll learn when you should (and shouldn't) create paginated reports.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: The course covers best practices in designing user-oriented and accessible visualizations, including optimizing for visually impaired users and understanding when to use paginated reports. These skills align with the intermediate level, which expects the ability to create complex visualizations, adapt communication for different audiences, and ensure accessibility.

The course emphasizes organizing insights for users and making reports accessible, which matches the intermediate proficiency level for technical communication-structuring narratives, adapting for stakeholders, and ensuring accessibility in data presentations.

title: Intermediate GitHub Concepts
description: Take your GitHub skills to the next level with this intermediate course, building on the foundations of our introductory course. You'll dive deeper into GitHub Projects, automation with GitHub Actions, and advanced security features. By the end, you'll be able to manage complex workflows, enhance team collaboration, and secure your projects more effectively. This course is perfect for those who already know the basics and want to streamline their data or software project management further!

parts.title: Managing Work with GitHub Projects
parts.description: Get a refresher on GitHub basics and dive into advanced project management. Learn how to set up and automate GitHub Projects for better team collaboration and workflow efficiency.

parts.title: GitHub Administration and Authentication
parts.description: Master GitHub's admin tools and security features. You'll explore managing permissions and user access and implementing secure authentication methods for your organization.

parts.title: Managing an InnerSource Program and Secure Development
parts.description: Learn how to set up InnerSource practices and ensure secure development. Discover best practices for managing multiple projects and tools for detecting vulnerabilities and securing your codebase.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers intermediate GitHub concepts such as advanced project management, automation, and security, aligning with the intermediate proficiency level's focus on collaborative codebase management, documentation, and code review practices.

The course emphasizes managing complex workflows, team collaboration, and project automation, which matches the intermediate level's requirements for independently managing project tasks, monitoring progress, and engaging with stakeholders.

title: Introduction to Statistics
description: Statistics are all around us, from marketing to sales to healthcare. The ability to collect, analyze, and draw conclusions from data is not only extremely valuable, but it is also becoming commonplace to expect roles that are not traditionally analytical to understand the fundamental concepts of statistics. This course will equip you with the necessary skills to feel confident in working with analyzing data to draw insights. You'll be introduced to common methods used for summarizing and describing data, learn how probability can be applied to commercial scenarios, and discover how experiments are conducted to understand relationships and patterns. You'll work with real-world datasets including crime data in London, England, and sales data from an online retail company!

parts.title: Summary Statistics
parts.description: Summary statistics gives you the tools you need to describe your data. In this chapter, you'll explore summary statistics including mean, median, and standard deviation, and learn how to accurately interpret them. You'll also develop your critical thinking skills, allowing you to choose the best summary statistics for your data.

parts.title: Probability and distributions
parts.description: Probability underpins a large part of statistics, where it is used to calculate the chance of events occurring. You'll work with real-world sales data and learn how data with different values can be interpreted as a probability distribution. You'll find out about discrete and continuous probability distributions, including the discovery of the normal distribution and how it occurs frequently in natural events!

parts.title: More Distributions and the Central Limit Theorem
parts.description: It's time to explore more probability distributions. You'll learn about the binomial distribution for visualizing the probability of binary outcomes,   and one of the most important distributions in statistics, the normal distribution. You'll see how distributions can be described by their shape,       along with discovering the Poisson distribution and its role in calculating the probabilities of events occuring over time. You'll also gain an         understanding of the central limit theorem!

parts.title: Correlation and Hypothesis Testing
parts.description: In the final chapter, you'll be introduced to hypothesis testing and how it can be used to accurately draw conclusions about a population. You'll discover correlation and how it can be used to quantify a linear relationship between two variables. You'll find out about experimental design techniques such as randomization and blinding. You'll also learn about concepts used to minimize the risk of drawing the wrong conclusion about the results of hypothesis tests!

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces fundamental statistical concepts such as mean, median, standard deviation, probability, distributions, correlation, and hypothesis testing, which align with the foundational proficiency requirements for summarizing, describing, and interpreting data.

The course covers basic experimental design, hypothesis formulation, and interpretation of research findings, matching the foundational level's emphasis on understanding the scientific method and basic research techniques.

title: Data Management Concepts
description: Dive into data management with this course designed for both enthusiasts and leaders. Learn about the data life cycle, key principles, and pillars such as governance, quality, and security. Understand how to evaluate and improve your organization's data management maturity, addressing ethical issues like privacy. Hear about emerging trends like data mesh architecture and prepare to make informed decisions in a data-driven business world.

parts.title: Demystifying data management
parts.description: Embark on an introductory journey into data management in this chapter. Uncover the benefits it offers, examine the stages of the data life cycle, and conclude by understanding the key principles that enable effective data management.

parts.title: Pillars of data management
parts.description: Delve into the pillars of data management in this chapter, where exploration of reliability, safety, governance, and intelligence unfolds. Uncover the complexities of building a robust data foundation and navigate the dynamic phases of data management through Peter Aiken's DMBoK Pyramid, acknowledging the adaptability essential for organizational distinctiveness.

parts.title: Data management within organizations
parts.description: As your data management journey nears its end, you'll be armed with practical blueprints to assess your data's maturity, build trust through transparent accountability, and uphold ethical practices. With these tools, you'll unlock your data's full potential, crafting future-proof strategies that propel your organization to new heights.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces the data life cycle, key principles, and foundational pillars such as governance and quality, which aligns with foundational proficiency in understanding and applying basic data management concepts.

The course covers evaluating and improving organizational data management maturity, addressing ethical issues, and understanding organizational data practices, which matches intermediate proficiency in applying and assessing data management within organizations.

The course helps learners understand how data management supports business decision-making and organizational goals, which is relevant for foundational business acumen in recognizing the value of data as an organizational asset.

The course addresses ethical issues like privacy and the importance of transparent accountability, matching foundational proficiency in recognizing and adhering to ethical and privacy standards in data management.

By covering organizational accountability and ethical practices in data management, the course supports intermediate proficiency in evaluating and upholding ethical standards within organizational data practices.

title: Introduction to Microsoft Copilot
description: Take your business to the next level with Microsoft Copilot! This hands-on course is perfect for business professionals who are new to Copilot and want to unlock its full potential. Discover how to supercharge productivity, streamline workflows, and make smarter, data-driven decisions. Through practical examples and real-world scenarios, you'll learn how to seamlessly integrate Copilot into your everyday operations, empowering your team to work faster and smarter. Don't just keep up with the competition-stay ahead by mastering the tools that drive business success!

parts.title: Overview of Microsoft Copilot
parts.description: Learn how to interact with Copilot and Copilot for Microsoft 365 apps. In this chapter, the learner will be introduced to writing prompts and the copilot system. They will also examine different user groups that can use Copilot and its capabilities.

parts.title: Working with Microsoft 365 Copilot
parts.description:
In this chapter, we look at the capabilities of Copilot in different Microsoft Teams Apps covering Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint. and Excel.
This chapter is heavily focused on the benefits of using Copilot to improve productivity,

parts.title: Copilot Best Practices and Responsible AI
parts.description:
This chapter looks at the RAI framework created by Microsoft. It also looks at Copilot lab, which the learner can use to help with writing prompts.
Lastly, this chapter covers a case study of how a Solution Architect would use Copilot in their work day.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces basic AI concepts through Microsoft Copilot, focusing on prompt engineering, productivity, and responsible AI, which aligns with foundational proficiency in applying basic AI tools and understanding their business impact.

Emphasizes using Copilot to drive business productivity and smarter decision-making, matching the foundational level of recognizing business opportunities where AI tools can contribute to business goals.
Covers presenting data-driven insights and communicating with Copilot in business contexts, supporting foundational skills in clear communication of technical information using AI tools.

proficiency.SA: Knowledge of Responsible and Ethical AI Use
proficiency.DS: Addresses responsible AI frameworks and best practices, reflecting foundational knowledge of ethical and responsible AI use as outlined in the competency profile.

title: Working with Dates and Times in Python
description: You'll probably never have a time machine, but how about a machine for analyzing time? As soon as time enters any analysis, things can get weird. It's easy to get tripped up on day and month boundaries, time zones, daylight saving time, and all sorts of other things that can confuse the unprepared. If you're going to do any kind of analysis involving time, you'll want to use Python to sort it out. Working with data sets on hurricanes and bike trips, we'll cover counting events, figuring out how much time has elapsed between events and plotting data over time. You'll work in both standard Python and in Pandas, and we'll touch on the dateutil library, the only timezone library endorsed by the official Python documentation. After this course, you'll confidently handle date and time data in any format like a champion.

parts.title: Dates and Calendars
parts.description: Hurricanes (also known as cyclones or typhoons) hit the U.S. state of Florida several times per year. To start off this course, you'll learn how to work with date objects in Python, starting with the dates of every hurricane to hit Florida since 1950. You'll learn how Python handles dates, common date operations, and the right way to format dates to avoid confusion.

parts.title: Combining Dates and Times
parts.description: Bike sharing programs have swept through cities around the world -- and luckily for us, every trip gets recorded! Working with all of the comings and goings of one bike in Washington, D.C., you'll practice working with dates and times together. You'll parse dates and times from text, analyze peak trip times, calculate ride durations, and more.

parts.title: Time Zones and Daylight Saving
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn to confidently tackle the time-related topic that causes people the most trouble: time zones and daylight saving. Continuing with our bike data, you'll learn how to compare clocks around the world, how to gracefully handle "spring forward" and "fall back," and how to get up-to-date timezone data from the dateutil library.

parts.title: Easy and Powerful: Dates and Times in Pandas
parts.description: To conclude this course, you'll apply everything you've learned about working with dates and times in standard Python to working with dates and times in Pandas. With additional information about each bike ride, such as what station it started and stopped at and whether or not the rider had a yearly membership, you'll be able to dig much more deeply into the bike trip data. In this chapter, you'll cover powerful Pandas operations, such as grouping and plotting results by time.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers practical programming skills in Python and Pandas, focusing on parsing, manipulating, and analyzing date and time data, including handling time zones and daylight saving time. These tasks align with the intermediate proficiency level, which expects the ability to use libraries for data manipulation and implement functions for more complex data tasks.

The course teaches combining, cleaning, and transforming time-based data, including parsing from text, handling time zones, and grouping/plotting by time in Pandas. These are key intermediate data processing skills, involving automation of data cleaning and processing both structured and time-based data.

title: Case Study: Analyzing Customer Churn in Power BI
description: Are you ready to apply your Power BI skills to a real-world dataset? For subscription-based businesses, reducing customer churn is a top priority. In this Power BI case study, you'll investigate a dataset from an example telecom company called Databel and analyze their churn rates. Analyzing churn doesn't just mean knowing what the churn rate is: it's also about figuring out why customers are churning at the rate they are, and how to reduce churn. You'll answer these questions by creating measures and calculated columns, while simultaneously creating eye-catching report pages.

parts.title: Exploratory Analysis
parts.description: In this first chapter, you'll start exploring the new dataset and revisit creating measures in Power BI to get a better understanding of why customers are churning.

parts.title: Investigating Churn Patterns
parts.description: You'll continue by leveraging the Power BI knowledge you gained from the prerequisite courses to further investigate why customers are leaving Databel.

parts.title: Visualizing your Analysis
parts.description: In the last chapter, you'll create dashboard-style pages and arrange them into stories, so that you can share your results with stakeholders.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: The course requires creating complex visualizations and dashboard-style pages to communicate insights, which aligns with the intermediate level's focus on organizing insights, adapting communication for stakeholders, and linking findings to business objectives.

The course involves investigating why customers churn and interpreting data patterns, which matches the intermediate level's emphasis on responding to complex analytical issues and developing recommendations.

By arranging visualizations into stories for stakeholders and analyzing business problems like churn, the course fits the intermediate level's requirements for tailoring insights to business objectives and communicating their impact.

title: Developing R Packages
description: Acquire the skills to develop your own R package from scratch by understanding how to structure your code, document your functions, and test your package. You'll learn how to use various packages including devtools, roxygen2, testthat and more as well as rmarkdown to speed up and improve your package development workflow. Get ready to dive into the dynamic world of R package development and empower yourself with a valuable toolset that can greatly enhance your data analysis journey!

parts.title: Creating R Packages: From Data to Functions
parts.description: Dive into the essentials of R package construction, from understanding the architecture, the critical R and man directories, to the significance of the DESCRIPTION and NAMESPACE files. Get hands-on with the usethis package as you create your own package skeleton and include data. Strengthen your R function writing skills, grasp best practices for package development, and get comfortable saving functions to a file. Finally, install your package locally using devtools.

parts.title: Designing R Packages: Package Naming and Dependencies
parts.description: Learn the advantages of creating packages versus using scripts, exploring the impact on code organization, reproducibility, collaboration, and sharing. Discover effective strategies for structuring code and functions within the R directory, and choosing an appropriate name and license for your package. Finally, you'll learn how to manage CRAN package dependencies.

parts.title: Package Documentation: Generating Help Files and Vignettes
parts.description: Harness the power of examples in documentation by creating function examples with roxygen2. Understand the significance of examples in clarifying function behavior and identifying key components of a well-documented R function. Explore the purpose of vignettes in R package documentation and learn best practices for creating engaging vignettes and evaluating their content and quality through metadata analysis.

parts.title: Testing R Packages: Using Unit Tests and Robust Checks
parts.description: Identify why the unit tests are important to package development and maintenance and learn how to implement the testthat package for unit tests. Convert R examples into expectations to build your unit test knowledge. You'll then gain an understanding on how to document your package data and run some final checks to ensure you have developed a robust R package.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced programming skills such as structuring code, managing dependencies, and developing, testing, and documenting R packages, which aligns with the advanced proficiency level requiring implementation of best practices and modular, maintainable code.

The course emphasizes code organization, documentation, versioning, and testing within R package development, matching the advanced level's focus on reproducibility, code standards, and collaborative workflows.

title: Deep Learning for Images with PyTorch
description: In this course, you'll use PyTorch to discover image classification, object recognition, segmentation, and image generation. You'll work with both binary and multi-class image classification models, utilize pre-trained models for deep learning tasks, and master object detection with bounding boxes. Additionally, you'll delve into image segmentation, including semantic, instance, and panoptic types, with real-world applications. Finally, you'll explore Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and learn to assess the quality and diversity of the generated images.

parts.title: Image classification with CNNs
parts.description: Learn about image classification with CNNs, the difference between the binary and multi-class image classification models, and how to use transfer learning for image classification in PyTorch.

parts.title: Object recognition
parts.description: Detect objects in images by predicting bounding boxes around them and evaluate the performance of object recognition models.

parts.title: Image Segmentation
parts.description: Learn about the three types of image segmentation (semantic, instance, and panoptic), their applications, and the appropriate machine learning model architectures to perform each of them.

parts.title: Image Generation with GANs
parts.description: Generate completely new images with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Learn to build and train a Deep Convolutional GAN, and how to evaluate the quality and variety of its outputs.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced AI methods such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image classification, object detection, segmentation, and generative adversarial networks (GANs), aligning with the advanced proficiency requirements for applying complex AI methodologies to real-world problems.

Learners use PyTorch to implement and fine-tune deep learning models, which matches the intermediate level's focus on using libraries and designing functions for data manipulation and model development.

title: Data Literacy Case Study: Remote Working Analysis
description:
Are you ready to apply your data literacy skills to a real-world case study?

In this case study, you'll work as a consultant for a fictitious company and investigate their current remote working policy and ways to improve it.

Through hands-on exercises, you'll go step-by-step from business problem to communicating the right insights. You'll practice data literacy skills like breaking the business problem down to analytical questions, choosing the right type of analytics, communicating insights effectively using visualizations and narrative structure, and formulating recommendations for your clients.

parts.title: Getting to Know the Case Study
parts.description:
Polaris Tech has hired you as a consultant to help them improve their remote working policy. They have a dataset they wish you and your team to analyze. 

To start, you'll get to know the business problem and the dataset better. You'll also plan out your analysis strategy from problem to actionable insights.

parts.title: Investigating Remote Working Habits
parts.description:
Now that you've planned out your analysis strategy and got to know the data, it is time for the main analysis of the remote working survey. 

You'll follow along with your team and practice how to build up to delivering actionable insights for Polaris Tech. 

Once the results are in, you'll practice how to use communication tools like visualizations, narrative structure, and the right format to help Polaris Tech make the most of its data.

proficiency.DS: The course guides learners through breaking down a business problem, formulating analytical questions, and making actionable recommendations, which aligns with foundational business acumen skills.
Participants practice communicating insights using visualizations and narrative structure, matching foundational requirements for clear, simple communication of data findings.
The course involves summarizing and describing data features and using basic analytics, which fits foundational statistical literacy.

title: Case Study: HR Analytics in Tableau
description:
Analyzing HR Data in Tableau
In this Tableau case study, you will explore a dataset for a fictitious software company called Atlas Labs. This course focuses on helping you import, analyze and visualize Human Resources data in Tableau. Building on your existing knowledge of the platform, you'll learn how to effectively work with Tableau using example data.

Visualize What Impacts Attrition
You'll carry out exploratory data analysis and will use calculated fields to help build powerful visualizations. You'll finish your analysis by diving deeper into attrition and what factors impact attrition. This analysis will help the organization determine what action it will need to take to retain more employees.

Summarize Your Findings in a Dashboard
We'll finalize the case study by making design changes to our Tableau dashboard that provides a clean, branded design.

parts.title: Preparing Data and EDA
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll start by bringing all your data into Tableau and building relationships between tables. Once your data is ready, you'll start by rolling your sleeves up and doing some initial exploratory data analysis on general HR trends.

parts.title: Analyzing Demographics and Performance
parts.description: This chapter is about using your Tableau skills to build custom visuals that you can use throughout your dashboard. Atlas Labs would like some answers on its employee demographics and performance. Luckily, they have you on their team as a data analyst to help them explore their data further.

parts.title: Bringing It All Together
parts.description: It's almost time to deliver your report to the key stakeholders at Atlas Labs. In this final chapter, you'll be focusing on delivering insights on attrition and what factors affect employee retention. Finally, you'll be cleaning up the overall layout of the dashboard to create a user-friendly, clean, and branded experience.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: This course requires learners to build custom visuals, perform exploratory data analysis, and design dashboards in Tableau, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on creating complex visualizations, structuring insights, and adapting communication for stakeholders.

The course emphasizes summarizing findings in a dashboard and delivering insights to stakeholders, matching the intermediate level's requirement to organize data insights, adapt communication for different audiences, and link findings to business objectives.

By analyzing HR data to determine factors impacting attrition and providing actionable recommendations, the course aligns with the intermediate level's focus on tailoring data projects to business objectives and communicating their impact on business performance.

title: Case Study: Analyzing City Time Series Data in R
description: In this course, you will strengthen your knowledge of time series topics through interactive exercises and interesting datasets. You'll explore a variety of datasets about Boston, including data on flights, weather, economic trends, and local sports teams.

parts.title: Flight Data
parts.description: You've been hired to understand the travel needs of tourists visiting the Boston area. As your first assignment on the job, you'll practice the  skills you've learned for time series data manipulation in R by exploring  data on flights arriving at Boston's Logan International Airport (BOS)  using xts & zoo.

parts.title: Weather Data
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll expand your time series data library to include weather data in the Boston area. Before you can conduct any analysis, you'll need to do some data manipulation, including merging multiple xts objects  and isolating certain periods of the data. It's a great opportunity for  more practice!

parts.title: Economic Data
parts.description: Now it's time to go further afield. In addition to flight delays, your client is interested in how Boston's tourism industry is affected by economic trends. You'll need to manipulate some time series data on economic indicators,  including GDP per capita and unemployment in the United States in general and  Massachusetts (MA) in particular.

parts.title: Sports Data
parts.description: Having exhausted other options, your client now believes Boston's tourism industry must be related to the success of local sports teams. In your final task on this project, your supervisor has asked you to assemble some time series data on Boston's sports teams over the past few years.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course focuses on advanced time series analysis, requiring manipulation and interpretation of multiple real-world datasets, which aligns with applying advanced statistical techniques and interpreting complex statistical output.
Learners practice merging, manipulating, and preparing time series data from various sources, matching the intermediate level's focus on automating data cleaning and handling structured datasets.

title: Introduction to Power Query in Excel
description: Unlock the true potential of your data! Say goodbye to manual data wrangling and hello to streamlined, efficient data transformation. In this introductory course to Excel Power Query, you will learn how to seamlessly connect to multiple data sources, clean and shape your data easily, and load it so it's ready for analysis. Along the way, you will learn about the many available functions that Power Query offers, giving you the confidence to streamline your next Excel-based report. Whether you're a data analyst, business professional, or spreadsheet enthusiast, this course will empower you to save time, make more informed decisions, and extract valuable insights from your data like never before.

parts.title: Getting Started with Power Query in Excel
parts.description: Imagine Excel as you've never seen it before - Power Query opens a window to a whole new world of data possibilities! In this chapter, you'll explore the layout and features of Power Query and its interplay with traditional Excel workbooks. You'll load data from multiple sources and learn to structure them through column and row manipulations while maintaining an applied steps log of all your actions.

parts.title: Data Cleaning and Preparation
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll harness Power Query's digital cleaning features to prepare a squeaky-clean dataset! Column profiling features will be covered, allowing you to handle errors and missing data effectively. You'll also master eliminating duplicate data and correcting for data entry issues and outliers.

parts.title: Column Transformations
parts.description: It's time to transform! This chapter covers many basic column transformations - a vital step in the journey from raw data to meaningful insights. You will learn how and when to apply numeric, date/time, and text transformations to both transform and derive column contents with Excel Power Query's many built-in features.

parts.title: Shaping and Grouping Data
parts.description: It's all about shaping and grouping in this final chapter! You will get hands-on experience with powerful transformation options to bring your analysis prep to the next level. You'll learn how and when to apply transpose, pivot, and group-by transformations - all within the Power Query editor. You'll also learn how to leverage existing queries to build new ones and track their connection in the Query Dependencies tree.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces foundational skills in loading, cleaning, transforming, and preparing data using Power Query in Excel, which aligns with the foundational proficiency level for Data Processing by teaching basic data cleaning, handling missing values, and preparing data for analysis.

title: Joining Data with dplyr
description: Often in data science, you'll encounter fascinating data that is spread across multiple tables. This course will teach you the skills you'll need to join multiple tables together to analyze them in combination. You'll practice your skills using a fun dataset about LEGOs from the Rebrickable website. The dataset contains information about the sets, parts, themes, and colors of LEGOs, but is spread across many tables. You'll work with the data throughout the course as you learn a total of six different joins! You'll learn four mutating joins: inner join, left join, right join, and full join, and two filtering joins: semi join and anti join. In the final chapter, you'll apply your new skills to Stack Overflow data, containing each of the almost 300,000 Stack Oveflow questions that are tagged with R, including information about their answers, the date they were asked, and their score. Get ready to take your dplyr skills to the next level!

parts.title: Joining Tables
parts.description: Get started with your first joining verb: inner-join! You'll learn to join tables together to answer questions about the LEGO dataset, which contains information across many tables about the sets, parts, themes, and colors of LEGOs over time.

parts.title: Left and Right Joins
parts.description: Learn two more mutating joins, the left and right join, which are mirror images of each other! You'll learn use cases for each type of join as you explore parts and colors of LEGO themes. Then, you'll explore how to join tables to themselves to understand the hierarchy of LEGO themes in the data.

parts.title: Full, Semi, and Anti Joins
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll cover three more joining verbs: full-join, semi-join, and anti-join. You'll then use these verbs to answer questions about the similarities and differences between a variety of LEGO sets.

parts.title: Case Study: Joins on Stack Overflow Data
parts.description: Put together all the types of join you learned in this course to analyze a new dataset: Stack Overflow questions, answers, and tags. This includes calculating and visualizing trends for some notable tags like dplyr and ggplot2. You'll also master one more method for combining tables, the bind_rows verb, which stacks tables on top of each other.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today's most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: This course covers combining multiple datasets using various join operations in R's dplyr, which aligns with the intermediate proficiency level requiring the ability to merge data from different sources and handle inconsistencies in data structure.

The course teaches the use of dplyr functions for data manipulation in R, including joining tables and using advanced verbs, which matches the intermediate level's focus on implementing libraries for data transformation.

title: Large Language Models for Business
description: Delve into the business applications of Large Language Models (LLMs). Discover how they are empowering businesses to improve their workflows and find success in the new AI-powered era. Grasping their foundational elements will equip you with key insights into LLMs and their impact on modern business.

parts.title: The Rise of LLMs in the Business Realm
parts.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are driving AI advancements, and reshaping the business world. This chapter explains how LLMs are poised to drive growth.

parts.title: LLMs Solutions
parts.description: This chapter will empower you to harness the potential of LLMs. Gain an understanding of their strengths and weaknesses and be on the lookout for the right opportunity for success.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces the foundational elements of Large Language Models (LLMs), their business applications, and their impact, aligning with the foundational proficiency of understanding core AI concepts and basic applications.
The course explores how LLMs empower businesses and drive growth, matching the foundational level of recognizing business opportunities where AI can contribute to business goals.

title: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for Language Modeling with Keras
description: Machine Learning models are based on numerical values to make predictions/classification, but how can computers deal with text data? With the huge increase of available text data, applications such as automatic document classification, text generation, and neural machine translation became possible. In this course, you will learn how to use Recurrent Neural Networks to classify text (binary and multiclass), generate phrases simulating the character Sheldon from The Big Bang Theory TV Show, and translate Portuguese sentences into English. Are you ready to start your journey into Language Models using Keras and Python? Dive in!

parts.title: Recurrent Neural Networks and Keras
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn the foundations of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). Starting with some prerequisites, continuing to understanding how information flows through the network and finally seeing how to implement such models with Keras in the sentiment classification task.

parts.title: RNN Architecture
parts.description:
You will learn about the vanishing and exploding gradient problems, often occurring in RNNs, and how to deal with them with the GRU and LSTM cells. 
Furthermore, you'll create embedding layers for language models and revisit the sentiment classification task.

parts.title: Multi-Class Classification
parts.description: Next, in this chapter you will learn how to prepare data for the multi-class classification task, as well as the differences between multi-class classification and binary classification (sentiment analysis). Finally, you will learn how to create models and measure their performance with Keras.

parts.title: Sequence to Sequence Models
parts.description:
This chapter introduces you to two applications of RNN models: Text Generation and Neural Machine Translation.  You will learn how to prepare the text data to the format needed by the models.
The Text Generation model is used for replicating a character's way of speech and will have some fun mimicking Sheldon from The Big Bang Theory. 
Neural Machine Translation is used for example by Google Translate in a much more complex model. In this chapter, you will create a model that translates Portuguese small phrases into English.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced AI methodologies, focusing on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), LSTM, GRU, sequence-to-sequence models, and their applications in text classification, generation, and translation using Keras and Python. These topics align with the advanced proficiency level, which includes applying complex AI models to solve challenging problems involving multiple data types and high-impact applications.

The course requires implementing RNNs with Keras in Python, involving the use of libraries, model building, and performance measurement, which matches the intermediate level's focus on designing and implementing functions, using libraries, and performing data manipulation for machine learning tasks.

title: Case Study: Mortgage Trading Analysis in Power BI
description: In this Power BI case study, you will play the part of a newly hired junior trader on a trading desk for a mortgage originator. Enjoy this fast-paced and challenging case study as you learn the ins and outs of the financial system. The flow of money through our economy happens on your desk, as it trickles down from big investment banks to your lending firm, to individual borrowers - and you're the one making it happen. You will identify a population of mortgages to trade, evaluate each mortgage and each bid received from prospective buyers, and finally execute a trade. By the end of this case study, you will have sharpened your data modeling, DAX, and financial analysis skills, and you will have experienced a unique perspective on the banking industry.

parts.title: Mortgage data
parts.description: In this chapter, you will focus on getting our data ready for trading. You'll clean up mortgage data, create loan statuses, and amortize loan balances.

parts.title: Trade on
parts.description: Bids are in on the loans, so now it's time for you to analyze the bids and determine the winners.

parts.title: Trade Profit Analysis
parts.description: Now that you've struck our trades, it's time to analyze the outcomes and Sooper Mortgage's business strategy.

topic.name: Applied Finance
topic.description: The finance community has been one of the eager to embrace data science. From stock market predictions, to asset pricing and calculating the probability of loan defaults, the applications are nearly endless!

proficiency.DS: The course covers cleaning and preparing mortgage data, which aligns with foundational data processing skills such as handling missing values and formatting issues.
Using Power BI to analyze and visualize mortgage trading data matches foundational skills in presenting data with basic charts and graphs for clear insights.
Participants gain an understanding of financial systems and business strategy in mortgage trading, which fits foundational business acumen by relating data analysis to business operations.

title: Analyzing Survey Data in Python
description: Whether it is a company looking to understand its employees' work preferences or a marketing campaign wanting to know how to best cater to its dominant audience, survey data is one of the best tools out there. Here, you'll learn the purpose of analyzing survey data and when it is appropriate to apply statistical tools that are descriptive and inferential. You will learn to apply multiple sampling methods using Python, and visualize your survey results to qualitatively interpret the variables and outcomes associated with modeling tests depending on the type of survey you're analyzing.

parts.title: Why Analyze Survey Data & When to Apply Statistical Tools
parts.description: What is survey data, and how do we determine which statistical test to use to analyze the data? To answer this, you'll be able to define all sorts of survey data types, encounter important concepts like descriptive and inferential statistics, and visualize survey data to determine the appropriate statistical modeling technique needed. In doing so, you will know how to best qualitatively and quantitatively define the trends and insights you come across in surveys.

parts.title: Sampling and Weighting
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn the different ways of creating sample survey data out of population survey data by analyzing the parameters by which the survey data was taken.

parts.title: Descriptive & Inferential Statistics
parts.description: Now it's time to understand the difference between descriptive and inferential statistics concerning survey data analysis with some real-life examples. Through hands-on exercises, you'll further interpret the meaning of different variables, key measures such as central tendency and zscore, and interpret results for actionable steps.

parts.title: Statistical Modeling
parts.description: Last but not least, it's time to apply statistical modeling to survey data analysis with regression analysis, the two-sample t-test, chi-square test, and interpret the assumptions associated with these tests.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course covers descriptive and inferential statistics, hypothesis testing (t-tests, chi-square), regression, and sampling methods, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on applying and interpreting statistical techniques using Python.
Learners use Python to manipulate and analyze survey data, apply statistical libraries, and visualize results, matching the intermediate proficiency in using programming tools for data analysis.

The course involves preparing, sampling, and weighting survey data, as well as visualizing and interpreting results, which fits the intermediate level's emphasis on combining, cleaning, and transforming data for analysis.

Participants learn to visualize and communicate survey results, interpret statistical findings, and present actionable insights, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on organizing and adapting data insights for stakeholders.

title: AWS Cloud Technology and Services
description: Are you ready to take your AWS skills to the next level? Look no further than our comprehensive AWS Cloud Technology and Services course designed for anyone wanting to try their hands on the AWS cloud offerings. You will dive deep into a spectrum of AWS services, from optimizing compute resources to uncovering the nuances of AWS storage solutions, database management, networking services, analytics, machine learning, and beyond. With interactive exercises and real-world examples, you'll gain hands-on experience using the AWS console, preparing you for AWS certifications.

parts.title: AWS Compute Services
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll dive into the core AWS compute services, starting with Amazon EC2 for scalable cloud computing. You'll explore how to optimize instances, use load balancing and auto-scaling to enhance performance, and learn about serverless options like AWS Lambda and Fargate for event-driven applications.

parts.title: AWS Databases, Networking, and Storage
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll explore AWS database services like RDS, DynamoDB, and MemoryDB. You'll also learn how to migrate databases to AWS using tools like Database Migration Service and AWS Snow Family. Finally, we'll cover essential networking services and other storage solutions.

parts.title: AWS Machine Learning, AI, Analytics, and Beyond
parts.description: Begin by delving into pre-trained artificial intelligence services,machine learning frameworks, and analytics tools. Finally, round out your understanding of AWS architecture by learning about various secondary service categories.

proficiency.DS: The course covers AWS database services, storage solutions, and data migration, aligning with the intermediate level's focus on combining datasets, automating data cleaning, and handling structured/unstructured data.

Hands-on experience with AWS compute services, serverless options, and scripting for cloud resource management matches the intermediate proficiency in implementing functions, using libraries, and automating tasks.

The course introduces pre-trained AI services and machine learning frameworks on AWS, which fits the foundational level's requirement to apply basic ML algorithms and use open-source libraries for basic models.
Exposure to AWS cloud project workflows and resource management supports foundational project management skills, such as assisting in planning tasks and understanding project timelines.

title: Financial Forecasting in Python
description: In Financial Forecasting in Python, you will step into the role of CFO and learn how to advise a board of directors on key metrics while building a financial forecast, the basics of income statements and balance sheets, and cleaning messy financial data. During the course, you will examine real-life datasets from Netflix, Tesla, and Ford, using the pandas package. Following the course, you will be able to calculate financial metrics, work with assumptions and variances, and build your own forecast in Python!

parts.title: Income statements
parts.description: In this chapter, we will learn the basics of financial statements, with a specific focus on the income statement, which provides details on our sales, costs, and profits. We will learn how to calculate profitability metrics and finish off what we have learned by building our profit forecast for Tesla!

parts.title: Balance sheet and forecast ratios
parts.description: In this chapter, we will learn a bit more about the balance sheet, covering assets and liabilities and specific ratios to help evaluate the financial health and efficiency of a company, as well as how these ratios can assist us in building a great forecast.

parts.title: Formatting raw data, managing dates and financial periods
parts.description: We have gotten a basic understanding of income statements and balance sheets. However, consolidating data for forecasting is complex, so in this chapter, we will look at some basic tools to help solve some of the complexities specifically relating to finance - working with dates and different financial periods, and formatting our raw data into the correct format for financial forecasting.

parts.title: Assumptions and variances in forecasts
parts.description: In this chapter, we will be exploring two more aspects to creating a good forecast. First, we will look at assumptions, what drives them and what happens when an assumption changes? Next, we will look at variances, as a forecast is built at one point in time, but what happens when the actual results do not correspond to our forecast? We need to build a sensitive forecast that can be sensitive to changes in both assumptions and take into account variances, and this is what we will explore in this chapter.

topic.name: Applied Finance
topic.description: The finance community has been one of the eager to embrace data science. From stock market predictions, to asset pricing and calculating the probability of loan defaults, the applications are nearly endless!

proficiency.DS: The course teaches data manipulation and forecasting using Python and pandas, requiring learners to implement functions and work with real datasets, aligning with intermediate programming proficiency.
Learners clean and format messy financial data, manage dates and periods, and consolidate raw data for forecasting, matching intermediate-level data processing skills.
The course focuses on interpreting financial statements, calculating business metrics, and aligning forecasts with business objectives, which fits the intermediate business acumen level.

title: Python for MATLAB Users
description: Python is a versatile programming language that is becoming more and more popular for doing data science. Companies worldwide are using Python to harvest insights from their data and get a competitive edge. This course focuses on helping Matlab users learn to use Python specifically for data science. You will quickly learn how to migrate from Matlab to Python for data analysis and visualization. Learn the fundamentals of Python syntax, how to use numpy arrays to store and manipulate data. You will learn how to use matplotlib to discover trends, correlations, and patterns in real datasets, including bicycle traffic in the city of Seattle and avocado prices across the United States.

parts.title: From MATLAB to Python
parts.description: This chapter gets you started moving from MATLAB to Python. You'll learn about some of the similarities and differences between MATLAB and Python, how to use methods and packages, and be introduced to the popular NumPy package.

parts.title: NumPy and Matplotlib
parts.description: In this chapter, you will build on your new NumPy knowledge. You will dive into NumPy arrays, the Python analog to matrices by performing mathematical operations and indexing. You will also begin to explore another important Python data structure, the list, and then round out the chapter by making customs plots of your arrays using Matplotlib.

parts.title: Dictionaries and pandas
parts.description: This chapter introduces some powerful Python data structures: the dictionary and the pandas DataFrame. You will learn to create dictionaries by setting key-value pairs, and view then how to view and modify your dictionary. Then you will be introduced to one of the most important packages in the Pythonista's toolbox, pandas. Specifically, you'll focus on the pandas' structure, the DataFrame, which organizes tabular data in an easily accessible way. Lastly, you'll learn how to transform different data types into DataFrames to make your data easier to work with.

parts.title: Control Flow and Loops
parts.description: You'll finish the course by controlling your  Python flow. You will learn how to iterate through different Python data structures using for loops. You will also learn about Python contingencies using if, else, and elif and the Python comparison operators (greater than, less than, etc.) that will decide which lines of your code will be executed. Lastly, you'll circle back to NumPy arrays by using Python comparison operators to filter your arrays.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist's toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course teaches Python fundamentals, including syntax, data structures (lists, arrays, dictionaries), control flow, and basic data manipulation, which aligns with foundational programming skills for data science.
Learners are introduced to loading, transforming, and organizing data using pandas DataFrames and NumPy arrays, matching foundational data processing competencies.
The course covers using matplotlib to create basic plots and visualize trends and patterns, which fits foundational data visualization skills.

title: Case Studies: Network Analysis in R
description: Now that you're familiar with the basics of network analysis it's time to see how to apply those concepts to large real-world data sets. You'll work through three different case studies, each building on your previous work. These case studies are working with the kinds of data you'll see in both academic and industry settings. We'll explore some of the computational and visualization challenges you'll face and how to overcome them. Your knowledge of igraph will continue to grow, but we'll also leverage other visualization libraries that will help you bring your visualizations to the web.

parts.title: Exploring graphs through time
parts.description: In this chapter you'll explore a subset of an Amazon purchase graph. You'll build on what you've already learned, finding important products and discovering what drives purchases. You'll also examine how graphs can change through time by looking at the graph during different time periods.

parts.title: How do people talk about R on Twitter?
parts.description: In this lesson you'll explore some Twitter data about R by looking at conversations using '#rstats'.  First you'll look at the raw data and think about how you want to build your graph.  There's a number of ways to do this, and we'll cover two ways: retweets and mentions.  You'll build those graphs and then compare them on a number of metrics.

parts.title: Bike sharing in Chicago
parts.description: In this chapter you will analyze data from a Chicago bike sharing network.  We will build on the concepts already covered in the introductory course, and add a few new ones to handle graphs with weighted edges. You will also start with data in a slightly more raw form and cover how to build your graph up from a data source you might find.

parts.title: Other ways to visualize graph data
parts.description: So far everything we've done has been using plotting from igraph. It provides many powerful ways to plot your graph data.  However many people prefer interacting with other plotting frameworks like ggplot2, or even interactive frameworks like d3.js. In this lesson you'll look at other plotting libraries that build on the ggplot2 framework. You'll also look at other non-"hairball" type methods like hive plots, as well as building interactive and animated plots.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course applies advanced network analysis to real-world datasets, requiring the use of complex statistical concepts, interpretation of graph metrics, and the ability to handle large, dynamic data structures-skills expected at the advanced proficiency level.

Learners use multiple visualization libraries (including web-based and interactive frameworks) to create sophisticated, non-standard graph visualizations, demonstrating advanced skills in integrating and communicating complex data patterns.

The course builds on prior programming knowledge in R, requiring the use of libraries like igraph and ggplot2, and introduces handling of raw data and graph construction, aligning with intermediate programming proficiency.
Students start with raw data, perform cleaning, transformation, and construct graphs from real-world sources, reflecting intermediate data processing skills.

title: Introduction to Anomaly Detection in R
description: Are you concerned about inaccurate or suspicious records in your data, but not sure where to start? An anomaly detection algorithm could help! Anomaly detection is a collection of techniques designed to identify unusual data points, and are crucial for detecting fraud and for protecting computer networks from malicious activity. In this course, you'll explore statistical tests for identifying outliers, and learn to use sophisticated anomaly scoring algorithms like the local outlier factor and isolation forest. You'll apply anomaly detection algorithms to identify unusual wines in the UCI Wine quality dataset and also to detect cases of thyroid disease from abnormal hormone measurements.

parts.title: Statistical outlier detection
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn how numerical and graphical summaries can be used to informally assess whether data contain unusual points.  You'll use a statistical procedure called Grubbs' test to check whether a point is an outlier, and learn about the Seasonal-Hybrid ESD algorithm, which can help identify outliers when the data are a time series.

parts.title: Distance and density based anomaly detection
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn how to calculate the  k-nearest neighbors distance and the local outlier factor, which are used to construct continuous anomaly scores for each data point when the data have multiple features.   You'll learn the difference between local and global anomalies and how the two algorithms can help in each case.

parts.title: Isolation forest
parts.description: k-nearest neighbors distance and local outlier factor use the distance or relative density of the nearest neighbors to score each point.  In this chapter, you'll explore an alternative tree-based approach called an isolation forest, which is a fast and robust method of detecting anomalies that measures how easily points can be separated by randomly splitting the data into smaller and smaller regions.

parts.title: Comparing performance
parts.description: You've now been introduced to a few different algorithms for anomaly scoring. In this final chapter, you'll learn to compare the detection performance of the algorithms in instances where labeled anomalies are available.  You'll learn to calculate and interpret the precision and recall statistics for an anomaly score, and how to adapt the algorithms so they can accommodate data with categorical features.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: The course covers statistical outlier detection, hypothesis testing (Grubbs' test), and introduces multivariate techniques like local outlier factor, aligning with intermediate proficiency in applying inferential statistics and multivariate analysis.

Learners apply machine learning algorithms such as isolation forest and local outlier factor for anomaly detection, and compare model performance using precision and recall, matching intermediate-level skills in applying AI techniques to real-world problems and evaluating models.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy
description: Unlock the power of AI strategy in the data-driven world. This course delves into the interconnectedness of business, data, and AI strategies, equipping you with the knowledge to create a strong strategic framework. You'll learn to differentiate AI from traditional software, set realistic business goals, and assess ROI for AI projects. Discover the key components of a successful AI strategy, emphasizing innovation and risk assessment. Finally, explore efficient AI scaling and the role of executive sponsors and champions in driving AI adoption. Get ready to navigate the AI landscape with confidence.

parts.title: Fundamentals of AI Strategy
parts.description:
The chapter underpins the intricate relationships between business, data, and AI strategies. It then goes deeper into how an effective AI strategy begins with a clear vision and the role of a focused action plan in driving an organization's strategic objectives.

You will also learn the skills that go into making a successful AI strategist, outlining their responsibilities and contributions towards achieving the business goals.

parts.title: Designing a Winning AI Strategy
parts.description:
This chapter sharpens the business acumen by distinguishing AI software from traditional software, ensuring the effective use of resources for pertinent business challenges. It further explains the key business drivers in identifying the most impactful AI initiatives and shares how to set the right AI goals. 
Alongside explaining the significance of ROI, learners will understand the challenges and drivers of assessing ROI.

parts.title: Components of AI Strategy
parts.description: This chapter explains different components of a successful AI strategy, such as innovation and building the right culture for high-performing teams.  It also underscores the importance of AI literacy, covering the pivotal do's and don'ts of AI usage.  While innovation is essential, understanding the potential AI-associated risks and asking the right questions is crucial to building a robust risk assessment framework for AI.

parts.title: Time for Action
parts.description:
In this chapter, we discuss the role of feasibility workshops and emphasize initiating a focused PoC to gauge AI's potential before a full-scale rollout. We will also highlight what it takes to build scalable AI systems and the significance of MLOps in scaling it right.

Ultimately, the chapter underscores the influence of executive sponsors and AI champions in fostering AI adoption.

proficiency.DS: The course focuses on developing and implementing AI strategies, aligning AI initiatives with business goals, scaling AI solutions, and championing responsible AI adoption-key aspects of lead-level proficiency.
Emphasizes integrating AI strategy with business objectives, assessing ROI, and guiding executive decision-making, which aligns with lead-level business acumen in data-driven organizations.
Covers strategic planning, risk assessment, resource allocation, and executive sponsorship for AI projects, reflecting lead-level project management competencies.

title: HR Analytics: Predicting Employee Churn in R
description: Organizational growth largely depends on staff retention. Losing employees frequently impacts the morale of the organization and hiring new employees is more expensive than retaining existing ones. Good news is that organizations can increase employee retention using data-driven intervention strategies. This course focuses on data acquisition from multiple HR sources, exploring and deriving new features, building and validating a logistic regression model, and finally, show how to calculate ROI for a potential retention strategy.

parts.title: Introduction
parts.description: This chapter begins with a general introduction to employee churn/turnover and reasons for turnover as shared by employees. You will learn how to calculate turnover rate and explore turnover rate across different dimensions. You will also identify talent segments for your analysis and bring together relevant data from multiple HR data sources to derive more useful insights.

parts.title: Feature Engineering
parts.description: In this chapter, you will create new variables from existing data to explain employee turnover. You will analyze compensation data and create compa-ratio to measure pay equity of all employees. To identify the most important variables influencing turnover, you will use the concept of Information Value (IV).

parts.title: Predicting Turnover
parts.description: In this chapter, you will build a logistic regression model to predict turnover by taking into account multicollinearity among variables.

parts.title: Model Validation, HR Interventions, and ROI
parts.description: In this chapter, you will calculate the accuracy of your model and categorize employees into specific risk buckets. You will then formulate an intervention strategy and calculate the ROI for this strategy.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course covers data acquisition from multiple HR sources and feature engineering, aligning with intermediate proficiency in combining datasets, automating cleaning tasks, and deriving variables for analysis.
Building and interpreting a logistic regression model, handling multicollinearity, and using Information Value for variable selection matches intermediate-level statistical modeling and analysis.
The course introduces logistic regression as a basic supervised machine learning algorithm, suitable for foundational proficiency in applying basic ML models.
Calculating ROI for retention strategies and linking model insights to business outcomes demonstrates intermediate-level ability to align data science work with business objectives.

title: Dashboard Design Concepts
description: Dashboard Design Concepts is a comprehensive course designed for data-driven individuals who want to learn how to turn data into insights and impact the decision-making process. You will become familiar with the fundamentals of dashboard design, including how to choose the right performance metrics, use data visualization to effectively communicate insights, and design dashboards that drive business success. Whether new to dashboard design or looking to improve your existing skills, this course will provide you with the knowledge and skills you need to create impactful and effective dashboards.

parts.title: The Building Blocks
parts.description: This course begins with introducing the fundamental concepts of dashboard design and structure. You will then learn how to define key measurements for the business performance dashboards and connect them to stakeholders who have an interest in the organization's decisions and goals.

parts.title: Visual Analytics Components
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn about dashboard design and the principles of visual analytics. You'll also look at ways to improve the dashboard via data quality and metadata.

parts.title: Types of Dashboards
parts.description: Chapter 3 introduces dashboard taxonomies. You'll also learn how to choose the right dashboard for particular situations.

parts.title: Dashboard Success and Integration
parts.description: In the final chapter, you'll learn about dashboard software, dashboard checklist, and how to measure the dashboard's success, impact, and adoption.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: This course covers the fundamentals of dashboard design, including basic visual analytics, choosing performance metrics, and communicating insights, aligning with foundational skills in data visualization.
The course emphasizes using dashboards to communicate data insights effectively to stakeholders, which matches foundational technical communication skills.
By teaching how to select key business metrics and connect dashboards to organizational goals, the course supports foundational business acumen in data-driven decision-making.

title: Data Visualization in Tableau
description:
Data visualization is one of the most desired skills for data analysts, allowing them to communicate insights in an understandable and impactful way. This course covers a range of data visualization skills using Tableau, allowing you to better present your findings.
If you're interested in data visualization or if you struggle to make your insights "land" with your stakeholders, then this course is for you.

You'll start by revisiting some of the core principles of visualizing data before learning the basics of Tableau, looking at how you can use the software to transform your data into something impactful.
You'll cover some of the data visualization best practices, as well as focus on how to make your Tableau dashboards interactive and appealing. As you progress, you'll explore how to spatial data to chart maps and non-geo use cases.

Communicating your insights visually will increase the understanding and retention of your information and create more impact. In this course, you will progress from basic data visualization skills toward advanced and custom-made charts, including Waffle charts, DNA charts, and a Sankey charts.
You'll learn how to accentuate insights and how to render information beautiful and useful at the same time. And all this while working on interesting datasets such as IMDB Movies or Airbnb data. Let's visualize!

parts.title: Start to Visualize
parts.description: In this chapter, we revisit the core principles of data visualization and learn how to use Tableau to turn your data into informative, useful, and attractive charts, from basic to more intermediate ones.

parts.title: Best Practices in Data Visualization
parts.description: Having already explored the first steps in data visualization, you will go through a practical course on best charting practices and learn the dos and don'ts. You will also focus on increasing the interactivity of our visualizations by using dashboard actions to your advantage.

parts.title: Maps and Spatial Visualizations
parts.description: This chapter focuses on map charting, starting with classic geospatial visualizations and progressing to non-geo use cases, such as visualizing schematics, processes, or traffic. You will also learn how to work with spatial data types and how to beautify your maps.

parts.title: Information is Beautiful - Expanding your Charting Toolbox
parts.description: In the final Chapter, you will focus on expanding your visualization toolbox with more fancy charts. You will learn how to build, among others, a Waffle chart, DNA chart, and a Sankey chart, and learn how to style them and assemble them into a brand-consistent infographic or dashboard with intuitive navigation. Finally, you will pick a few takeaways from the analysis and assemble them into a data story.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces core principles of data visualization, basic chart creation, and the use of Tableau to present simple insights, aligning with foundational proficiency in creating clear, basic visuals for technical and non-technical audiences.

The course covers best practices, dashboard interactivity, spatial visualizations, and more complex chart types, matching the intermediate level's focus on complex visualizations, adapting communication for stakeholders, and linking insights to business objectives.

Advanced and custom chart creation (e.g., Waffle, DNA, Sankey charts), dashboard assembly, and data storytelling in the course correspond to advanced proficiency, which involves integrating multiple data sources and crafting actionable, sophisticated visuals and narratives.
The course emphasizes presenting insights visually and communicating findings in an understandable way, supporting foundational skills in summarizing and clearly presenting basic analysis results.

By teaching how to structure narratives, adapt visuals for different audiences, and assemble data stories, the course aligns with intermediate proficiency in organizing insights, creating complex visuals, and tailoring communication to stakeholders.

title: Data Preparation in Excel
description:
In this course, you'll learn how to prepare and clean raw data in Excel worksheets.  You'll learn to bring in data from different sources and prepare the data by filtering, deduping, and organizing your columns and rows to ensure subsequent analysis tasks are done as efficiently as possible.
As well as the built-in features Excel offers, you will learn to use different functions to handle and manipulate dates and text strings. You will be introduced to logical functions that will allow you to create new flags and categories within your raw data while understanding how different logical functions can be combined in nested formulas. You will also understand how to use lookup functions in Excel to bring in data from different sheets and identify specific results within large datasets. Finally, you will get your first glimpse of PivotTables - a powerful Excel feature that allows you to summarize and analyze large volumes of data using dynamic tables.

parts.title: Starting Data Preparation in Excel
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn different ways to source and import your raw data into Excel. You will then start your preparation of raw data by removing duplicates added in error and filling in the missing parts of your data that will help you prepare the best dataset for analytical use.

parts.title: Functions for Data Preparation
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn how to use text category functions to combine text strings with useful variables for better analysis. You will also utilize some of Excel's date and time functions, taking simple date columns to a new level.

parts.title: Conditional Formulas
