proficiency.DS: The course covers advanced statistical techniques such as time series modeling (ARIMA), price elasticity, regression, and hierarchical forecasting, which align with the advanced proficiency level requiring expertise in complex models and their application to real-world business problems.

The course teaches how to identify drivers of demand and apply forecasting to business scenarios, matching the intermediate level's focus on aligning data science projects with business objectives and communicating findings for business decisions.

title: Mixture Models in R
description: Mixture modeling is a way of representing populations when we are interested in their heterogeneity. Mixture models use familiar probability distributions (e.g. Gaussian, Poisson, Binomial) to provide a convenient yet formal statistical framework for clustering and classification. Unlike standard clustering approaches, we can estimate the probability of belonging to a cluster and make inference about the sub-populations. For example, in the context of marketing, you may want to cluster different customer groups and find their respective probabilities of purchasing specific products to better target them with custom promotions. When applying natural language processing to a large set of documents, you may want to cluster documents into different topics and understand how important each topic is across each document. In this course, you will learn what Mixture Models are, how they are estimated, and when it is appropriate to apply them!

parts.title: Introduction to Mixture Models
parts.description: In this chapter, you will be introduced to fundamental concepts in model-based clustering and how this approach differs from other clustering techniques. You will learn the generating process of Gaussian Mixture Models as well as how to visualize the clusters.

parts.title: Structure of Mixture Models and Parameters Estimation
parts.description: In this chapter, you will be introduced to the main structure of Mixture Models, how to address different data with this approach and how to estimate the parameters involved. To accomplish the estimation, you will learn an iterative method called Expectation-Maximization algorithm.

parts.title: Mixture of Gaussians with `flexmix`
parts.description: This chapter shows how to fit Gaussian Mixture Models in 1 and 2 dimensions with `flexmix` package. The data used is formed by 10.000 observations of people with their weight, height, body mass index and informed gender.

parts.title: Mixture Models Beyond Gaussians
parts.description: In this module, you will learn how Mixture Models extends to consider probability distributions different from the Gaussian and how these models are fitted with `flexmix`. The datasets used are handwritten digits images and the number of crimes in Chicago city. For the first dataset you will find clusters that summarize the handwritten digits and for the second dataset, you will find clusters of communities where is more or less dangerous to live in.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced statistical techniques such as mixture models, model-based clustering, and the Expectation-Maximization algorithm, which are suitable for solving complex problems and interpreting sub-populations in data.

The course teaches probabilistic clustering and classification using mixture models, including practical implementation in R, which aligns with advanced proficiency in machine learning for handling heterogeneous data and inference.

title: Software Engineering Principles in Python
description: Data scientists can experience huge benefits by learning concepts from the field of software engineering, allowing them to more easily reutilize their code and share it with collaborators. In this course, you'll learn all about the important ideas of modularity, documentation, & automated testing, and you'll see how they can help you solve Data Science problems quicker and in a way that will make future you happy. You'll even get to use your acquired software engineering chops to write your very own Python package for performing text analytics.

parts.title: Software Engineering & Data Science
parts.description: Why should you as a Data Scientist care about Software Engineering concepts?  Here we'll cover specific Software Engineering concepts and how these important ideas can revolutionize your Data Science workflow!

parts.title: Writing a Python Module
parts.description: Become a fully fledged Python package developer by writing your first package!  You'll learn how to structure and write Python code that you can be installed, used, and distributed just like famous packages such as NumPy and Pandas.

parts.title: Utilizing Classes
parts.description: Object Oriented Programming is a staple of Python development.  By leveraging classes and inheritance your Python package will become a much more powerful tool for your users.

parts.title: Maintainability
parts.description: You've now written a fully functional Python package for text analysis!  To make maintaining your project as easy as possible we'll leverage best practices around concepts such as documentation and unit testing.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist' toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: The course covers object-oriented programming, modularity, and writing Python packages, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in designing and implementing functions and classes, and applying programming principles for data manipulation.

The emphasis on code optimization, maintainability, documentation, and automated testing matches advanced proficiency, which includes applying software engineering best practices and developing scalable, maintainable code.

The course teaches documentation, modular code organization, and collaborative practices, which are key aspects of intermediate code management such as organizing repositories and documenting code for reproducibility.

By focusing on maintainability, documentation standards, and automated testing, the course supports advanced proficiency in enforcing coding standards and mentoring others in code management practices.

title: Introduction to Data Visualization with Plotly in Python
description: Producing high-quality, interactive visualizations historically required complex code, extensive time, and effort. Not anymore. In this course, you'll learn how to create publication-quality graphs harnessing the power of JavaScript, without leaving the comfort of the Python programming language we all love. You'll create, style, and customize a variety of stunning, interactive graphs- using datasets ranging from stock prices to basketball team stats, and even penguin beak sizes! Using the Plotly charting library, you'll also learn to customize interactivity such as hover information, range sliders, custom buttons, and even drop-downs that reactively change the visualization. Are you ready to level-up your data visualization skills?

parts.title: Introduction to Plotly
parts.description: Enter the world of Plotly! In this first chapter, you'll learn different ways to create plots and receive an introduction to univariate plots. You'll then build several popular plot types, including box plots and histograms, and discover how to style them using the Plotly color options.

parts.title: Customizing Plots
parts.description: Add to your Plotly toolkit as you explore and implement bivariate plots. Next, you'll explore how to customize your plots to make them look amazing with annotations, hover information, legends, and custom axis titles and scales.

parts.title: Advanced Customization
parts.description: Take your Plotly graphs to the next level with more advanced customizations. Through hands-on exercises, you'll learn how to layer multiple interactive chart types in the same plot (such as a bar chart with line chart over the top). You'll then create time-series selectors, such as year to date (YTD), to help you zoom in and out of your line charts.

parts.title: Advanced Interactivity
parts.description: In this final chapter, you'll harness Plotly' advanced user interactivity as you learn how to create buttons, dropdowns, and sliders that change everything from graph types to annotations and much more. Take your Plotly skills to the next level and build truly interactive user experiences.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces basic concepts of data visualization, including creating and styling simple plots like box plots and histograms, which aligns with foundational proficiency in presenting data using basic charts and graphs.

The course covers customizing visualizations, creating bivariate plots, and adding interactivity such as hover information and legends, matching intermediate proficiency in creating complex visualizations and adapting communication for different audiences.

Advanced chapters teach layering multiple chart types, building interactive dashboards with buttons and sliders, and integrating multiple data sources, which fits advanced proficiency in integrating complex visuals and crafting actionable data stories.

title: Visualizing Time Series Data in R
description: As the saying goes, "A chart is worth a thousand words". This is why visualization is the most used and powerful way to get a better understanding of your data. After this course you will have a very good overview of R time series visualisation capabilities and you will be able to better decide which model to choose for subsequent analysis. You will be able to also convey the message you want to deliver in an efficient and beautiful way.

parts.title: R Time Series Visualization Tools
parts.description: This chapter will introduce you to basic R time series visualization tools.

parts.title: Univariate Time Series
parts.description: Univariate plots are designed to learn as much as possible about the distribution, central tendency and spread of the data at hand. In this chapter you will be presented with some visual tools used to diagnose univariate times series.

parts.title: Multivariate Time Series
parts.description: What to do if you have to deal with multivariate time series? In this chapter, you will learn how to identify patterns in the distribution, central tendency and spread over pairs or groups of data.

parts.title: Case study: Visually Selecting a Stock That Improves Your Existing Portfolio
parts.description: Let's put everything you learned so far in practice! Imagine you already own a portfolio of stocks and you have some spare cash to invest, how can you wisely select a new stock to invest your additional cash? Analyzing the statistical properties of individual stocks vs. an existing portfolio is a good way of approaching the problem.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces basic R time series visualization tools and univariate plots, matching foundational skills in presenting and understanding data using simple charts and graphs.
It covers multivariate time series visualization and pattern identification, aligning with intermediate proficiency in creating complex visualizations and organizing insights for different audiences.
The course applies statistical concepts like distribution, central tendency, and spread in time series, which matches intermediate-level skills in interpreting and visualizing statistical patterns.

The case study on stock selection demonstrates the use of data visualization and statistical analysis to inform business decisions, aligning with intermediate proficiency in applying data insights to business problems.

title: Reports in Power BI
description: In this advanced course, take your Power BI visualizations up a level with the skills you already have. You'll learn complex alternative data storytelling techniques to simply building dashboards, including buttons and bookmarks to create more interactive visualizations. Customize the user experience by drillthrough filters and emoji, and learn how to tweak the Q&A feature for personalized reports.

parts.title: Power BI Reports
parts.description: You've built compelling dashboards in Power BI, but that's not all you can do. In this first chapter, you'll learn the differences between reports and dashboards. Next, you'll add drill-through filters to your Power BI report to increase user interaction.

parts.title: Bookmarks, Buttons and Navigation
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn to add interactive story-telling to your reports with bookmarks, buttons and navigation.

parts.title: Customizing the Experience
parts.description: Now it's time to customize the look and feel of buttons and tables using unicode and emojis in tables. You'll also change how visuals interact with one another and see how conditional formatting can be a powerful tool for your report.

parts.title: Customize a Report with Q&A
parts.description: Asking a question in natural language is sometimes the quickest way to get an answer from your data. In this chapter, you'll learn how to add and tweak the Q&A visual to your Power BI Reports.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced Power BI features such as interactive storytelling, drillthrough filters, bookmarks, and custom Q&A, aligning with the advanced proficiency level where users integrate multiple data sources and variables into cohesive, actionable visuals and stories.

The course teaches complex storytelling techniques and customization for user experience, matching the advanced level of technical communication which requires integrating data into actionable visuals and explaining complex patterns and trends.

title: Streaming Concepts
description:
Streaming is a huge aspect of the data world right now and is being used by nearly every industry from manufacturing to healthcare. Would you like to learn more about the general concepts behind data pipelines and how the processes work?

This course provides a general introduction to streaming concepts including batching, queuing, and stream processing along with where they fit into data processing frameworks. It covers real-world examples of how streaming is implemented in production. It is designed as a general introduction to these concepts and does not require an extensive background in data processing.

parts.title: Methods for Processing Data
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll be given an introduction to basic concepts in batch data processing, revolving around implementation, scaling, and potential challenges during use.

parts.title: Intro to Streaming
parts.description: Here, you'll learn about the basics of streaming, event-based data processing, and the advantages  over traditional batch-based data processing.

parts.title: Streaming Systems
parts.description: This chapter introduces the concepts behind modern streaming systems, how to scale them, and some of the issues found in using streaming processes.

parts.title: Real-World Use Cases
parts.description: In this final chapter, you'll learn about common streaming systems and consider the implementation of streaming data processing in different use cases.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces basic concepts of batch and stream data processing, including implementation and scaling, which aligns with foundational proficiency in understanding and applying basic data processing methods.

title: Database Design
description: A good database design is crucial for a high-performance application. Just like you wouldn't start building a house without the benefit of a blueprint, you need to think about how your data will be stored beforehand. Taking the time to design a database saves time and frustration later on, and a well-designed database ensures ease of access and retrieval of information. While choosing a design, a lot of considerations have to be accounted for. In this course, you'll learn how to process, store, and organize data in an efficient way. You'll see how to structure data through normalization and present your data with views. Finally, you'll learn how to manage your database and all of this will be done on a variety of datasets from book sales, car rentals, to music reviews.

parts.title: Processing, Storing, and Organizing Data
parts.description: Start your journey into database design by learning about the two approaches to data processing, OLTP and OLAP. In this first chapter, you'll also get familiar with the different forms data can be stored in and learn the basics of data modeling.

parts.title: Database Schemas and Normalization
parts.description: In this chapter, you will take your data modeling skills to the next level. You'll learn to implement star and snowflake schemas, recognize the importance of normalization and see how to normalize databases to different extents.

parts.title: Database Views
parts.description: Get ready to work with views! In this chapter, you will learn how to create and query views. On top of that, you'll master more advanced capabilities to manage them and end by identifying the difference between materialized and non-materialized views.

parts.title: Database Management
parts.description: This final chapter ends with some database management-related topics. You will learn how to grant database access based on user roles, how to partition tables into smaller pieces, what to keep in mind when integrating data, and which DBMS fits your business needs best.

proficiency.DS: The course covers database normalization, schema design, and management, which align with intermediate proficiency in structuring, organizing, and maintaining data for analysis and business needs.
Learners process, store, and organize data efficiently, including handling different data forms and integrating datasets, matching intermediate-level data processing competencies.

The course addresses choosing DBMS based on business needs and integrating data for business applications, reflecting intermediate business acumen in aligning technical solutions with organizational goals.

title: Writing Functions in Python
description: You've done your analysis, built your report, and trained a model. What's next? Well, if you want to deploy your model into production, your code will need to be more reliable than exploratory scripts in a Jupyter notebook. Writing Functions in Python will give you a strong foundation in writing complex and beautiful functions so that you can contribute research and engineering skills to your team. You'll learn useful tricks, like how to write context managers and decorators. You'll also learn best practices around how to write maintainable reusable functions with good documentation. They say that people who can do good research and write high-quality code are unicorns. Take this course and discover the magic!

parts.title: Best Practices
parts.description: The goal of this course is to transform you into a Python expert, and so the first chapter starts off with best practices when writing functions. You'll cover docstrings and why they matter and how to know when you need to turn a chunk of code into a function. You will also learn the details of how Python passes arguments to functions, as well as some common gotchas that can cause debugging headaches when calling functions.

parts.title: Context Managers
parts.description: If you've ever seen the "with" keyword in Python and wondered what its deal was, then this is the chapter for you! Context managers are a convenient way to provide connections in Python and guarantee that those connections get cleaned up when you are done using them. This chapter will show you how to use context managers, as well as how to write your own.

parts.title: Decorators
parts.description: Decorators are an extremely powerful concept in Python. They allow you to modify the behavior of a function without changing the code of the function itself. This chapter will lay the foundational concepts needed to thoroughly understand decorators (functions as objects, scope, and closures), and give you a good introduction into how decorators are used and defined. This deep dive into Python internals will set you up to be a superstar Pythonista.

parts.title: More on Decorators
parts.description: Now that you understand how decorators work under the hood, this chapter gives you a bunch of real-world examples of when and how you would write decorators in your own code. You will also learn advanced decorator concepts like how to preserve the metadata of your decorated functions and how to write decorators that take arguments.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist' toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers writing functions, context managers, and decorators in Python, which aligns with intermediate proficiency by teaching object-oriented principles, reusable code, and best practices for maintainability and documentation.

The course delves into advanced Python concepts such as context managers and decorators, code optimization, and writing maintainable code, matching advanced proficiency requirements for implementing complex data structures and software engineering best practices.
Emphasis on documentation, reusable functions, and maintainable code supports intermediate code management skills, including clean code and standardized documentation practices.
The course's focus on best practices, advanced function design, and documentation aligns with advanced code management, promoting reproducibility and adherence to coding standards.

title: Understanding Data Science
description: What is data science, why is it so popular, and why did the Harvard Business Review hail it as the "sexiest job of the 21st century"? In this non-technical course, you'll be introduced to everything you were ever too afraid to ask about this fast-growing and exciting field, without needing to write a single line of code. Through hands-on exercises, you'll learn about the different data scientist roles, foundational topics like A/B testing, time series analysis, and machine learning, and how data scientists extract knowledge and insights from real-world data. So don't be put off by the buzzwords. Start learning, gain skills in this hugely in-demand field, and discover why data science is for everyone!

parts.title: Introduction to Data Science
parts.description: We'll start the course by defining what data science is. We'll cover the data science workflow and how data science is applied to real-world problems. We'll finish the chapter by learning about different roles within the data science field.

parts.title: Data Collection and Storage
parts.description: Now that we understand the data science workflow, we'll dive deeper into the first step: data collection and storage. We'll learn about the different data sources you can draw from, what that data looks like, how to store the data once it's collected, and how a data pipeline can automate the process.

parts.title: Preparation, Exploration, and Visualization
parts.description: Data preparation is fundamental: data scientists spend 80% of their time cleaning and manipulating data, and only 20% of their time actually analyzing it. This chapter will show you how to diagnose problems in your data, deal with missing values and outliers. You will then learn about visualization, another essential tool to both explore your data and convey your findings.

parts.title: Experimentation and Prediction
parts.description: In this final chapter, we'll discuss experimentation and prediction! Beginning with experiments, we'll cover A/B testing, and move on to time series forecasting where we'll learn about predicting future events. Finally, we'll end with machine learning, looking at supervised learning, and clustering.

proficiency.DS: Covers data collection, storage, and pipelines, matching foundational skills in handling and preparing data for analysis.
Introduces A/B testing and time series analysis, aligning with basic statistical concepts and experimental design.
Explains supervised learning and clustering, suitable for foundational understanding of core machine learning techniques.
Teaches basic visualization for data exploration and communication, fitting foundational proficiency in presenting data.
Covers experimentation and hypothesis testing, matching foundational research skills in data science.
Explains how data science applies to real-world problems and business roles, supporting foundational business understanding.

title: Machine Learning with Tree-Based Models in Python
description:
Decision trees are supervised learning models used for problems involving classification and regression. Tree models present a high flexibility that comes at a price: on one hand, trees are able to capture complex non-linear relationships; on the other hand, they are prone to memorizing the noise present in a dataset. By aggregating the predictions of trees that are trained differently, ensemble methods take advantage of the flexibility of trees while reducing their tendency to memorize noise. Ensemble methods are used across a variety of fields and have a proven track record of winning many machine learning competitions.
In this course, you'll learn how to use Python to train decision trees and tree-based models with the user-friendly scikit-learn machine learning library. You'll understand the advantages and shortcomings of trees and demonstrate how ensembling can alleviate these shortcomings, all while practicing on real-world datasets. Finally, you'll also understand how to tune the most influential hyperparameters in order to get the most out of your models.

parts.title: Classification and Regression Trees
parts.description: Classification and Regression Trees (CART) are a set of supervised learning models used for problems involving classification and regression. In this chapter, you'll be introduced to the CART algorithm.

parts.title: The Bias-Variance Tradeoff
parts.description: The bias-variance tradeoff is one of the fundamental concepts in supervised machine learning. In this chapter, you'll understand how to diagnose the problems of overfitting and underfitting. You'll also be introduced to the concept of ensembling where the predictions of several models are aggregated to produce predictions that are more robust.

parts.title: Bagging and Random Forests
parts.description: Bagging is an ensemble method involving training the same algorithm many times using different subsets sampled from the training data. In this chapter, you'll understand how bagging can be used to create a tree ensemble. You'll also learn how the random forests algorithm can lead to further ensemble diversity through randomization at the level of each split in the trees forming the ensemble.

parts.title: Boosting
parts.description: Boosting refers to an ensemble method in which several models are trained sequentially with each model learning from the errors of its predecessors. In this chapter, you'll be introduced to the two boosting methods of AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting.

parts.title: Model Tuning
parts.description: The hyperparameters of a machine learning model are parameters that are not learned from data. They should be set prior to fitting the model to the training set. In this chapter, you'll learn how to tune the hyperparameters of a tree-based model using grid search cross validation.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced tree-based machine learning methods, including ensemble techniques (bagging, random forests, boosting), bias-variance tradeoff, and hyperparameter tuning, which align with the advanced proficiency level's expectation to apply and fine-tune complex algorithms and evaluate model performance.

Learners use Python and scikit-learn to implement and tune machine learning models, matching the intermediate proficiency level's requirement to design and implement functions using libraries for data manipulation and analysis.
The course addresses bias-variance tradeoff, overfitting, underfitting, and model evaluation, which are key advanced statistical concepts required for rigorous model assessment and selection.

title: Data Connections in Power BI
description: Data connections are an essential part of Power BI. In this course, you will be introduced to the many different options for connecting to data. You'll learn the differences between Power BI Desktop and Power BI Service when it comes to data connections. You'll also learn about the different ways that Power BI stores data when connecting to a source, and how you are able to amend connections after they have been made. Finally, you'll learn how you can use parameters and M Language in Power BI Desktop to level up your handling of data import processes.

parts.title: Data Connections in Power BI
parts.description: Whenever using Power BI, a data connection is required. In this chapter, you'll be introduced to commonly used data connections for Power BI. You'll also get an insight into the data connection features of Power BI Serice while finally having the chance to carry out your own database connection.

parts.title: Databases and More
parts.description: It's time to take the next step in your data connections journey! Through hands-on exercises, you will interact with a new database connection and learn how different settings can be changed. You'll also learn about the different storage modes offered by Power BI and how you can use coding to alter the import process.

parts.title: Data Source Settings
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn how to create parameters that can be used for incremental refreshes. You will also implement an incremental refresh on your data connection. Finally, you'll understand how M Language can be utilized to tackle issues with your data import processes.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today' most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: This course introduces basic concepts of connecting to data sources, handling data imports, and understanding storage modes in Power BI, which aligns with foundational data management skills such as loading and preparing data for analysis.

The course covers using parameters and M Language in Power BI Desktop, which involves scripting and automation for data import processes, matching intermediate programming proficiency in data manipulation and automation.

title: Web Scraping in Python
description: The ability to build tools capable of retrieving and parsing information stored across the internet has been and continues to be valuable in many veins of data science. In this course, you will learn to navigate and parse html code, and build tools to crawl websites automatically. Although our scraping will be conducted using the versatile Python library scrapy, many of the techniques you learn in this course can be applied to other popular Python libraries as well, including BeautifulSoup and Selenium. Upon the completion of this course, you will have a strong mental model of html structure, will be able to build tools to parse html code and access desired information, and create a simple scrapy spiders to crawl the web at scale.

parts.title: Introduction to HTML
parts.description: Learn the structure of HTML. We begin by explaining why web scraping can be a valuable addition to your data science toolbox and then delving into some basics of HTML. We end the chapter by giving a brief introduction on XPath notation, which is used to navigate the elements within HTML code.

parts.title: XPaths and Selectors
parts.description: Leverage XPath syntax to explore scrapy selectors. Both of these concepts will move you towards being able to scrape an HTML document.

parts.title: CSS Locators, Chaining, and Responses
parts.description: Learn CSS Locator syntax and begin playing with the idea of chaining together CSS Locators with XPath. We also introduce Response objects, which behave like Selectors but give us extra tools to mobilize our scraping efforts across multiple websites.

parts.title: Spiders
parts.description: Learn to create web crawlers with scrapy. These scrapy spiders will crawl the web through multiple pages, following links to scrape each of those pages automatically according to the procedures we've learned in the previous chapters.

proficiency.DS: This course teaches automated data collection and parsing from web sources using Python libraries, which aligns with intermediate-level skills in combining, cleaning, and transforming data from diverse sources for analysis.

Learners build Python tools using libraries like scrapy, BeautifulSoup, and Selenium, applying object-oriented programming and automation for data retrieval and manipulation, matching intermediate programming proficiency.

title: Intermediate Predictive Analytics in Python
description: Building good models only succeeds if you have a decent base table to start with. In this course you will learn how to construct a good base table, create variables and prepare your data for modeling. We finish with advanced topics on the matter.

parts.title: Crucial base table concepts
parts.description: In this chapter you will learn how to construct the foundations of your base table, namely the population and the target.

parts.title: Creating variables
parts.description: You will learn how to add variables to the base table that you can use to predict the target.

parts.title: Data preparation
parts.description: Once you derived variables from the raw data, it is time to clean the data and prepare it for modeling. In this Chapter we discuss the steps that need to be taken to make your data modeling-ready.

parts.title: Advanced base table concepts
parts.description: In some cases, the target or variables change heavily with the seasons. You will learn how you can deal with seasonality by adding different snapshots to the base table.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course covers combining datasets, creating variables, cleaning and preparing data for modeling, which matches intermediate data processing skills such as automating cleaning tasks and handling structured/unstructured data.

The course focuses on preparing data for predictive modeling and addresses advanced topics like seasonality, aligning with intermediate machine learning proficiency in applying techniques to real-world problems and preparing data for modeling.

The course uses Python for data preparation and variable creation, which fits intermediate programming skills such as using libraries for data manipulation and implementing functions for modeling tasks.

title: Introduction to Databases in Python
description: In this course, you'll learn the basics of using SQL with Python. This will be useful because databases are ubiquitous and data scientists, analysts, and engineers must interact with them constantly. The Python SQL toolkit SQLAlchemy provides an accessible and intuitive way to query, build, and write to essential databases, including SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL.

parts.title: Basics of Relational Databases
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll get acquainted with the fundamentals of relational databases and the relational model for database management. You will learn how to connect to a database and interact with it by writing basic SQL queries, both in raw SQL as well as SQLAlchemy, which provides a Pythonic way of interacting with databases.

parts.title: Applying Filtering, Ordering and Grouping to Queries
parts.description: In this chapter, you will build on your database knowledge by writing more nuanced queries that allow you to filter, order, and count your data- all within the Pythonic framework provided by SQLAlchemy.

parts.title: Advanced SQLAlchemy Queries
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn to perform advanced- and incredibly useful- queries that enable you to interact with your data in powerful ways.

parts.title: Creating and Manipulating your own Databases
parts.description: In the previous chapters, you interacted with existing databases and queried them in different ways. Now, you will learn how to build your own databases and keep them updated.

parts.title: Putting it all together
parts.description: Bring together all of the skills you acquired in the previous chapters to work on a real-life project. From connecting to a database and populating it, to reading and querying it.

topic.name: Data Manipulation
topic.description: Once you've got some data, you'll often want to reshape it, move it around, and merge it with other data. Learn the basics of data manipulation using today' most powerful and popular tools.

proficiency.DS: Covers basic relational database concepts, connecting to databases, and writing simple SQL queries using Python and SQLAlchemy, matching foundational data management skills.
Teaches filtering, ordering, grouping, and advanced queries, as well as creating and updating databases, aligning with intermediate proficiency in data management.
Introduces using Python for database interaction, including basic data manipulation and use of libraries, which fits foundational programming skills.
Covers use of SQLAlchemy for more complex queries and database management, reflecting intermediate programming proficiency.

title: Cleaning Data in PostgreSQL Databases
description: If you surveyed a large number of data scientists and data analysts about which tasks are most common in their workday, cleaning data would likely be in almost all responses. This is the case because real-world data is messy. To help you tame messy data, this course teaches you how to clean data stored in a PostgreSQL database. You'll learn how to solve common problems such as how to clean messy strings, deal with empty values, compare the similarity between strings, and much more. You'll get hands-on practice with these tasks using interesting (but messy) datasets made available by New York City's Open Data program. Are you ready to whip that messy data into shape?

parts.title: Data Cleaning Basics
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll gain an understanding of data cleaning approaches when working with PostgreSQL databases and learn the value of cleaning data as early as possible in the pipeline. You'll also learn basic string editing approaches such as removing unnecessary spaces as well as more involved topics such as pattern matching and string similarity to identify string values in need of cleaning.

parts.title: Missing, Duplicate, and Invalid Data
parts.description: You'll learn how to write queries to solve common problems of missing, duplicate, and invalid data in the context of PostgreSQL database tables. Through hands-on exercises, you'll use the COALESCE() function, SELECT query, and WHERE clause to clean messy data.

parts.title: Converting  Data
parts.description: Sometimes you need to convert data stored in a PostgreSQL database from one data type to another.  In this chapter, you'll explore the expressions you need to convert text to numeric types and how to format strings for temporal data.

parts.title: Transforming Data
parts.description: In the final chapter, you'll learn how to transform your data and construct pivot tables. Working with real-world postal data, you'll discover how to combine and split addresses into city, state, and zip codes using a multitude of powerful functions including CONCAT(), SUBSTRING(), and REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE().

proficiency.DS: The course covers basic data cleaning tasks such as handling missing, duplicate, and invalid data, as well as basic string manipulation and formatting in PostgreSQL, which aligns with foundational proficiency in data processing.

The course includes combining and transforming data, converting data types, and using SQL functions for more complex cleaning and manipulation, which matches intermediate proficiency in data processing.

title: Introduction to Python
description: Python is a general-purpose programming language that is becoming ever more popular for data science. Companies worldwide are using Python to harvest insights from their data and gain a competitive edge. Unlike other Python tutorials, this course focuses on Python specifically for data science. In our Introduction to Python course, you'll learn about powerful ways to store and manipulate data, and helpful data science tools to begin conducting your own analyses. Start DataCamp' online Python curriculum now.

parts.title: Python Basics
parts.description: An introduction to the basic concepts of Python. Learn how to use Python interactively and by using a script. Create your first variables and acquaint yourself with Python's basic data types.

parts.title: Python Lists
parts.description: Learn to store, access, and manipulate data in lists: the first step toward efficiently working with huge amounts of data.

parts.title: Functions and Packages
parts.description: You'll learn how to use functions, methods, and packages to efficiently leverage the code that brilliant Python developers have written. The goal is to reduce the amount of code you need to solve challenging problems!

parts.title: NumPy
parts.description: NumPy is a fundamental Python package to efficiently practice data science. Learn to work with powerful tools in the NumPy array, and get started with data exploration.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist' toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course teaches basic programming concepts in Python, including variables, data types, lists, functions, and packages, which align with foundational proficiency requirements for programming in data science.

title: Machine Learning with Tree-Based Models in R
description: Tree-based machine learning models can reveal complex non-linear relationships in data and often dominate machine learning competitions. In this course, you'll use the tidymodels package to explore and build different tree-based models- from simple decision trees to complex random forests. You'll also learn to use boosted trees, a powerful machine learning technique that uses ensemble learning to build high-performing predictive models. Along the way, you'll work with health and credit risk data to predict the incidence of diabetes and customer churn.

parts.title: Classification Trees
parts.description: Ready to build a real machine learning pipeline? Complete step-by-step exercises to learn how to create decision trees, split your data, and predict which patients are most likely to suffer from diabetes. Last but not least, you'll build performance measures to assess your models and judge your predictions.

parts.title: Regression Trees and Cross-Validation
parts.description: Ready for some candy? Use a chocolate rating dataset to build regression trees and assess their performance using suitable error measures. You'll overcome statistical insecurities of single train/test splits by applying sweet techniques like cross-validation and then dive even deeper by mastering the bias-variance tradeoff.

parts.title: Hyperparameters and Ensemble Models
parts.description: Time to get serious with tuning your hyperparameters and interpreting receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. In this chapter, you'll leverage the wisdom of the crowd with ensemble models like bagging or random forests and build ensembles that forecast which credit card customers are most likely to churn.

parts.title: Boosted Trees
parts.description: Ready for the high society of tree-based models? Apply gradient boosting to create powerful ensembles that perform better than anything that you have seen or built. Learn about their fine-tuning and how to compare different models to pick a winner for production.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced tree-based machine learning techniques, including ensemble methods like random forests and boosted trees, model tuning, and cross-validation, which align with the advanced proficiency requirements for applying complex ML methodologies and building production-ready AI solutions.

The course teaches advanced model evaluation techniques such as cross-validation, bias-variance tradeoff, and performance metrics, matching the advanced proficiency level for rigorous statistical analysis and model assessment.

Learners use the tidymodels package in R to build, tune, and evaluate machine learning models, demonstrating intermediate proficiency in implementing functions, using libraries, and automating data tasks in R.

title: MLOps for Business
description:
Learn the essential concepts and practices of MLOps, an emerging set of tools and techniques for automating and scaling machine learning applications.

Machine learning model development used to be a lengthy manual task, and most models never made it into production. With MLOps, businesses can effectively scale and automate the design, development, and operation of machine learning models.

This course will teach you what MLOps is and how you can use it to become a fully mature machine-learning company. You will learn about the requirements for MLOps, the tools, techniques, and people involved, and how to avoid common pitfalls.

By the end of the course, you'll have a deep understanding of how to design, develop, and operate machine learning applications at scale and will be able to leverage the impact of machine learning on your business.

parts.title: Introducing MLOps
parts.description: The first chapter will introduce MLOps and why it is necessary for businesses that want to design, develop, and operate multiple machine learning applications simultaneously. You will learn about the main elements of MLOps, such as scaling and automation, its benefits, and why MLOps remain challenging. You will also explore what it takes to start the MLOps journey both from a technological and managerial perspective.

parts.title: The MLOps Life Cycle
parts.description: In the second chapter, you'll learn about the entire MLOps life cycle from design to development, deployment, and operations. You'll explore why monitoring is essential for productive machine learning applications and why we must regularly re-train machine learning models.

parts.title: MLOps: From Theory to Practice
parts.description: In the third chapter, you will move from theory to practice and discover the main challenges and risks of deploying machine learning models. You'll also learn how MLOps teams successfully operate and what management can do to foster successful scaling machine learning.

parts.title: MLOps in the wild
parts.description: The final chapter will demonstrate how to successfully jumpstart your business's MLOps journey by discussing best practices and pitfalls to avoid. Finally, you'll examine the different levels of MLOps maturity and conclude the course with a real-life case study about designing, developing, and operating a machine learning application for critical production processes.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: This course covers the full MLOps lifecycle, including design, development, deployment, monitoring, and retraining of machine learning models, which aligns with advanced proficiency in applying complex methodologies and deploying production-ready AI solutions.

The course emphasizes managing the scaling and automation of machine learning projects, coordinating cross-functional teams, and implementing best practices, which matches advanced project management skills in data science.

Learners are taught to leverage MLOps for business impact, align machine learning initiatives with organizational goals, and avoid common pitfalls, reflecting advanced business acumen in translating data insights into actionable strategies.

title: Dimensionality Reduction in R
description: Do you ever work with datasets with an overwhelming number of features? In this course, you will learn dimensionality reduction techniques that will help you simplify your data and the models that you build with your data while maintaining good predictive performance. Dimensionality reduction is your Occam' razor in data science. Using R, you will learn how to identify and remove features, how to extract combinations of features as condensed components that contain maximal information, and use real-world data to build models with fewer features without sacrificing significant performance.

parts.title: Foundations of Dimensionality Reduction
parts.description: Prepare to simplify large data sets! You will learn about information, how to assess feature importance, and practice identifying low-information features. By the end of the chapter, you will understand the difference between feature selection and feature extraction- the two approaches to dimensionality reduction.

parts.title: Feature Selection for Feature Importance
parts.description: Learn how to identify information-rich and information-poor features missing value ratios, variance, and correlation. Then you'll discover how to build tidymodel recipes to select features using these information indicators.

parts.title: Feature Selection for Model Performance
parts.description: Chapter three introduces the difference between unsupervised and supervised feature selection approaches. You'll review how to use tidymodels workflows to build models. Then, you'll perform supervised feature selection using lasso regression and random forest models.

parts.title: Feature Extraction and Model Performance
parts.description: In this final chapter, you'll gain a strong intuition of feature extraction by understanding how principal components extract and combine the most important information from different features. Then learn about and apply three types of feature extraction -  principal component analysis (PCA), t-SNE, and UMAP. Discover how you can use these feature extraction methods as a preprocessing step in the tidymodels model-building process.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: Covers multivariate statistical techniques such as principal component analysis (PCA), feature selection, and correlation, which are expected at the intermediate level for handling multiple variables and uncovering patterns in data.

Teaches supervised and unsupervised feature selection, lasso regression, random forest, and model-building workflows, aligning with intermediate proficiency in applying machine learning techniques to real-world problems.
Uses R and tidymodels to automate feature selection and extraction, requiring knowledge of libraries and scripting for data manipulation and modeling, which matches intermediate programming skills.

title: Supervised Learning in R: Classification
description: This beginner-level introduction to machine learning covers four of the most common classification algorithms. You will come away with a basic understanding of how each algorithm approaches a learning task, as well as learn the R functions needed to apply these tools to your own work.

parts.title: k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN)
parts.description: As the kNN algorithm literally "learns by example" it is a case in point for starting to understand supervised machine learning. This chapter will introduce classification while working through the application of kNN to self-driving vehicle road sign recognition.

parts.title: Naive Bayes
parts.description: Naive Bayes uses principles from the field of statistics to make predictions. This chapter will introduce the basics of Bayesian methods while exploring how to apply these techniques to iPhone-like destination suggestions.

parts.title: Logistic Regression
parts.description: Logistic regression involves fitting a curve to numeric data to make predictions about binary events. Arguably one of the most widely used machine learning methods, this chapter will provide an overview of the technique while illustrating how to apply it to fundraising data.

parts.title: Classification Trees
parts.description: Classification trees use flowchart-like structures to make decisions. Because humans can readily understand these tree structures, classification trees are useful when transparency is needed, such as in loan approval. We'll use the Lending Club dataset to simulate this scenario.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: Covers basic supervised classification algorithms (kNN, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Classification Trees) and their application in R, matching foundational proficiency in understanding and applying core machine learning concepts.
Introduces use of R functions for applying machine learning algorithms, aligning with foundational programming skills for basic data manipulation and analysis.
Explains statistical concepts underlying algorithms like Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression, suitable for foundational understanding of basic probability and statistics in data science.

title: Visualizing Time Series Data in Python
description: Time series data is omnipresent in the field of Data Science. Whether it is analyzing business trends, forecasting company revenue or exploring customer behavior, every data scientist is likely to encounter time series data at some point during their work. To get you started on working with time series data, this course will provide practical knowledge on visualizing time series data using Python.

parts.title: Line Plots
parts.description: You will learn how to leverage basic plottings tools in Python, and how to annotate and personalize your time series plots. By the end of this chapter, you will be able to take any static dataset and produce compelling plots of your data.

parts.title: Summary Statistics and Diagnostics
parts.description: In this chapter, you will gain a deeper understanding of your time series data by computing summary statistics and plotting aggregated views of your data.

parts.title: Seasonality, Trend and Noise
parts.description: You will go beyond summary statistics by learning about autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation plots. You will also learn how to automatically detect seasonality, trend and noise in your time series data.

parts.title: Work with Multiple Time Series
parts.description: In the field of Data Science, it is common to be involved in projects where multiple time series need to be studied simultaneously. In this chapter, we will show you how to plot multiple time series at once, and how to discover and describe relationships between multiple time series.

parts.title: Case Study: Unemployment Rate
parts.description: This chapter will give you a chance to practice all the concepts covered in the course. You will visualize the unemployment rate in the US from 2000 to 2010.

topic.name: Data Visualization
topic.description: Creating visual representations of your data is one of the quickest and most effective ways to understand it, discover surprising results, and communicate those results to others. Learn the basics of data visualization using state-of-the-art tools.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces basic plotting tools in Python, enabling learners to create and personalize simple time series visualizations, which aligns with foundational proficiency in presenting data clearly.

Learners compute summary statistics, plot aggregated views, and visualize relationships between multiple time series, matching intermediate proficiency in creating complex visualizations and highlighting key insights.

The course covers summary statistics, autocorrelation, and partial autocorrelation plots, supporting intermediate proficiency in applying statistical analysis and uncovering patterns in time series data.

title: Intermediate R
description: Intermediate R is the next stop on your journey in mastering the R programming language. In this R training, you will learn about conditional statements, loops, and functions to power your own R scripts. Next, make your R code more efficient and readable using the apply functions. Finally, the utilities chapter gets you up to speed with regular expressions in R, data structure manipulations, and times and dates. This course will allow you to take the next step in advancing your overall knowledge and capabilities while programming in R.

parts.title: Conditionals and Control Flow
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn about relational operators for comparing R objects, and logical operators like "and" and "or" for combining TRUE and FALSE values.  Then, you'll use this knowledge to build conditional statements.

parts.title: Loops
parts.description: Loops can come in handy on numerous occasions. While loops are like repeated if statements, the for loop is designed to iterate over all elements in a sequence. Learn about them in this chapter.

parts.title: Functions
parts.description: Functions are an extremely important concept in almost every programming language, and R is no different. Learn what functions are and how to use them- then take charge by writing your own functions.

parts.title: The apply family
parts.description: Whenever you're using a for loop, you may want to revise your code to see whether you can use the lapply function instead. Learn all about this intuitive way of applying a function over a list or a vector, and how to use its variants, sapply and vapply.

parts.title: Utilities
parts.description: Mastering R programming is not only about understanding its programming concepts. Having a solid understanding of a wide range of R functions is also important. This chapter introduces you to many useful functions for data structure manipulation, regular expressions, and working with times and dates.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist' toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course covers intermediate programming concepts in R such as conditional statements, loops, functions, and the apply family, aligning with the intermediate proficiency level which requires designing and implementing functions and classes, and using libraries for data manipulation.

title: Fully Automated MLOps
description: Learn to deploy and maintain ML models with full automation in MLOps. Understand the impact of hidden technical debt and how streamlining the ML lifecycle boosts operations and scalability. Engage in hands-on exercises to explore MLOps architecture components essential for automating ML systems. Master CI/CD, Continuous Monitoring (CM), and Continuous Training (CT) to avoid technical debt in ML deployments. By the end of the course, grasp how MLOps automation enhances deployment robustness and scalability. Start learning to excel in this in-demand field.

parts.title: Introduction: to Fully Automated MLOps
parts.description: In this first chapter, we motivate the use of MLOps in an industrial setting. You'll learn about its importance in supporting the generation of value in businesses. You'll also recap the ML stages, focusing on how MLOps enhances these. At the end of the chapter, you'll explore a reference architecture for a fully automated MLOps system. You will then use this architecture to explore components important for any MLOps system and a starting point for the rest of the course.

parts.title: Fully Automated MLOps Architecture
parts.description: In this chapter, you will continue your exploration of the critical components that make up a fully automated MLOps system. First, you'll examine the importance of orchestration in MLOps and how it helps to ensure the efficiency and scalability of ML pipelines. After this, you'll examine the different deployment strategies in MLOps and learn how to choose the right strategy for your system. Finally, you'll learn about CI/CD/CT/CM and how it complements orchestration and best practices to achieve full automation in MLOps systems. With these lessons under your belt, you will be better equipped to build a fully automated MLOps system that is efficient, accurate, and reliable.

parts.title: Automation Patterns
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll dive into the exciting world of automation and learn how to design more resilient and efficient ML systems. You'll start by understanding the fundamentals of automation in MLOps systems and then move on to discover the power of design patterns and fail-safe mechanisms. You'll also learn how to implement automated testing in MLOps systems and how to use hyperparameter tuning to optimize your models and workflows. By the end of this chapter, you'll be equipped with the skills and knowledge necessary to build and manage fully automated MLOps systems that are both efficient and reliable.

parts.title: Automation in MLOps Deployments
parts.description: In this final chapter, you'll delve into the crucial components of an automated MLOps architecture. From understanding automated experiment tracking and the model registry to exploring the feature store and the role of the metadata store, this chapter is designed to equip you with a comprehensive understanding of the intricacies of a fully automated MLOps system. Whether you're a seasoned ML practitioner or just starting out, this chapter will provide you with the knowledge and skills necessary to design automated MLOps workflows.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: This course covers advanced MLOps concepts such as CI/CD, continuous monitoring, and automation patterns, aligning with the advanced proficiency level's focus on deploying and maintaining robust, scalable ML systems.
The course teaches how to plan, build, and optimize automated ML pipelines, which matches the advanced level's requirement for managing complex, cross-functional data science projects and workflows.
Hands-on exercises in automating ML deployments and implementing orchestration, CI/CD, and testing reflect advanced programming skills in building scalable, maintainable systems.
Topics such as experiment tracking, model registry, and feature store demonstrate advanced data management practices required for large-scale, automated ML operations.

title: Fraud Detection in R
description: The Association of Certified Fraud Examiners estimates that fraud costs organizations worldwide $3.7 trillion a year and that a typical company loses five percent of annual revenue due to fraud. Fraud attempts are expected to even increase further in future, making fraud detection highly necessary in most industries. This course will show how learning fraud patterns from historical data can be used to fight fraud. Some techniques from robust statistics and digit analysis are presented to detect unusual observations that are likely associated with fraud. Two main challenges when building a supervised tool for fraud detection are the imbalance or skewness of the data and the various costs for different types of misclassification. We present techniques to solve these issues and focus on artificial and real datasets from a wide variety of fraud applications.

parts.title: Introduction & Motivation
parts.description: This chapter will first give a formal definition of fraud. You will then learn how to detect anomalies in the type of payment methods used or the time these payments are made to flag suspicious transactions.

parts.title: Social network analytics
parts.description: In the second chapter, you will learn how to use networks to fight fraud. You will visualize networks and use a sociology concept called homophily to detect fraudulent transactions and catch fraudsters.

parts.title: Imbalanced class distributions
parts.description: Fortunately, fraud occurrences are rare. However, this means that you're working with imbalanced data, which if left as is will bias your detection models. In this chapter, you will tackle imbalance using over and under-sampling methods.

parts.title: Digit analysis and robust statistics
parts.description: In this final chapter, you will learn about a surprising mathematical law used to detect suspicious occurrences. You will then use robust statistics to make your models even more bulletproof.

topic.name: Machine Learning
topic.description: Machine learning is one of the most exciting and dynamic fields in the world of data science. Everything from self-driving cars, to smartphones and search engines are built on this powerful set of tools for generating useful predictions from data.

proficiency.DS: The course covers supervised machine learning for fraud detection, handling imbalanced data, and model evaluation, which aligns with intermediate proficiency in applying AI techniques to real-world business problems.
It introduces robust statistics and digit analysis, applying advanced statistical techniques to solve complex problems such as fraud detection and model evaluation.
The course uses R for implementing fraud detection models and data manipulation, matching intermediate-level programming skills in data science.

title: Introduction to MongoDB in Python
description: MongoDB is a tool to explore data structured as you see fit. As a NoSQL database, it doesn't follow the strict relational format imposed by SQL. By providing capabilities that typically require adding layers to SQL, it collapses complexity. With dynamic schema, you can handle vastly different data together and consolidate analytics. The flexibility of MongoDB empowers you to keep improving and fix issues as your requirements evolve. In this course, you will learn the MongoDB language and apply it to search and analytics. Working with unprocessed data from the official nobelprize.org API, you will explore and answer questions about Nobel Laureates and prizes.

parts.title: Flexibly Structured Data
parts.description: This chapter is about getting a bird's-eye view of the Nobel Prize data's structure. You will relate MongoDB documents, collections, and databases to JSON and Python types. You'll then use filters, operators, and dot notation to explore substructure.

parts.title: Working with Distinct Values and Sets
parts.description: Now you have a sense of the data's structure. This chapter is about dipping your toes into the pools of values for various fields. You'll collect distinct values, test for membership in sets, and match values to patterns.

parts.title: Get Only What You Need, and Fast
parts.description: You can now query collections with ease and collect documents to examine and analyze with Python. But this process is sometimes slow and onerous for large collections and documents. This chapter is about various ways to speed up and simplify that process.

parts.title: Aggregation Pipelines: Let the Server Do It For You
parts.description: You've used projection, sorting, indexing, and limits to speed up data fetching. But there are still annoying performance bottlenecks in your analysis pipelines. You still need to fetch a ton of data. Thus, network bandwidth and downstream processing and memory capacity still impact performance. This chapter is about using MongoDB to perform aggregations for you on the server.

proficiency.DS: The course introduces basic concepts of NoSQL databases, MongoDB documents, collections, and querying, which aligns with foundational data management skills such as loading, exploring, and filtering data.

The course covers aggregation pipelines, indexing, and performance optimization, which are relevant to intermediate proficiency in data management, including combining datasets, automating cleaning tasks, and optimizing data processing.
Learners use Python to interact with MongoDB, manipulate data structures, and apply basic programming concepts, matching foundational programming skills.

title: Optimizing R Code with Rcpp
description:
R is a great language for data science, but sometimes the code can be slow to run. Combining the comfort of R with the speed of a compiled language
is a great way to reclaim the performance your code deserves.

C++ is a modern, high performance language that is simple enough to learn
in the context of accelerating R code. With the help of the Rcpp package,
C++ integrates very neatly with R. You will learn how to create and manipulate
typical R objects (vectors and lists), and write your own C++ functions
to dramatically boost the performance of your R code.

parts.title: Introduction
parts.description: Writing, benchmarking, and debugging your first C++ code.

parts.title: Functions and Control Flow
parts.description: Writing functions, controlling the flow with if and else, and learning to use the three kinds of loops in C++.

parts.title: Vector classes
parts.description: Manipulate and compute with Rcpp and native C++ vectors.

parts.title: Case Studies
parts.description: Use random numbers and write algorithms for applied time series models.

topic.name: Programming
topic.description: Programming is an essential tool in every data scientist' toolbox. Learn the basics of data types, loops, control flow, functions, and more and you'll be well on your way to data science mastery!

proficiency.DS: This course teaches optimization of R code using C++ via Rcpp, covering advanced topics such as integrating compiled code, manipulating vectors, and boosting performance, which aligns with advanced proficiency in programming for data science.

title: Inference for Numerical Data in R
description: In this course, you'll learn how to use statistical techniques to make inferences and estimations using numerical data. This course uses two approaches to these common tasks. The first makes use of bootstrapping and permutation to create resample based tests and confidence intervals. The second uses theoretical results and the t-distribution to achieve the same result. You'll learn how (and when) to perform a t-test, create a confidence interval, and do an ANOVA!

parts.title: Bootstrapping for estimating a parameter
parts.description: In this chapter you'll use bootstrapping techniques to estimate a single parameter from a numerical distribution.

parts.title: Introducing the t-distribution
parts.description: In this chapter you'll use Central Limit Theorem based techniques to estimate a single parameter from a numerical distribution. You will do this using the t-distribution.

parts.title: Inference for difference in two parameters
parts.description: In this chapter you'll extend what you have learned so far to use both simulation and CLT based techniques for inference on the difference between two parameters from two independent numerical distributions.

parts.title: Comparing many means
parts.description: In this chapter you will use ANOVA (analysis of variance) to test for a difference in means across many groups.

topic.name: Probability & Statistics
topic.description: Much of data science comes from the world of probability and statistics, which together provide a set of tools for understanding how data is generated, how to model it effectively, and how to make inferences and predictions based on those models.

proficiency.DS: Covers inferential statistics including t-tests, confidence intervals, and ANOVA, matching the intermediate proficiency requirements for applying hypothesis testing and interpreting regression and multivariate techniques.

title: Building Dashboards with shinydashboard
description: Learn to create an interactive dashboard using the shinydashboard package in R. This course teaches you how to use shinydashboard in R to create a dynamic and interactive dashboard. You will cover the ins and outs of shinydashboard and learn about good UI/UX practices. You will first build a shinyApp and then graduate to building a shinydashboard. Then, you learn how to include interactive elements with hover-over effects. Finally, you will explore how to tweak your design elements of a shinydashboard using CSS code and more.

parts.title: ShinyApps
parts.description: Before you build a shinydashboard, you will first need to understand what a shinyApp is. In this chapter, you will learn what a shinyApp is, and learn what goes into a shinyApp. At the end of this chapter, you will be able to render your own shinyApp.

parts.title: Basics of a shinydashboard
parts.description: In the previous chapter, you learned about shiny apps. In this chapter, you will realize that a shinydashboard is really just another shiny app but with more tweakable features. The same outputs and inputs discussed in the previous chapter can be used in exactly the same manner here. You will then learn to carry out some simple wire-framing for a dashboard, during which you can decide where to position outputs and inputs in the dashboard.

parts.title: Interactive plots and geospatial maps
parts.description: In this chapter, you will learn to further enhance your shinydashboard by inserting interactive elements. These will include graphs, geospatial maps, and tables that dashboard users can interact with in real-time.

parts.title: Adding design elements and improving UI/UX
parts.description: Now that you are familiar with shinydashboard, we can now add design elements. We will be able to change background colors, modify box dimensions and so on. We will also discuss some basic principles of good UI/UX. Finally, we will show how statuses and CSS formatting can be utilized.

topic.name: Reporting
topic.description: Most analyses are useless until they are communicated effectively to the right audience. Knowing how to report your findings in an interesting and interpretable way empowers others with greater understanding and the ability to make important data-driven decisions.

proficiency.DS: This course teaches the creation of interactive dashboards and visualizations using shinydashboard in R, including real-time graphs and geospatial maps, which aligns with the intermediate level's focus on complex visualizations and interactive elements.

The course emphasizes reporting findings through dashboards and good UI/UX practices, matching the intermediate proficiency in organizing data insights, adapting communication for stakeholders, and linking visuals to business objectives.

Learners build shinyApps and dashboards in R, manipulate UI elements, and use CSS, which fits the intermediate level's requirements for implementing functions, using libraries, and enhancing data-driven applications.

title: Introduction to Google Sheets
description:
Google Sheets is one of the most popular and powerful data analytics tools. Millions of people use software such as Google Sheets to acquire meaningful insights from data.

In this course, you'll learn the fundamentals of spreadsheets by working with tabular data and performing calculations. You'll also create your own formulas and learn how to use references to connect cells and bring your spreadsheets to life.

parts.title: Cells and Formulas
parts.description: You'll begin by learning how to use spreadsheets to extract insights from your data. In this chapter, you'll learn how to write formulas, perform calculations in spreadsheets, use comparison operators, and format cells.

parts.title: Cell References
parts.description: In this chapter, you'll learn about one of the most powerful concepts in spreadsheets: cell references. Using geographical and demographical data from the ten most populous countries, you'll utilize cell references to make your spreadsheets reactive to changes and learn useful shortcuts to start applying calculations at scale.

proficiency.DS: This course teaches basic spreadsheet skills such as writing formulas, performing calculations, and using cell references, which align with foundational data processing tasks like cleaning, transforming, and preparing data for analysis.
Learners develop fundamental skills in summarizing and calculating data using spreadsheets, supporting foundational statistical concepts such as measures of central tendency and basic data analysis.

title: Data Storytelling Concepts
description:
People value the information data may hold and also appreciate the value of stories. Data storytelling is the art of building a narrative around the insights provided by data. It combines the intellectual and emotional in a meaningful and memorable way that leads to action, whether for individuals or within organizations.
